subject: Arithmetic
q: When the number (67⁶⁷ + 67) is divided by 68, what is the remainder?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 66 • (A) 1: Common trap if candidate calculates 67 mod 68 as +1 instead of -1.
• (B) 66: Correct! (-1)⁶⁷ + (-1) = -1 - 1 = -2 ≡ 68 - 2 = 66 (mod 68).
• (C) 67: Trap if candidate only looks at the second term 67 and ignores the power.
• (D) 0: Occurs only if the number were completely divisible.
tip: 💡 10-Second Negative Remainder Trick: Whenever base N is 1 less than divisor (D = N + 1), write base as -1. Here, (68 - 1)⁶⁷ + 67 ≡ (-1)⁶⁷ + (-1) = -2. Add divisor: 68 - 2 = 66! Zero long division needed.

subject: Arithmetic
q: The least number which when divided by 12, 16, 24, and 36 leaves a remainder of 7 in each case, but is completely divisible by 13 is:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 871 • (A) 144: This is merely the LCM of 12, 16, 24, 36. 144 mod 13 = 1 (not divisible by 13).
• (B) 151: 144 + 7 = 151. While 151 leaves remainder 7 with 12, 16, 24, 36, 151 mod 13 = 8 (not divisible).
• (C) 871: Correct! General form is 144k + 7. For k = 6, 144(6) + 7 = 871. 871 / 13 = 67 exactly!
• (D) 1014: 1014 is divisible by 13 (13 × 78 = 1014), but 1014 leaves remainder 6 with 12 (not 7).
tip: 💡 Option Elimination Hack: In the exam, don't test 12, 16, 24, 36! Directly test divisibility by 13 on the options first. Only 871 and 1014 are divisible by 13. Then 871 - 7 = 864, which is 144 × 6. Instant 15-second answer!

subject: Arithmetic
q: What is the unit digit in the product (7⁹⁵ − 3⁵⁸)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 4 • (A) 0: Trap if candidate subtracts 3 - 3 without calculating cyclicity.
• (B) 4: Correct! Powers of 7 and 3 have cyclicity of 4. 7⁹⁵: 95 mod 4 = 3 -> 7³ ends in 3. 3⁵⁸: 58 mod 4 = 2 -> 3² ends in 9. Borrow 1: 13 - 9 = 4.
• (C) 6: Common mistake if candidate does 9 - 3 instead of borrowing (13 - 9).
• (D) 7: Ends with 7 if only 7⁹⁵ were evaluated.
tip: 💡 Golden Cyclicity Rule: Divide power by 4. If remainder is r, take base^r. If r = 0, take base^4. Whenever (unit1 < unit2) in subtraction, simply prefix 1 (e.g. 3 becomes 13). 13 - 9 = 4!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Three bells begin to toll together and toll at intervals of 9, 12, and 15 seconds respectively. How many times will they toll together in the next 1 hour (excluding the one at the start)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 20 times • (A) 15 times: Trap if candidate calculates LCM as 240 seconds.
• (B) 20 times: Correct! LCM of 9, 12, 15 = 180 seconds = 3 minutes. In 1 hour (60 minutes), they toll together 60 / 3 = 20 times.
• (C) 25 times: Calculation error.
• (D) 30 times: Occurs if LCM is mistakenly assumed to be 2 minutes.
tip: 💡 Conversion Tip: Convert LCM to minutes immediately! LCM(9, 12, 15) = 180 sec = 3 min. Total occurrences = 60 / 3 = 20 times (excluding the start).

subject: Arithmetic
q: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 2 : 1. What quantity of water must be added to this mixture to make the ratio of milk to water 1 : 2?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 60 litres • (A) 20 litres: Amount of water in original mixture (40L milk, 20L water).
• (B) 40 litres: Amount of milk in the mixture.
• (C) 60 litres: Correct! Original Milk = 40L, Water = 20L. New ratio M:W = 1:2. Since Milk remains 40L, 1 unit = 40L, so 2 units of Water = 80L. Added water = 80 - 20 = 60 litres.
• (D) 80 litres: Total final volume of water, not the added quantity.
tip: 💡 Constant Quantity Shortcut: The quantity of MILK never changes! In new ratio (1:2), 1 part = 40L, so 2 parts = 80L water. Added water = 80 - 20 = 60L! Solved in 5 seconds.

subject: Arithmetic
q: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price, but he uses a false weight of 920 grams for a kilogram. Find his gain percentage.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 8 16/23% • (A) 8 16/23%: Correct! Gain % = [Error / (True Value - Error)] × 100 = (80 / 920) × 100% = 800/92% = 200/23% = 8 16/23%.
• (B) 8%: Trap if candidate mistakenly calculates profit on the nominal 1000g (80/1000 = 8%).
• (C) 9 1/11%: Value for 1/11 fraction.
• (D) 8 ½%: Common rounding error trap.
tip: 💡 Faulty Balance Rule: Always calculate gain percentage over the ACTUAL GOODS DISPENSED to the buyer: Gain % = [Error / Goods actually sold] × 100 = (80 / 920) × 100 = 8 16/23%!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% for cash payment. What is his net profit percentage?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 10.5% • (A) 10.5%: Correct! Net % = x - y - (xy/100) = 30 - 15 - (30 × 15)/100 = 15 - 4.5 = 10.5%.
• (B) 12%: Computational error.
• (C) 15%: Trap if candidate simply does 30 - 15 without applying discount on markup.
• (D) 11.5%: Arithmetic slip.
tip: 💡 Net Effect Formula: Profit % = M - D - (M × D)/100 = 30 - 15 - 4.5 = 10.5%. Or assume CP = 100 -> MP = 130 -> SP = 130 × 0.85 = 110.5 -> 10.5% profit!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A sum of money amounts to Rs. 9,680 in 2 years and to Rs. 10,648 in 3 years at compound interest, compounded annually. What is the rate of interest per annum?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10% • (A) 8%: Incorrect rate.
• (B) 10%: Correct! Interest for 3rd year = Rs. 10,648 - Rs. 9,680 = Rs. 968. Rate = (968 / 9,680) × 100 = 10%.
• (C) 12%: Incorrect rate.
• (D) 15%: Incorrect rate.
tip: 💡 Consecutive Years CI Hack: In compound interest, the difference between Amount in Year (n+1) and Year (n) is strictly 1 year's simple interest on Year (n)'s Amount! 968 / 9680 = 1/10 = 10%!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money at 10% per annum for 3 years is Rs. 930. What is the principal sum?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Rs. 30,000 • (A) Rs. 25,000: Result if 2-year difference formula were used.
• (B) Rs. 30,000: Correct! For 3 years at 10%: SI = 30%, CI = 33.1%. Difference = 3.1%. Principal = 930 / 0.031 = Rs. 30,000.
• (C) Rs. 35,000: Incorrect.
• (D) Rs. 40,000: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Standard 10% Benchmark: At 10% for 3 years, CI is always 33.1% and SI is 30.0%. Difference is always 3.1%! Principal = 930 / 3.1 × 100 = Rs. 30,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A person invested Rs. X at 15% simple interest per annum and Rs. Y at 10% simple interest per annum for 1 year, receiving total interest of Rs. 3,500. Had he interchanged the amounts invested, he would have received Rs. 3,000. Find the value of (X − Y).
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Rs. 10,000 • (A) Rs. 10,000: Correct! 0.15X + 0.10Y = 3500 and 0.10X + 0.15Y = 3000. Subtracting gives 0.05(X - Y) = 500 -> X - Y = 500 / 0.05 = Rs. 10,000.
• (B) Rs. 8,000: Trap from algebraic slip.
• (C) Rs. 12,000: Incorrect.
• (D) Rs. 15,000: Value of X + Y / 4.
tip: 💡 Symmetric Equation Shortcut: Whenever coefficients are swapped (aX + bY and bX + aY), NEVER solve for X and Y! Subtract the equations directly: (a - b)(X - Y) = Difference -> 0.05(X - Y) = 500 -> X - Y = 10,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The salaries of A, B, and C are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. If their salaries are increased by 15%, 10%, and 20% respectively, what will be the new ratio of their salaries?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 23 : 33 : 60 • (A) 23 : 33 : 60: Correct! Assume salaries are 20, 30, 50. New salaries: 20 × 1.15 = 23; 30 × 1.10 = 33; 50 × 1.20 = 60.
• (B) 21 : 33 : 60: Trap if 2 was increased by only 5%.
• (C) 23 : 30 : 50: Forgets to increase B and C.
• (D) 20 : 31 : 58: Arithmetic error.
tip: 💡 Scaling Technique: Scale base ratio 2 : 3 : 5 up by multiplying by 10 or 100: 20 -> 23 (+15%), 30 -> 33 (+10%), 50 -> 60 (+20%). Result: 23 : 33 : 60!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A, B, and C enter into a partnership. A invests Rs. 40,000 for 8 months, B invests Rs. 60,000 for 6 months, and C invests Rs. 50,000 for 12 months. Out of a total profit of Rs. 64,000, what is C's share?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Rs. 30,000 • (A) Rs. 20,000: Share of Partner A.
• (B) Rs. 24,000: Share of Partner B.
• (C) Rs. 30,000: Correct! Profit ratio = (40×8) : (60×6) : (50×12) = 320 : 360 : 600 = 8 : 9 : 15. Total = 32 units. 1 unit = 64,000 / 32 = 2,000. C's share = 15 × 2,000 = Rs. 30,000.
• (D) Rs. 32,000: Value if C worked for only 10 months.
tip: 💡 Capital × Time Rule: Profit ratio = Investment × Duration. Cancel four zeros right away: A = 4×8 = 32, B = 6×6 = 36, C = 5×12 = 60. Divide by 4: 8:9:15!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A can complete a work in 12 days, and B can complete the same work in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which B leaves and C joins. A and C finish the remaining work in 4 days. In how many days can C alone complete the entire work?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 36 days • (A) 24 days: Trap if work done by A is miscalculated.
• (B) 36 days: Correct! Work = 36 units. Rate of A = 3, B = 2. In 4 days, A+B do 4×5 = 20 units. Remaining = 16 units. A+C do 16 units in 4 days -> Rate of A+C = 4. Since A = 3, C = 1 unit/day. Time for C alone = 36 / 1 = 36 days.
• (C) 18 days: Rate of B.
• (D) 30 days: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Unit Work Method: Take LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units. Calculate daily efficiencies as integers (3 and 2) to eliminate fractions completely!

subject: Arithmetic
q: 12 men and 16 boys can do a piece of work in 5 days, while 13 men and 24 boys can do it in 4 days. How long will 7 men and 10 boys take to complete the same work?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 8 ⅓ days • (A) 8 ⅓ days: Correct! 5(12m + 16b) = 4(13m + 24b) -> 60m + 80b = 52m + 96b -> 8m = 16b -> 1m = 2b. Total work = (24 + 16) × 5 = 200 boy-days. 7m + 10b = 14 + 10 = 24 boys. Time = 200 / 24 = 25/3 = 8 ⅓ days.
• (B) 7 days: Calculation error.
• (C) 8 days: Rounding trap.
• (D) 9 days: Calculation error.
tip: 💡 Convert to One Gender: Always equate M1 × D1 = M2 × D2 to find 1 man = 2 boys. Then convert everyone into boys: 200 / 24 = 25/3 = 8 ⅓ days!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the cistern?
opts: The cistern will never be filled
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 60 minutes • (A) 40 minutes: Incorrect.
• (B) 50 minutes: Incorrect.
• (C) 60 minutes: Correct! Capacity = LCM(20, 30, 15) = 60 units. Pipe A = +3, Pipe B = +2, Pipe C = -4. Net rate = +3 + 2 - 4 = +1 unit/min. Time = 60 / 1 = 60 minutes.
• (D) Cistern never filled: Trap if negative rate were larger than positive rate.
tip: 💡 Flow Balance Trick: Net filling rate = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15 = (3 + 2 - 4)/60 = 1/60. Since net rate is positive, it fills in exactly 60 minutes!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A leak in the bottom of a tank can empty the full tank in 8 hours. An inlet pipe fills water at the rate of 6 litres per minute. When the tank is full, the inlet is opened and the leak empties the tank in 12 hours. What is the capacity of the tank?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 8,640 litres • (A) 7,200 litres: Occurs if inlet rate is multiplied by 20 hours.
• (B) 8,640 litres: Correct! Inlet alone takes (8 × 12) / (12 - 8) = 96 / 4 = 24 hours. Rate = 6 L/min = 360 L/hr. Capacity = 24 × 360 = 8,640 litres.
• (C) 5,760 litres: Capacity if inlet alone were 16 hours.
• (D) 9,400 litres: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Net Inlet Time Formula: Time for inlet alone = (T1 × T2) / (T2 - T1) = (8 × 12) / 4 = 24 hours. Capacity = 24 × 60 min × 6 L/min = 8,640 L!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A train traveling at 72 km/h crosses a platform of length 250 metres in 26 seconds. How long will it take for the same train to cross a man running at 7.2 km/h in the same direction?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 15 seconds • (A) 12 seconds: If relative speed was not subtracted.
• (B) 14 seconds: Calculation error.
• (C) 15 seconds: Correct! Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Train length = (20 × 26) - 250 = 520 - 250 = 270 m. Man speed = 7.2 km/h = 2 m/s. Relative speed = 20 - 2 = 18 m/s. Time = 270 / 18 = 15 seconds.
• (D) 18 seconds: Opposite direction trap.
tip: 💡 Two-Step Train Rule: 1. Train length = Total distance - Platform = (20×26) - 250 = 270m. 2. Same direction: subtract speeds (20 - 2 = 18 m/s). Time = 270 / 18 = 15 s!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Two trains 140 m and 160 m long are running towards each other on parallel lines at speeds of 60 km/h and 48 km/h respectively. In how many seconds will they clear each other from the moment they meet?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 seconds • (A) 9 seconds: Incorrect.
• (B) 10 seconds: Correct! Total distance = 140 + 160 = 300 m. Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s. Time = 300 / 30 = 10 seconds.
• (C) 12 seconds: Trap if relative speed was taken as 25 m/s.
• (D) 15 seconds: Trap if distance was 450 m.
tip: 💡 Speed of 108 km/h Benchmark: Remember that 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Therefore 108 km/h = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s! Distance = 300 m. Time = 300 / 30 = 10 seconds flat!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A man can row 9 km/h in still water. He finds that it takes him twice as long to row upstream as to row downstream for the same distance. What is the speed of the stream?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 3 km/h • (A) 2 km/h: Incorrect.
• (B) 3 km/h: Correct! Still speed u = 9 km/h. Stream speed v. Downstream = 9 + v, Upstream = 9 - v. (9 + v) = 2(9 - v) -> 3v = 9 -> v = 3 km/h.
• (C) 4.5 km/h: Trap if u/2 was selected.
• (D) 1.5 km/h: Trap if 3/2 was calculated.
tip: 💡 Upstream/Downstream Ratio Shortcut: Speed of stream v = u × (n - 1)/(n + 1). Here n = 2, so v = 9 × (2 - 1)/(2 + 1) = 9 × 1/3 = 3 km/h!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The average weight of 24 students in a class is 35 kg. If the weight of the teacher is included, the average increases by 400 grams. What is the weight of the teacher?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 45 kg • (A) 45 kg: Correct! Old average = 35 kg. New count = 25. Teacher weight = 35 + (25 × 0.4 kg) = 35 + 10 = 45 kg.
• (B) 42 kg: Trap if increase was distributed over only 24 students (35 + 9.6).
• (C) 48 kg: Calculation slip.
• (D) 40 kg: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Surplus Distribution Method: New Member Weight = Old Average + (Total New Members × Increase) = 35 + 25(0.4) = 35 + 10 = 45 kg! Solved without multiplying 24 × 35.

subject: Arithmetic
q: The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first six numbers is 49 and that of the last six numbers is 52. What is the value of the sixth number?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 56 • (A) 52: Average of last six numbers.
• (B) 54: Intermediate value.
• (C) 56: Correct! Sum of 11 = 550. Sum of first 6 = 294, last 6 = 312. Sum of both = 606. Middle 6th number = 606 - 550 = 56.
• (D) 58: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Net Deviation Shortcut: First 6 deviate by 6 × (-1) = -6. Last 6 deviate by 6 × (+2) = +12. Net deviation = +6. Middle number = Base average + Net deviation = 50 + 6 = 56!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A jar contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 litres of the mixture is drawn off and 10 litres of liquid B is poured in the jar, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. How many litres of liquid A was originally contained in the jar?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 16 litres • (A) 16 litres: Correct! Let total mixture = 5x. A = 4x, B = x. Removing 10L removes 8L of A and 2L of B. Adding 10L B gives (4x - 8)/(x + 8) = 2/3 -> 12x - 24 = 2x + 16 -> 10x = 40 -> x = 4. Initial A = 4x = 16 litres.
• (B) 20 litres: Total volume of original mixture (16 + 4 = 20L).
• (C) 24 litres: Incorrect.
• (D) 32 litres: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Back-Solve from Options: If A was 16L, total is 20L (16L A, 4L B). 10L drawn takes away half of A (8L left) and half of B (2L left). Adding 10L B makes B = 12L. Ratio 8:12 = 2:3! Confirmed in 10 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: In what ratio must a grocer mix tea at Rs. 180 per kg and Rs. 240 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 253 per kg he gains a profit of 15%?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1 : 2 • (A) 1 : 2: Correct! SP = Rs. 253 with 15% profit -> CP = 253 / 1.15 = Rs. 220. Alligation between 180 and 240 with mean 220: (240 - 220) : (220 - 180) = 20 : 40 = 1 : 2.
• (B) 2 : 1: Common trap reversing the ratio order.
• (C) 3 : 2: Incorrect.
• (D) 3 : 4: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Always Convert SP to CP First: Never alligate Selling Price directly with Cost Prices! Mean CP = 253 / 1.15 = 220. Cross difference: (240-220)=20 vs (220-180)=40 -> Ratio = 1:2!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The present ages of three persons are in proportions 4 : 7 : 9. Eight years ago, the sum of their ages was 56. What are their present ages (in years)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 16, 28, 36 • (A) 16, 28, 36: Correct! 8 years ago sum was 56. Present sum = 56 + 3(8) = 80. Ratio sum = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 units. 1 unit = 80 / 20 = 4. Ages = 16, 28, 36.
• (B) 20, 35, 45: Sum = 100.
• (C) 12, 21, 27: Ages 4 years ago.
• (D) 24, 42, 54: Sum = 120.
tip: 💡 Each Person Ages Equally: 8 years ago means 3 × 8 = 24 years total reduction! Present sum = 56 + 24 = 80. Divide 80 in ratio 4:7:9 directly: 16, 28, 36!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If the radius of a circle is increased by 25%, by what percentage does its area increase?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 56.25% • (A) 50%: Trap if candidate simply does 25% + 25% linearly.
• (B) 56.25%: Correct! Area = πr². Net % change = 2r + (r²/100) = 2(25) + (625/100) = 50 + 6.25 = 56.25%.
• (C) 60%: Incorrect.
• (D) 62.5%: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Universal 2D Area Formula: Area % change = a + b + (ab/100). For radius r = 25%: 25 + 25 + 6.25 = 56.25%!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The length, breadth, and height of a room are in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1. If the length is doubled and breadth is halved while height remains the same, the area of the four walls will:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Increase by 40% • (A) Remain unchanged: Trap if candidate assumes doubling length cancels halving breadth.
• (B) Increase by 40%: Correct! Area of 4 walls = 2(l + b)h. Let l=3, b=2, h=1 -> Area = 2(3+2)(1) = 10. New l=6, b=1, h=1 -> Area = 2(6+1)(1) = 14. Increase = (14 - 10)/10 = 40%.
• (C) Decrease by 20%: Calculation trap.
• (D) Increase by 10%: Trap from simple addition.
tip: 💡 Value Substitution Hack: Area depends on (l + b). Initial (3 + 2) = 5. New (6 + 1) = 7. Ratio is 5 : 7, an increase of 2/5 = 40%!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many such small spheres can be obtained?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 27 • (A) 9: Trap of squaring radius ratio (3² = 9).
• (B) 18: Incorrect.
• (C) 27: Correct! Number of spheres = (R / r)³ = (6 / 2)³ = 3³ = 27.
• (D) 36: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Volume Scaling Rule: Volume of any 3D geometric solid scales with the CUBE of its linear dimension: (6 / 2)³ = 3³ = 27 spheres!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The diameter of the base of a right circular cone is 12 cm and its slant height is 10 cm. What is the total surface area of the cone? (Take π = 3.14 or in terms of π)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 96π cm² • (A) 60π cm²: Curved surface area only (πrl = π × 6 × 10 = 60π).
• (B) 96π cm²: Correct! Total Surface Area = πr(l + r) = π × 6 × (10 + 6) = 96π cm².
• (C) 120π cm²: Volume trap.
• (D) 144π cm²: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Read the Question Carefully: 'Total Surface Area' = Curved Area (πrl) + Base Area (πr²) = 60π + 36π = 96π cm²!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A wheel of a police patrolling vehicle makes 1,000 revolutions in traveling a distance of 1.76 km. What is the diameter of the wheel?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 56 cm • (A) 28 cm: Radius of the wheel (trap if question asks for diameter).
• (B) 56 cm: Correct! Distance = 1.76 km = 176,000 cm. Circumference = 176,000 / 1000 = 176 cm. πd = 176 -> (22/7)d = 176 -> d = 56 cm.
• (C) 70 cm: Incorrect.
• (D) 84 cm: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Watch Out: Radius vs. Diameter! The math gives r = 28 cm, but the question explicitly asks for DIAMETER: 2 × 28 = 56 cm!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The perimeter of a rhombus is 100 cm and one of its diagonals is 40 cm. What is the area of the rhombus?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 600 cm² • (A) 400 cm²: Incorrect.
• (B) 500 cm²: Incorrect.
• (C) 600 cm²: Correct! Perimeter = 100 cm -> side = 25 cm. Half-diagonal = 20 cm. In right triangle, other half = √(25² - 20²) = 15 cm. Full d2 = 30 cm. Area = ½ × 40 × 30 = 600 cm².
• (D) 800 cm²: d1 × d2 without dividing by 2.
tip: 💡 Pythagorean Triplet Hack: Side 25 and half-diagonal 20 belong to the 3-4-5 triplet scaled by 5 (15-20-25)! Second diagonal = 30. Area = ½(40)(30) = 600 cm²!

subject: Arithmetic
q: How many terms of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, 15, ... must be added to get a sum of 406?
tip: 💡 Option Test Hack: In AP sum n/2[2a + (n-1)d] = n(2n + 1) = 406. Don't factor the quadratic; test options: 14 × 29 = 406!

subject: Arithmetic
q: In a geometric progression, the 3rd term is 24 and the 6th term is 192. What is the 10th term of this progression?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 3072 • (A) 1536: 9th term.
• (B) 3072: Correct! T3 = ar² = 24, T6 = ar⁵ = 192 -> r³ = 8 -> r = 2. 10th term T10 = T6 × r⁴ = 192 × 16 = 3072.
• (C) 6144: 11th term.
• (D) 768: 8th term.
tip: 💡 Direct Power Multiplication: T10 = T6 × r⁴. You don't even need to find the first term 'a'! T10 = 192 × 2⁴ = 192 × 16 = 3072!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If x + 1/x = 5, find the value of x³ + 1/x³.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 110 • (A) 110: Correct! x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ - 3(x + 1/x) = 5³ - 3(5) = 125 - 15 = 110.
• (B) 125: Trap if candidate only computes 5³.
• (C) 140: Trap if candidate adds 3k instead of subtracting (125 + 15).
• (D) 115: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Universal Formula: If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ - 3k. For k = 5: 125 - 15 = 110!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If a + b + c = 0, what is the value of a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 3 • (A) 0: Common trap.
• (B) 1: Incorrect.
• (C) 3: Correct! Combining fractions: (a³ + b³ + c³)/(abc). When a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc. Result = 3abc / abc = 3.
• (D) -1: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Variable Assumption Hack: Let a = 1, b = 1, c = -2 (sum = 0). Then 1/(-2) + 1/(-2) + 4/1 = -0.5 - 0.5 + 4 = 3! Instant 5-second proof.

subject: Arithmetic
q: The price of sugar falls by 20%. How much percent must a household increase its sugar consumption so as not to decrease expenditure on this item?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 25% • (A) 20%: Trap assuming consumption increases by same % as price drop.
• (B) 25%: Correct! Increase % = [R / (100 - R)] × 100 = (20 / 80) × 100% = 25%.
• (C) 16 ⅔%: Increase needed if price rose by 20%.
• (D) 30%: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Percentage Ladder Shortcut: Price drop of -20% (-1/5) demands consumption rise of +1/(5-1) = +1/4 = +25%!

subject: Arithmetic
q: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not cast their votes and 10% of the votes cast were found invalid. The winning candidate got 54% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 1,620 votes. What was the total number of voters enrolled on the voter list?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 25,000 • (A) 20,000: Incorrect.
• (B) 22,500: Number of votes cast.
• (C) 25,000: Correct! Valid votes = 0.90 × 0.90 × Total = 0.81 Total. Winner majority = 54% - 46% = 8% of valid votes. 0.08 × 0.81 × Total = 1,620 -> Total = 1,620 / 0.0648 = 25,000.
• (D) 27,000: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Reverse Chaining Trick: 8% of Valid = 1,620 -> Valid = 20,250. Since 90% cast and 90% valid (81% overall): Total = 20,250 / 0.81 = 25,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A sum of Rs. 7,500 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for 8 years at 7% per annum equals the simple interest on the second part for 5 years at 8% per annum. What is the smaller part?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Rs. 3,125 • (A) Rs. 3,125: Correct! SI1 = SI2 -> P1 × 8 × 7 = P2 × 5 × 8 -> 56 P1 = 40 P2 -> P1 : P2 = 5 : 7. Sum = 12 units = 7,500 -> 1 unit = 625. Smaller part P1 = 5 × 625 = Rs. 3,125.
• (B) Rs. 3,000: Incorrect.
• (C) Rs. 3,250: Incorrect.
• (D) Rs. 3,500: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Inverse Ratio Shortcut: Principal ratio P1 : P2 = 1/(R1×T1) : 1/(R2×T2) = 1/56 : 1/40 = 5 : 7. Smaller part = (5/12) × 7,500 = Rs. 3,125!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A motorboat whose speed is 15 km/h in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back to the starting point in a total time of 4 hours 30 minutes. What is the speed of the river current?
tip: 💡 Plug Options Directly: 30 / (15 + v) + 30 / (15 - v) = 4.5. Test v = 5: 1.5 + 3 = 4.5 hours! Never waste time solving quadratics.

subject: Arithmetic
q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 16 hours and pipe B can fill it in 24 hours. Both pipes are opened together, but 4 hours before the tank is filled, pipe A is closed. What is the total time taken to fill the tank?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 12 hours • (A) 12 hours: Correct! Total = 48 units. A = 3, B = 2. Last 4 hrs B alone = 8 units. Remaining 40 units by (A+B) = 40 / 5 = 8 hrs. Total = 8 + 4 = 12 hours.
• (B) 14 hours: Incorrect.
• (C) 10 hours: Incorrect.
• (D) 16 hours: Time taken by A alone.
tip: 💡 Add Back Imaginary Work: If pipe A was NOT turned off, it would have added 4 × 3 = 12 units. Total = 48 + 12 = 60 units. Time = 60 / (3 + 2) = 12 hours!

subject: Arithmetic

Correct Answer: (B) 7 • (A) 6: Value if the sequence had minus signs: √(42 - √(42 - ...)).
• (B) 7: Correct! Factor 42 into consecutive integers: 42 = 6 × 7. For '+' series, the answer is the larger factor = 7.
• (C) 8: Incorrect.
• (D) 42: Value inside radical.
tip: 💡 Consecutive Factors Rule: N = n(n + 1). For '+' sign, take (n + 1). For '-' sign, take n. Here 42 = 6 × 7 -> Answer is 7!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A vendor bought toffees at 6 for a rupee. How many for a rupee must he sell to gain 20%?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 5 • (A) 3: Gives 100% profit.
• (B) 4: Gives 50% profit.
• (C) 5: Correct! CP of 1 toffee = 1/6 Re. SP for 20% gain = (1/6) × 1.20 = 1/5 Re. Toffees per rupee = 5.
• (D) 6: Cost price quantity (0% profit).
tip: 💡 Inverse Quantity Trick: To gain 20%, quantity must decrease: 6 / 1.20 = 5 toffees for a rupee!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 4 and their HCF is 4. What is their LCM?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) 48 • (A) 12: The smaller number (3 × 4).
• (B) 16: The larger number (4 × 4).
• (C) 24: Common multiple.
• (D) 48: Correct! Numbers are 3 × 4 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16. LCM = 3 × 4 × HCF = 12 × 4 = 48.
tip: 💡 Ratio LCM Formula: LCM = (Ratio Product) × HCF = 3 × 4 × 4 = 48! Solved in 2 seconds.

subject: Arithmetic
q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. A waste pipe can empty the tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, what fraction of the tank will be filled in 1 hour?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1/10 • (A) 1/10: Correct! 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 of the tank.
• (B) 1/12: Rate of pipe 1.
• (C) 1/15: Rate of pipe 2.
• (D) 1/8: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Net Hourly Work: (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 of tank per hour! Full tank takes 10 hours.

subject: Arithmetic
q: A train running at 54 km/h takes 20 seconds to pass through a tunnel. Next, it takes 12 seconds to pass a telegraph post by the side of the track. What is the length of the tunnel?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 120 m • (A) 120 m: Correct! Speed = 54 km/h = 15 m/s. Train length = 15 × 12 = 180 m. Tunnel passage = 15 × 20 = 300 m. Tunnel length = 300 - 180 = 120 m.
• (B) 150 m: Incorrect.
• (C) 180 m: Length of the train.
• (D) 200 m: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Time Difference Shortcut: The extra (20 - 12) = 8 seconds was spent exclusively covering the tunnel! Tunnel Length = 8 s × 15 m/s = 120 m!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the positions of its digits is 36. What is the difference between the two digits of that number?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 4 • (A) 4: Correct! (10a + b) - (10b + a) = 9(a - b) = 36 -> a - b = 36 / 9 = 4.
• (B) 3: If difference was 27.
• (C) 6: If difference was 54.
• (D) 9: Divisor constant.
tip: 💡 Divisibility by 9 Rule: The difference between any two-digit number and its reversal is ALWAYS 9 times the difference of digits: Difference of digits = 36 / 9 = 4!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If 5 men or 9 women can do a piece of work in 19 days, then in how many days will 3 men and 6 women complete the same work?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 15 days • (A) 12 days: Incorrect.
• (B) 15 days: Correct! Days = Total Days / [(m2/m1) + (w2/w1)] = 19 / [(3/5) + (6/9)] = 19 / [(3/5) + (2/3)] = 19 / (19/15) = 15 days.
• (C) 18 days: Incorrect.
• (D) 10 days: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Standard AND/OR Work Formula: Days = D / [(M_and / M_or) + (W_and / W_or)] = 19 / (3/5 + 6/9) = 19 / (19/15) = 15 days!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A sum of Rs. 4,200 is divided among A, B, C, and D in such a way that (Share of A)/(Share of B) = (Share of B)/(Share of C) = (Share of C)/(Share of D) = 1/2. What is the sum of shares of B and D?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Rs. 2,800 • (A) Rs. 2,600: Incorrect.
• (B) Rs. 3,080: Share of C + D.
• (C) Rs. 2,800: Correct! A:B:C:D = 1:2:4:8 (Sum = 15 units). 1 unit = 4,200 / 15 = 280. B + D = 2 + 8 = 10 units = 10 × 280 = Rs. 2,800.
• (D) Rs. 3,200: Share of D alone (8 × 280 = 2,240).
tip: 💡 Geometric Progression of Shares: When A:B = B:C = C:D = 1:2, shares double each time (1 : 2 : 4 : 8). Total = 15 units. B + D = 10 units = (10/15) × 4,200 = Rs. 2,800!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If the height of a cylinder is increased by 15% and the radius of its base is decreased by 10%, then what is the percentage change in its curved surface area?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 3.5% increase • (A) 3.5% increase: Correct! Curved Surface Area = 2πrh. Net % change = 15 - 10 - (15 × 10)/100 = 5 - 1.5 = +3.5% (increase).
• (B) 3.5% decrease: Sign error.
• (C) 5% increase: Trap ignoring product term (15 - 10).
• (D) No change: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Successive % Shortcut: CSA depends on product r × h. Use x + y + (xy/100) = +15 - 10 - 1.5 = +3.5%! Positive sign means increase!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A car covers a distance of 450 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 15 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less to cover the same distance. What is the original speed of the car?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 75 km/h • (A) 60 km/h: 450/60 = 7.5 hrs, 450/75 = 6.0 hrs (diff = 1.5 hrs).
• (B) 75 km/h: Correct! 450/75 = 6 hours; 450/90 = 5 hours. Difference = 6 - 5 = 1 hour!
• (C) 90 km/h: Increased speed of the car.
• (D) 80 km/h: 450 is not divisible by 80.
tip: 💡 Option Verification: Test 75 km/h: Time at 75 = 6 hrs. Time at 90 = 5 hrs. 6 - 5 = 1 hour exact! Takes only 10 seconds.

subject: Arithmetic
q: A merchant marks his goods up by 40% and gives two successive discounts of 10% and 10%. Find his net profit or loss percentage.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 13.4% profit • (A) 13.4% profit: Correct! Let CP = 100. MP = 140. SP = 140 × 0.90 × 0.90 = 140 × 0.81 = 113.4. Profit = 13.4%.
• (B) 15% profit: Incorrect.
• (C) 10.6% profit: Trap if single 20% discount is applied.
• (D) 2.4% loss: Arithmetic slip.
tip: 💡 Successive Discount Multiplier: Two 10% discounts = 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81. SP = 140 × 0.81 = 113.4 -> Net Profit = 13.4%!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing number in the series: 4, 7, 12, 19, 28, ?, 52
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 39 • (A) 36: Trap if candidate adds 8 instead of following the odd difference sequence.
• (B) 39: Correct! Differences are consecutive odd numbers: 7-4=3, 12-7=5, 19-12=7, 28-19=9. Next difference is +11 -> 28 + 11 = 39. (Check: 39 + 13 = 52).
• (C) 41: Trap if adding 13 directly.
• (D) 42: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Difference of Differences: Calculate differences between consecutive terms: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. 28 + 11 = 39!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the next term in the alphanumeric series: Z1A, X2D, V6G, T24J, ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) R120M • (A) R120M: Correct! First letter decreases by 2: Z(26) -> X(24) -> V(22) -> T(20) -> R(18). Number multiplies sequentially: 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 6×4=24, 24×5=120. Last letter increases by 3: A(1) -> D(4) -> G(7) -> J(10) -> M(13).
• (B) R120L: Incorrect last letter.
• (C) S120M: Incorrect first letter.
• (D) Q120N: Incorrect letters.
tip: 💡 Independent Stream Breakdown: Break alphanumeric terms into 3 streams: 1st letter (-2 each), middle number (×2, ×3, ×4, ×5), 3rd letter (+3 each) -> R, 120, M!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code language, 'ROBUST' is written as 'QNATRS'. How will 'ZXCMPL' be written in that code?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) YWBLOK • (A) YYBLOK: Second letter shifted incorrectly.
• (B) YWBNPK: Fourth and fifth letters shifted incorrectly.
• (C) YWBLOK: Correct! In ROBUST -> QNATRS, each letter is shifted by -1. For ZXCMPL: Z-1=Y, X-1=W, C-1=B, M-1=L, P-1=O, L-1=K.
• (D) YYBNOK: Second letter error.
tip: 💡 Rapid Letter Check: In ROBUST, R->Q, O->N, B->A is clearly -1 for each letter. Look at 2nd letter of ZXCMPL: X - 1 = W. Options A and D eliminated in 2 seconds!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'DELHI' is coded as '73541' and 'CALCUTTA' as '82589662', how will 'CALICUT' be coded?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 8251896 • (A) 8251896: Correct! From DELHI (73541) and CALCUTTA (82589662): C=8, A=2, L=5, I=1, C=8, U=9, T=6. Therefore CALICUT = 8251896.
• (B) 8251296: C coded as 2 trap.
• (C) 8251962: T and U reversed.
• (D) 8521896: A and L reversed.
tip: 💡 Direct Symbol Substitution: Notice that C=8, A=2, L=5 appear in both sample words. Simply map each letter directly to its given digit!

subject: Reasoning
q: Pointing to a photograph of a lady, Rajesh said, 'The son of her only brother is the brother of my wife.' How is the lady related to Rajesh?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Sister of father-in-law • (A) Mother-in-law: Wife's mother.
• (B) Sister of father-in-law: Correct! 'Brother of my wife' = Rajesh's brother-in-law. 'Son of her only brother' is that brother-in-law. Thus 'her only brother' is the wife's father (father-in-law). The lady is the sister of Rajesh's father-in-law.
• (C) Maternal aunt: Mother's sister.
• (D) Grandmother: Wife's grandmother.
tip: 💡 Reverse Chaining Method: Start from the end: 'Brother of my wife' = Wife's brother -> 'Son of her only brother' = Wife's brother -> Her brother = Wife's father (father-in-law) -> She is Father-in-law's sister!

subject: Reasoning
q: If A + B means A is brother of B; A − B means A is sister of B; A × B means A is father of B; A ÷ B means A is mother of B. Which expression indicates that 'M is the maternal uncle of N'?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) M + K ÷ N • (A) M + K ÷ N: Correct! M + K means M is brother of K. K ÷ N means K is mother of N. Brother of mother is maternal uncle.
• (B) M − K × N: M is sister of father (paternal aunt).
• (C) M × K + N: M is father.
• (D) M + K × N: M is paternal uncle (brother of father).
tip: 💡 Target Relation Formula: Maternal Uncle = Brother (+) of Mother (÷). Therefore, look for M + [Female] ÷ N!

subject: Reasoning
q: A police officer starts patrolling from his station and drives 6 km South, then turns left and drives 8 km. He then turns right and drives 4 km, then takes another right turn and drives 8 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his starting police station?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 10 km South • (A) 10 km South: Correct! South 6 km -> Left (East) 8 km -> Right (South) 4 km -> Right (West) 8 km. East 8 km and West 8 km cancel out. Net displacement = 6 South + 4 South = 10 km South.
• (B) 10 km North: Direction reversal trap.
• (C) 18 km South: Simple distance summation.
• (D) 12 km West: Incorrect axis.
tip: 💡 Axis Cancellation Hack: East 8 km and West 8 km completely cancel each other out! The only movement that counts is 6 km South + 4 km South = 10 km South!

subject: Reasoning
q: One morning after sunrise, Suresh was standing facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. In which direction was Suresh facing?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) South • (A) East: Shadow falls behind him.
• (B) West: Shadow falls in front of him.
• (C) North: If facing North, West (shadow) is to his LEFT.
• (D) South: Correct! Morning sun is in East, so shadows fall toward WEST. For West to be to one's RIGHT, one must face SOUTH.
tip: 💡 Morning Shadow Rule: Morning shadow = WEST. Stand and test: If you face South, your right hand points West! Hence Suresh was facing South.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a class of 45 students, rank of Rahul is 18th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 28th • (A) 27th: Trap if candidate simply subtracts 45 - 18 without adding 1.
• (B) 28th: Correct! Rank from Bottom = Total - Rank from Top + 1 = 45 - 18 + 1 = 28th.
• (C) 29th: Double addition trap.
• (D) 26th: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Standard Ranking Formula: Bottom Rank = Total - Top Rank + 1 = 45 - 18 + 1 = 28th! Never forget the '+ 1' compensation for the person themselves.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a row of girls, Kamla is 9th from the left and Veena is 16th from the right. If they interchange their positions, Kamla becomes 25th from the left. How many girls are there in the row?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 40 • (A) 39: Forgets to add both ranks.
• (B) 40: Correct! Kamla occupies Veena's seat. That seat is 25th from left and 16th from right. Total = 25 + 16 - 1 = 40.
• (C) 41: Forgets to subtract 1.
• (D) 42: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Position Interchange Rule: Total = (New rank of Person 1 + Old rank of Person 2) - 1 = 25 + 16 - 1 = 40! Takes 5 seconds.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. All flowers are trees. 2. No tree is a fruit. Conclusions: I. No flower is a fruit. II. Some trees are flowers.
opts: Both conclusions I and II follow
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Both conclusions I and II follow • (A) Only I: Overlooks valid conversion of statement 1.
• (B) Only II: Overlooks transitive deduction.
• (C) Neither: Incorrect.
• (D) Both I and II follow: Correct! Flowers ⊂ Trees, and Trees disjoint from Fruits -> No Flower is Fruit (I follows). All Flowers are Trees -> Some Trees are Flowers (II follows by subalternation).
tip: 💡 Subset Disjoint Rule: If circle A is inside circle B, and circle B does not touch circle C, then circle A can NEVER touch circle C! Both conclusions are valid.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. Some doctors are teachers. 2. All teachers are engineers. 3. All engineers are scientists. Conclusions: I. Some scientists are doctors. II. All teachers are scientists. III. Some engineers are doctors.
opts: All I, II, and III follow
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) All I, II, and III follow • (A) Only I and II follow.
• (B) Only II and III follow.
• (C) Only I and III follow.
• (D) All follow: Correct! Doctors overlap Teachers; Teachers ⊂ Engineers ⊂ Scientists. Thus: Doctors overlap Scientists (I), Teachers ⊂ Scientists (II), Engineers overlap Doctors (III).
tip: 💡 Concentric Enclosure: Teachers ⊂ Engineers ⊂ Scientists. Since some Doctors are Teachers, that portion of Doctors is simultaneously Teachers, Engineers, and Scientists!

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following Venn diagrams correctly depicts the relationship between: Judges, Thieves, and Criminals?
opts: Two circles intersecting inside a large circle
Circle of Thieves entirely inside Criminals, and Judges completely separate
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Circle of Thieves entirely inside Criminals, and Judges completely separate • (A) Three separate circles: Ignores that thieves are criminals.
• (B) Partial intersection: A thief cannot be outside the category of criminals.
• (C) Thieves inside Criminals, Judges separate: Correct! By definition, all thieves are criminals. Judges belong to the judicial system, entirely separate from criminals.
• (D) All three concentric circles: Absurd implication that judges are thieves.
tip: 💡 Legal Hierarchy: All Thieves are Criminals (concentric). Judges administer law and are mutually exclusive from criminals (disjoint circle)!

subject: Reasoning
q: At what angle are the hands of a clock inclined at 15 minutes past 4 o'clock?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 37.5° • (A) 30°: Trap assuming hour hand stays fixed at 4.
• (B) 37.5°: Correct! Angle θ = |30H - 5.5M| = |30(4) - 5.5(15)| = |120 - 82.5| = 37.5°.
• (C) 45°: Calculation error.
• (D) 52.5°: Adding instead of subtracting.
tip: 💡 Standard Clock Angle Formula: Angle = |30H - 5.5M| = |120 - 82.5| = 37.5°! In 15 minutes, the hour hand moves 15 × 0.5° = 7.5° past 4: 30° + 7.5° = 37.5°!

subject: Reasoning
q: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock will the hands of a clock be in the same straight line but pointing in opposite directions?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 5 5/11 minutes past 7 • (A) 5 minutes past 7: Ignores hour hand movement.
• (B) 5 5/11 minutes past 7: Correct! At 7:00, hands are 35 min apart. To be opposite, they must be 30 min apart -> minute hand must gain 5 min spaces. Time = 5 × (12/11) = 60/11 = 5 5/11 min.
• (C) 5 3/11 minutes: Calculation slip.
• (D) 5 7/11 minutes: Calculation slip.
tip: 💡 Target Space Multiplier: Identify opposite mark on dial: Opposite to 7 is 1 (5 minute mark). Multiply by 12/11: 5 × 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes past 7!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 15th August 2023 was a Tuesday, on which day of the week did 26th January 2024 fall?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Friday • (A) Wednesday: 1 odd day.
• (B) Thursday: 2 odd days.
• (C) Friday: Correct! Days: Aug (16) + Sep (30) + Oct (31) + Nov (30) + Dec (31) + Jan (26) = 164 days. 164 mod 7 = 3 odd days. Tuesday + 3 days = Friday.
• (D) Saturday: 4 odd days.
tip: 💡 Month-wise Odd Days: Aug (16 mod 7 = 2) + Sep (2) + Oct (3) + Nov (2) + Dec (3) + Jan (26 mod 7 = 5) = 17 odd days ≡ 3 odd days. Tuesday + 3 = Friday!

subject: Reasoning
q: How many times does the 29th day of a month occur in 400 consecutive years?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 4497 • (A) 4497: Correct! In 400 years, 11 months always have a 29th day (400 × 11 = 4400). In 400 years, there are 97 leap years (each adding Feb 29). Total = 4400 + 97 = 4497.
• (B) 4400: Ignores all February 29ths.
• (C) 97: Trap if candidate only counts Feb 29!
• (D) 4800: Assumes all 12 months have 29 days every year.
tip: 💡 Read the Question Trap: It asks for the '29th day of a month', NOT just 'February 29'! All 11 other months have a 29th every year: (400 × 11) + 97 leap Febs = 4497!

subject: Reasoning
q: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, and F are sitting in a circle facing towards the centre. E is to the immediate left of D. C is between A and B. F is between E and A. Who is sitting to the immediate right of C?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) B • (A) A: Sits to the immediate left of C.
• (B) B: Correct! Arrangement clockwise: D -> E -> F -> A -> C -> B -> D. Facing center, the person to the immediate right of C is B.
• (C) D: Sits opposite C.
• (D) E: Sits between D and F.
tip: 💡 Center-Facing Rule: When facing the center of a circle, 'Immediate Right' moves Counter-Clockwise! Right of C is B.

subject: Reasoning
q: Five persons P, Q, R, S, and T are standing in a queue. T is behind P. S is between P and Q. R is immediately in front of Q. Who is standing at the front of the queue?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) R • (A) P: Second from the back.
• (B) Q: Second from the front.
• (C) R: Correct! R is in front of Q (R > Q). S is between P and Q (Q > S > P). T is behind P (P > T). Full queue from front to back: R -> Q -> S -> P -> T.
• (D) T: At the very back of the queue.
tip: 💡 Directional Linkages: Link clues from front to back: R > Q > S > P > T. R is at the front of the queue!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: 'Use our eco-friendly municipal electric buses to reduce air pollution and traffic congestion in the city' — An appeal by Urban Transport Authority. Assumptions: I. People prefer eco-friendly public transport. II. Electric buses help reduce urban traffic emissions.
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Both assumptions I and II are implicit • (A) Only I is implicit.
• (B) Only II is implicit.
• (C) Neither is implicit.
• (D) Both are implicit: Correct! An official public appeal assumes: (I) People will respond positively to eco-friendly options; (II) The recommended vehicle actually reduces urban pollution.
tip: 💡 Public Appeal Principle: Whenever an authority appeals to the public, it implicitly assumes both that the solution works AND that the public is receptive to the appeal!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A large number of college students have been found indulging in substance abuse near campuses. Courses of Action: I. Police should conduct strict vigilance and crack down heavily on drug peddling networks around campuses. II. The government should shut down all colleges indefinitely.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Only I follows • (A) Only I follows: Correct! Targeted law enforcement against drug peddlers directly tackles crime without disrupting education.
• (B) Only II follows: Shutting down all colleges is extreme, absurd, and counter-productive.
• (C) Either follows.
• (D) Neither follows.
tip: 💡 Administrative Proportionality: A valid course of action must be constructive, proportionate, and target the wrongdoers, never shut down essential civic institutions!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the odd one out:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Gold : Corrosion • (A) Iron : Rust: Iron oxidizes into rust.
• (B) Bronze : Patina: Bronze develops a green surface patina.
• (C) Copper : Tarnish: Copper tarnishes upon exposure.
• (D) Gold : Corrosion: Correct! Gold is a noble, chemically inert metal that does NOT undergo natural atmospheric corrosion or rust.
tip: 💡 Chemical Reactivity Series: Gold (Au) and Platinum (Pt) are noble metals; they resist corrosion and do not rust under normal conditions!

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the pair that shows the same relationship as: Courage : Bravery
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Embezzlement : Fraud • (A) Wealth : Poverty: Antonyms.
• (B) Embezzlement : Fraud: Correct! Courage and Bravery are exact synonyms. Embezzlement and Fraud are synonymous criminal misappropriations.
• (C) Mentor : Disciple: Teacher-student relationship.
• (D) Law : Anarchy: Antonyms.
tip: 💡 Semantic Equality: Courage = Bravery (Synonyms). Embezzlement = Fraud (Synonyms)! All other pairs are antonyms or roles.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'P' denotes '+', 'Q' denotes '−', 'R' denotes '×', and 'S' denotes '÷', then what is the value of: 32 S 4 R 8 P 16 Q 14 = ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 66 • (A) 66: Correct! 32 ÷ 4 × 8 + 16 - 14 = (8 × 8) + 16 - 14 = 64 + 16 - 14 = 66.
• (B) 68: Arithmetic slip.
• (C) 70: Incorrect.
• (D) 72: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Strictly Follow BODMAS: Division (32÷4=8) -> Multiply (8×8=64) -> Add (64+16=80) -> Subtract (80-14=66)!

subject: Reasoning

Correct Answer: (B) 924 • (A) 524: Incorrect.
• (B) 924: Correct! Reverse digits of both factors: 13×12 -> 31×21 = 651. 41×23 -> 14×32 = 448. For 24×22 -> 42×22 = 924.
• (C) 825: Incorrect.
• (D) 428: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Reversal Operation: Reverse the digits before multiplying: 24 becomes 42, 22 stays 22. 42 × 22 = 924!

subject: Reasoning
q: How many triangles are there in the standard figure formed by a square with both diagonals drawn and horizontal/vertical bisectors connecting opposite midpoints?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 16 • (A) 12: Missing large triangles.
• (B) 14: Missing 2 composite triangles.
• (C) 16: Correct! Square divided by diagonals and mid-point bisectors forms 8 basic sectors: 8 small (1 sector) + 4 medium (2 sectors) + 4 large (4 sectors) = 16 triangles.
• (D) 18: Overcounting.
tip: 💡 Standard Formula: For an 8-sector symmetrical central junction: Total Triangles = 2 × (Number of sectors) = 2 × 8 = 16!

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the alternative that closely resembles the mirror image of the given combination when mirror is placed to its right: POLICE2024
opts: P O L I C E 2 0 2 4
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 4202ECILOP (with mirrored glyphs) • (A) P O L I C E 2 0 2 4: Unmodified string.
• (B) 4202ECILOP (mirrored glyphs): Correct! Mirror to the right inverts the entire sequence (starts with 4, ends with P) and reflects each letter/digit laterally.
• (C) 4202POLICE: Only digits reversed.
• (D) ECILOP2024: Letters and numbers split.
tip: 💡 Right-Side Mirror Rule: The rightmost character (4) becomes the leftmost, and every individual glyph is flipped horizontally!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a code language: 'pit dar na' means 'you are welcome', 'na ho pa' means 'welcome to home', 'dar pa so' means 'home are bright'. What is the code for 'bright'?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) so • (A) dar: Means 'are' (common in sentences 1 and 3).
• (B) pa: Means 'home' (common in sentences 2 and 3).
• (C) so: Correct! In sentence 3 ('dar pa so' = 'home are bright'), 'dar'='are' and 'pa'='home'. The only remaining word is 'so' = 'bright'.
• (D) pit: Means 'you'.
tip: 💡 Elimination Cross-Reference: Compare sentence 3 with 1 and 2: 'dar' is 'are', 'pa' is 'home'. The leftover code 'so' corresponds directly to 'bright'!

subject: Reasoning
q: Introducing a man, a woman says, 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the woman?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Husband • (A) Brother: Father's son.
• (B) Husband: Correct! 'Only daughter of my father' for a female speaker is herself. If his wife is herself, the man is her husband.
• (C) Father-in-law: Spouse's father.
• (D) Uncle: Father's brother.
tip: 💡 Identity Clue: 'Only daughter of my father' spoken by a woman is strictly HERSELF. His wife is me -> He is my husband!

subject: Reasoning
q: If South-East becomes North, North-East becomes West, and so on, what will West become?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) South-East • (A) South-East: Correct! South-East becomes North -> rotated 135° anti-clockwise. Turning West by 135° anti-clockwise lands on South-East.
• (B) North-East: Clockwise rotation trap.
• (C) South-West: 45° rotation.
• (D) North-West: 45° clockwise.
tip: 💡 Constant Angle Shift: Measure angle from SE to N = 135° anti-clockwise. Rotate West by 135° anti-clockwise: West -> South-West (45°) -> South (90°) -> South-East (135°)!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing number in the matrix: [Row 1: 6, 9, 12; Row 2: 4, 8, 16; Row 3: 24, 72, ?]
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 192 • (A) 144: 12 × 12.
• (B) 192: Correct! Row 1 × Row 2 = Row 3: 6 × 4 = 24; 9 × 8 = 72; 12 × 16 = 192.
• (C) 180: Incorrect.
• (D) 120: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Vertical Product Pattern: Column 1: 6×4=24. Column 2: 9×8=72. Column 3: 12×16 = 192!

subject: Reasoning
q: If '+' means '÷', '−' means '×', '×' means '−', and '÷' means '+', what is the value of: 40 + 5 − 6 ÷ 18 × 12 = ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 54 • (A) 54: Correct! Replacing signs: 40 ÷ 5 × 6 + 18 - 12 = 8 × 6 + 18 - 12 = 48 + 18 - 12 = 54.
• (B) 48: Neglects addition.
• (C) 50: Arithmetic slip.
• (D) 62: Sign error.
tip: 💡 Substitution Rule: Write out new signs clearly: (40 ÷ 5) × 6 + 18 - 12 = 48 + 6 = 54!

subject: Reasoning
q: Question: Is X the brother of Y? Statements: I. X and Y are children of Z, and X is a male. II. Y is the sister of W.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Statement I alone is sufficient • (A) Statement I alone is sufficient: Correct! Stmt I specifies X and Y share parents Z, and X is male. Therefore X is unconditionally the brother of Y (regardless of Y's gender).
• (B) Statement II alone is sufficient: Stmt II only gives Y's relation to W, saying nothing about X.
• (C) Both together needed: Unnecessary since I alone resolves the question.
• (D) Neither sufficient: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Focus on the Subject: The question asks 'Is X the brother of Y?' Statement I confirms X is male and shares parents with Y. That guarantees X is Y's brother! Y's gender is completely irrelevant!

subject: Reasoning
q: Question: What is the code for 'apple' in a code language? Statements: I. 'kio su pie' means 'fresh sweet apple'. II. 'pie ron tik' means 'sweet red cherry'.
opts: Even both statements together are not sufficient
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Even both statements together are not sufficient • (A) Statement I alone sufficient: 3 words mapped to 3 codes.
• (B) Statement II alone sufficient: Does not contain 'apple'.
• (C) Both together sufficient: Incorrect.
• (D) Neither sufficient: Correct! Common word is 'sweet' = 'pie'. In Stmt I, 'fresh' and 'apple' remain ambiguously mapped to 'kio' and 'su'. It is impossible to know which code belongs to 'apple'.
tip: 💡 Ambiguous Remainder: Eliminating 'sweet' = 'pie' leaves TWO words ('fresh', 'apple') and TWO codes ('kio', 'su'). Without a third statement, 'apple' cannot be determined uniquely!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code, 'MONKEY' is written as 'XDJMNL'. How is 'TIGER' written in that code?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) QDFHS • (A) QDFHS: Correct! Reverse MONKEY to Y-E-K-N-O-M, then subtract 1 from each: X-D-J-M-N-L. For TIGER, reverse to R-E-G-I-T, then subtract 1: R-1=Q, E-1=D, G-1=F, I-1=H, T-1=S -> QDFHS.
• (B) SDFHS: Forward shift on R.
• (C) SHFDQ: Direct order reversed.
• (D) UJHFS: Shifted forward.
tip: 💡 Two-Step Coding Logic: Step 1: Reverse letter order. Step 2: Subtract 1 from each letter: R-E-G-I-T -> Q-D-F-H-S!

subject: Reasoning
q: If each digit in the number 9436527 is arranged in ascending order from left to right, what will be the difference between the fourth digit from the left and the second digit from the right?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 2 • (A) 2: Correct! Digits of 9436527 in ascending order: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9. Fourth digit from left = 5. Second digit from right = 7. Difference = 7 - 5 = 2.
• (B) 3: Calculation slip.
• (C) 4: Difference between 7 and 3.
• (D) 1: Difference between adjacent digits.
tip: 💡 Sort and Mark: 2, 3, 4, [5], 6, [7], 9. Left-to-right 4th is 5; right-to-left 2nd is 7. 7 - 5 = 2!

subject: Reasoning
q: Complete the series: 2, 3, 8, 27, 112, ?
tip: 💡 Standard Progression: Pattern is ×n + n. For the 5th step: (112 × 5) + 5 = 560 + 5 = 565!

subject: Reasoning
q: Complete the letter series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) V • (A) S: Position 19.
• (B) T: Position 20.
• (C) V: Correct! Letter positions: B(2) +2 = D(4); D(4) +3 = G(7); G(7) +4 = K(11); K(11) +5 = P(16); P(16) +6 = V(22).
• (D) W: Position 23.
tip: 💡 Triangular Increment: Differences are +2, +3, +4, +5, +6. P is 16; 16 + 6 = 22 = V!

subject: Reasoning
q: In an army camp of 50 officers, 30 like tea, 25 like coffee, and 10 like both tea and coffee. How many officers like neither tea nor coffee?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 5 • (A) 5: Correct! n(Tea ∪ Coffee) = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Neither = Total - 45 = 50 - 45 = 5.
• (B) 10: Number liking both.
• (C) 15: Officers liking only coffee.
• (D) 8: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Union Formula: Total liking at least one = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Those liking neither = 50 - 45 = 5!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the odd one out among: 27, 64, 125, 144, 216
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) 144 • (A) 27: Perfect cube (3³).
• (B) 64: Perfect cube (4³), also 8².
• (C) 125: Perfect cube (5³).
• (D) 144: Correct! 144 is 12² (a square), but NOT a cube. 216 is 6³. All others are cubes.
tip: 💡 Cube Pattern Identification: 3³=27, 4³=64, 5³=125, 6³=216. 144 is only a square (12²), making it the odd one out!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. All pens are bags. 2. All bags are glasses. 3. No glass is a spoon. Conclusions: I. No pen is a spoon. II. Some glasses are pens.
opts: Both conclusions I and II follow
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Both conclusions I and II follow • (A) Only I follows.
• (B) Only II follows.
• (C) Neither follows.
• (D) Both I and II follow: Correct! Pens ⊂ Bags ⊂ Glasses. Glasses disjoint from Spoons -> No Pen is a Spoon (I follows). All Pens are Glasses -> Some Glasses are Pens (II follows).
tip: 💡 Concentric Circles Rule: Pens are nested inside Glasses. Since Glasses cannot touch Spoons, Pens cannot touch Spoons either! Both follow.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: Most citizens in the metropolis support strict environmental regulations on industrial units. Conclusions: I. Industrial pollution is a major civic concern. II. All industries in the metropolis must be closed down.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Only conclusion I follows • (A) Only I follows: Correct! High public support for strict industrial pollution rules indicates pollution is an active civic concern. Shutting down all industries is an extreme, unsupported generalization.
• (B) Only II follows.
• (C) Either follows.
• (D) Neither follows.
tip: 💡 Avoid Extreme Conclusions: 'Regulating' never implies 'shutting down all industries'! Absolute words ('all', 'every') in conclusions are almost always false.

subject: Reasoning
q: A man walks 1 km East, then turns South and walks 5 km, then turns East and walks 2 km, then turns North and walks 9 km. How far is he from his starting point?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 5 km • (A) 3 km: Net horizontal displacement.
• (B) 4 km: Net vertical displacement.
• (C) 5 km: Correct! East: 1 + 2 = 3 km. North: 9 - 5 = 4 km. Straight-line distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.
• (D) 7 km: Sum of 3 + 4.
tip: 💡 3-4-5 Pythagorean Triplet: Net East = 3 km, Net North = 4 km. The hypotenuse of a 3-4 right triangle is ALWAYS 5 km!

subject: Reasoning
q: Which digit appears opposite to the face with number 4 when a standard die is rolled and faces are shown: Pos 1: (1, 2, 3); Pos 2: (1, 3, 5); Pos 3: (2, 3, 6)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 3 • (A) 1: Adjacent to 3.
• (B) 2: Adjacent to 3.
• (C) 3: Correct! 3 is adjacent to 1, 2, 5, and 6 across the views. The only number not adjacent to 3 is 4, which means 3 is opposite to 4.
• (D) 5: Adjacent to 3.
tip: 💡 Elimination of Adjacent Faces: If a number is seen adjacent to 4 other numbers (1, 2, 5, 6), the one unseen number (4) MUST be on its opposite face!

subject: Reasoning
q: A clock gains 5 seconds every 3 minutes. It was set right at 7:00 a.m. In the afternoon of the same day, when the clock indicated 4:15 p.m., what was the true time?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 4:00 p.m. • (A) 4:00 p.m.: Correct! Clock gains 5s in 3 min = 1 min in 36 min. From 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 9 hours = 540 min. Gain = 540 / 36 = 15 min. When clock shows 4:15 p.m., actual time is 4:00 p.m.
• (B) 4:05 p.m.: Partial correction.
• (C) 3:45 p.m.: Subtracting gain twice.
• (D) 4:10 p.m.: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Rate of Gain Hack: Gain = 5 sec / 3 min = 1 min every 36 min. In 9 true hours (540 min), it gains 540/36 = 15 minutes. 4:15 p.m. minus 15 min = 4:00 p.m.!

subject: Reasoning
q: In an examination, a candidate gets 3 marks for every correct answer and loses 1 mark for every wrong answer. If he attempts all 100 questions and scores 180 marks, how many questions did he answer correctly?
tip: 💡 Net Score Loss Shortcut: Perfect score = 300. Deficit = 300 - 180 = 120 marks. Each wrong answer loses 3 + 1 = 4 marks. Wrong answers = 120 / 4 = 30. Correct answers = 100 - 30 = 70!

subject: Reasoning
q: Arrange the words in a logical sequence: 1. Crime, 2. Police, 3. Judge, 4. Judgment, 5. Punishment
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 • (A) 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: Correct! Sequential order: Crime occurs (1) -> Police investigate (2) -> Presented before Judge (3) -> Judgment delivered (4) -> Punishment served (5).
• (B) 1, 2, 4, 3, 5: Judgment before Judge is impossible.
• (C) 2, 1, 3, 4, 5: Police before Crime is incorrect.
• (D) 1, 3, 2, 4, 5: Judge before Police investigation.
tip: 💡 Chronological Flow: Crime -> Police -> Judge -> Judgment -> Punishment! Follows standard Indian Criminal Procedure (CrPC/BNSS).

subject: Reasoning
q: Count the number of straight lines in a geometric figure containing a regular hexagon with all three principal diagonals connecting opposite vertices.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 9 • (A) 9: Correct! A regular hexagon has 6 outer boundary sides. Joining opposite vertices produces 3 principal diagonals traversing through the center. Total continuous straight lines = 6 + 3 = 9.
• (B) 12: Overcounting line segments.
• (C) 15: Incorrect.
• (D) 18: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Continuous Lines Rule: A straight line runs from end to end without bending! 6 perimeter lines + 3 central cross-diagonals = 9 straight lines!

subject: Reasoning
q: If in a code language 'EARTH' is written as 'FCUXM', how will 'VENUS' be written?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) WGQYX • (A) WGQYX: Correct! EARTH -> FCUXM shifts each letter by +1, +2, +3, +4, +5: E+1=F, A+2=C, R+3=U, T+4=X, H+5=M. For VENUS: V+1=W, E+2=G, N+3=Q, U+4=Y, S+5=X -> WGQYX.
• (B) WGPZX: Arithmetic error.
• (C) WHQZX: First shift error.
• (D) WGPZW: Last shift error.
tip: 💡 Incremental Ladder: Add (+1, +2, +3, +4, +5) to letter values. V(22)+1=23(W), E(5)+2=7(G), N(14)+3=17(Q) -> WGQ eliminates other options!

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the total number of parallelograms formed by a set of 4 parallel lines intersecting another set of 3 parallel lines?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 18 • (A) 12: 4 × 3.
• (B) 18: Correct! Number of parallelograms formed by m and n parallel lines = ᵐC₂ × ⁿC₂ = ⁴C₂ × ³C₂ = 6 × 3 = 18.
• (C) 24: Incorrect.
• (D) 36: Incorrect.
tip: 💡 Standard Combinations Formula: Parallelograms = ⁴C₂ × ³C₂ = [(4×3)/2] × [(3×2)/2] = 6 × 3 = 18!

subject: General Science
q: Consider the following statements regarding the optical phenomenon of Total Internal Reflection (TIR): 1. Light must travel from an optically denser to an optically rarer medium. 2. Angle of incidence must exceed critical angle. 3. Optical fibres work on TIR principle. Which are correct?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) 1, 2, and 3 • (A) 1 and 2 only: Overlooks technological application in telecommunications.
• (B) 2 and 3 only: Overlooks essential density condition.
• (C) 1 and 3 only: Overlooks critical angle requirement.
• (D) 1, 2, and 3: Correct! TIR requires light to travel from denser to rarer medium (1), angle of incidence i > critical angle c (2), and forms the operational foundation of modern fiber-optic cables (3).
tip: 💡 Twin TIR Prerequisites: (1) Denser -> Rarer medium; (2) Angle of incidence > Critical angle. Applications include Optical fibers, Endoscopes, Mirage, and Diamond brilliance!

subject: General Science
q: Match List-I (Vitamins) with List-II (Deficiency Disorders): (a) Vitamin B1 − (3) Beri-Beri; (b) Vitamin C − (4) Scurvy; (c) Vitamin D − (2) Rickets; (d) Vitamin B12 − (1) Pernicious Anemia. Select the correct code:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) (a)-3, (b)-4, (c)-2, (d)-1 • (A) (a)-3, (b)-4, (c)-2, (d)-1: Correct! Vit B1 (Thiamine) -> Beri-Beri; Vit C (Ascorbic acid) -> Scurvy (bleeding gums); Vit D (Calciferol) -> Rickets (soft bones); Vit B12 (Cyanocobalamin) -> Pernicious Anemia.
• (B) Mismatches Vitamin C and B1.
• (C) Mismatches Vitamin C and D.
• (D) Mismatches Vitamin B1 and B12.
tip: 💡 Vitamin Chemical Names Mnemonic: B1 = Thiamine (Beri-beri); C = Ascorbic (Scurvy); D = Calciferol (Rickets); B12 = Cobalamin (Pernicious Anemia, contains Cobalt)!

subject: General Science
q: Which of the following greenhouse gases has the highest Global Warming Potential (GWP) over a 100-year time horizon?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆) • (A) Carbon dioxide (CO₂): Baseline standard with GWP = 1, but largest total volume emitted.
• (B) Methane (CH₄): 100-year GWP of ~28.
• (C) Nitrous oxide (N₂O): 100-year GWP of ~273.
• (D) Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆): Correct! SF₆ has an astronomical 100-year GWP of ~23,500, used as an electrical insulator in high-voltage switchgear.
tip: 💡 Highest Volume vs. Highest Potency: CO₂ causes the MOST warming by sheer volume, but molecule-for-molecule, SF₆ is the most potent greenhouse gas known (~23,500 times CO₂)!

subject: General Science
q: Consider the following statements regarding ISRO's Aditya-L1 Mission: 1. It is India's first dedicated space observatory to study the Sun. 2. Spacecraft is placed in halo orbit around L1 point (1.5 million km from Earth). 3. VELC payload was built by PRL Ahmedabad. Which is/are correct?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1 and 2 only • (A) 1 and 2 only: Correct! Aditya-L1 is India's 1st dedicated solar mission (1) placed in a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 point 1.5 million km away (2). Statement 3 is false: VELC was developed by Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) Bengaluru, not PRL Ahmedabad.
• (B) 2 only.
• (C) 1 and 3 only.
• (D) 1, 2, and 3: Trap attributing VELC to PRL.
tip: 💡 Payload Institution Match: Primary payload VELC (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) was designed by IIA Bengaluru! ASPEX was developed by PRL Ahmedabad.

subject: General Science
q: Which enzyme is responsible for the breakdown of emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol in the human digestive system?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Lipase • (A) Pepsin: Gastric enzyme that hydrolyzes proteins into peptones in the acidic stomach.
• (B) Lipase: Correct! Secreted by pancreas and small intestine, lipase breaks down bile-emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
• (C) Trypsin: Pancreatic enzyme breaking down proteins in the alkaline duodenum.
• (D) Amylase: Breaks starch into maltose (salivary and pancreatic).
tip: 💡 Biochemical Suffix Rule: Lipase acts on LIPIDS (fats). Amylase acts on AMYLOSE (starch). Pepsin/Trypsin act on PEPTIDE bonds (proteins)!

subject: General Science
q: The fuel used in a Fast Breeder Reactor (FBR), such as the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam, is:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mixed Plutonium-Uranium Oxide (MOX) • (A) Natural Uranium Oxide: Fuel for Stage-1 PHWRs (Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors).
• (B) Mixed Plutonium-Uranium Oxide (MOX): Correct! India's Stage-2 500 MWe PFBR at Kalpakkam utilizes MOX fuel with liquid sodium coolant to breed more fissile fuel than it consumes.
• (C) Enriched Thorium-232: Fertile blanket material earmarked for Stage-3 reactors.
• (D) Heavy Water and Deuterium: Moderator/coolant in Stage-1, not fuel.
tip: 💡 India's 3-Stage Nuclear Plan: Stage 1 = PHWR (Natural Uranium); Stage 2 = FBR (MOX - Plutonium + Uranium); Stage 3 = AHWR (Thorium-232 / U-233)!

subject: General Science
q: What type of electromagnetic radiation is utilized in night vision equipment and thermal imaging cameras used by police forces?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Infrared radiation • (A) Ultraviolet radiation: Used for forensic detection of latent fingerprints and body fluids.
• (B) Infrared radiation: Correct! Thermal imaging cameras detect blackbody radiation emitted in the far-infrared spectrum (heat signatures) in absolute darkness.
• (C) Gamma radiation: High-energy ionizing rays used for cancer radiotherapy and industrial radiography.
• (D) Microwaves: Used in speed radar guns and wireless satellite communication.
tip: 💡 Police Tech Tip: Heat = Infrared (thermal cameras & night goggles). Fingerprint luminescence = Ultraviolet!

subject: General Science
q: Which chemical compound is commonly used as a 'coagulant' in municipal water treatment plants to purify turbidity and suspended particles?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Alum (Potash Alum) • (A) Bleaching powder: Chemical disinfectant (CaOCl₂) releasing chlorine to kill pathogens.
• (B) Alum (Potash Alum): Correct! KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O hydrolyzes in water to produce gelatinous aluminum hydroxide, neutralizing negatively charged clay colloids to precipitate them as floc.
• (C) Sodium bicarbonate: Baking soda (NaHCO₃), an antacid.
• (D) Copper sulphate: Algicide used to control algal blooms in open reservoirs.
tip: 💡 Two-Step Municipal Treatment: Coagulation/Sedimentation = ALUM; Disinfection/Sterilization = BLEACHING POWDER / CHLORINE!

subject: General Science
q: In forensic science and criminal investigation, the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) technique is primarily used for:
opts: Amplifying minute quantities of DNA samples
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Amplifying minute quantities of DNA samples • (A) Separating blood serum proteins: Accomplished via gel electrophoresis.
• (B) Amplifying minute quantities of DNA samples: Correct! Invented by Kary Mullis (1983), PCR replicates microscopic biological traces (hair root, drop of blood) into millions of DNA copies for forensic profiling.
• (C) Detecting alcohol concentration: Measured using breathalyzers (fuel-cell or infrared).
• (D) Ballistic gunpowder residue: Analyzed via Griess test or SEM-EDX.
tip: 💡 Crime Lab Golden Technique: PCR = Molecular Photocopier! Amplifies trace DNA from crime scenes so forensic scientists can run STR (Short Tandem Repeat) profiling.

subject: General Science
q: Consider statements about AI: 1. Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning based on Artificial Neural Networks. 2. Large Language Models (LLMs) utilize transformer architecture. Which is/are correct?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Both 1 and 2 • (A) 1 only.
• (B) 2 only.
• (C) Both 1 and 2: Correct! Deep Learning is a neural network-based subset of ML (1), and modern LLMs (such as GPT-4, Gemini) rely fundamentally on the Transformer self-attention architecture introduced by Vaswani et al. in 2017 (2).
• (D) Neither 1 nor 2.
tip: 💡 AI Taxonomy Hierarchy: Artificial Intelligence ⊃ Machine Learning ⊃ Deep Learning (Neural Networks). Transformers power modern LLMs!

subject: General Science
q: The human body's master biological clock that regulates circadian rhythms (sleep-wake cycles) is located in the:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of hypothalamus • (A) Pineal gland: Synthesizes melatonin hormone, but acts downstream under instructions from SCN.
• (B) Suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of hypothalamus: Correct! Located directly above the optic chiasm, the SCN is the pacemaker of the 24-hour circadian rhythm in mammals.
• (C) Thyroid gland: Regulates basal metabolic rate (BMR) via thyroxine.
• (D) Pituitary gland: Master endocrine gland controlling hormone secretion.
tip: 💡 Pacemaker vs. Hormone: Master Clock = SCN (in Hypothalamus); Sleep Hormone Producer = Pineal Gland (Melatonin)!

subject: General Science
q: Which of the following is NOT an indigenous missile system developed under India's Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) BrahMos • (A) Prithvi: Surface-to-surface ballistic missile under IGMDP.
• (B) Agni: Intermediate/intercontinental ballistic missile under IGMDP.
• (C) Akash: Medium-range surface-to-air missile under IGMDP.
• (D) BrahMos: Correct! BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed as an Indo-Russian joint venture (Brahmaputra + Moskva), NOT part of Kalam's 1983 IGMDP.
tip: 💡 Kalam's IGMDP Mnemonic: PATNA = Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Nag, Akash. BrahMos was developed outside IGMDP with Russia!

subject: Current Events
q: Which country hosted the 16th BRICS Summit in October 2024, the first summit held after the formal expansion of BRICS?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Russia (Kazan) • (A) South Africa: Hosted 15th Summit at Johannesburg (2023).
• (B) Russia (Kazan): Correct! Held in Kazan, Russia in October 2024, marking the historic expansion of BRICS (incorporating Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE).
• (C) Brazil: Scheduled to host in 2025.
• (D) India: Hosted 13th Summit in 2021.
tip: 💡 BRICS Expansion Milestone: Kazan Summit (October 2024) was chaired by Vladimir Putin and attended by PM Narendra Modi, marking BRICS expansion!

subject: Current Events
q: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2024 was awarded to Nihon Hidankyo, a grassroots movement of atomic bomb survivors (Hibakusha), for its efforts to:
opts: Achieve a world free of nuclear weapons
Protect civilian rights in active conflict zones
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Achieve a world free of nuclear weapons • (A) Promote climate change mitigation: E.g., IPCC / Al Gore (2007).
• (B) Achieve a world free of nuclear weapons: Correct! Awarded to Nihon Hidankyo, the Japanese confederation of atomic bomb survivors (Hibakusha) from Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
• (C) Protect civilian rights in active conflict zones.
• (D) Mediate democratic transitions.
tip: 💡 Hibakusha Taboo: Nihon Hidankyo was honored for creating the international moral norm/taboo against the use of nuclear weapons!

subject: Current Events
q: India won historic dual gold medals in both the Open and Women's sections at which international sports event in 2024?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad (Budapest) • (A) World Table Tennis Championship.
• (B) 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad (Budapest): Correct! India won unprecedented dual gold medals in both Open section (Gukesh, Erigaisi, Praggnanandhaa, Vidit, Harikrishna) and Women's section (Harika, Vaishali, Divya, Vantika, Tania).
• (C) Badminton Super Series.
• (D) Asian Athletics Championship.
tip: 💡 Telangana Chess Pride: Grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi (from Warangal, Telangana) played board 3 and won individual individual Gold with a 2968 performance rating!

subject: Current Events
q: In the Global Innovation Index (GII) published by WIPO, India's ranking improved to which position in recent editions?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 39th • (A) 39th: Correct! Published annually by WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization), India rose to 39th position among 133 economies in the GII 2024 edition.
• (B) 48th: Rank in 2020.
• (C) 52nd: Rank in 2019.
• (D) 61st: Rank in 2017.
tip: 💡 India's Innovation Leap: India rose from 81st in 2015 to 39th in 2024! WIPO publishes GII; Switzerland ranks #1 globally.

subject: Current Events
q: Who among the following was conferred the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 in recognition of his socialist leadership and defense of backward classes?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Karpoori Thakur • (A) Ram Manohar Lohia: Socialist icon, but not awarded Bharat Ratna in 2024.
• (B) Karpoori Thakur: Correct! Former Chief Minister of Bihar known as 'Jan Nayak', champion of backward classes and OBC reservation formula.
• (C) Jayaprakash Narayan: Awarded Bharat Ratna in 1999.
• (D) Morarji Desai: Awarded in 1991.
tip: 💡 2024 Bharat Ratna Recipients (5 stalwarts): Karpoori Thakur, P.V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh, M.S. Swaminathan, and L.K. Advani!

subject: Current Events
q: Which state in India became the first to pass a legislation implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in 2024?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Uttarakhand • (A) Goa: Retained Portuguese Civil Code 1867, but did not pass post-independence UCC legislation.
• (B) Uttarakhand: Correct! Passed the Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2024 in February 2024, becoming the first State in post-independence India to enact a comprehensive UCC.
• (C) Gujarat: Constituted a committee, but Uttarakhand passed it first.
• (D) Assam: Repealed Muslim Marriage Act, but hasn't enacted full UCC.
tip: 💡 Constitutional Co-relation: Article 44 (DPSP) directs the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code. Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to legislate it!

subject: Current Events
q: The historic Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was signed in 1971 in the city of Ramsar located in which country?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Iran • (A) Iraq: Tigris-Euphrates wetlands.
• (B) Iran: Correct! Adopted in 1971 in the Iranian resort city of Ramsar on the Caspian Sea shore. Entered into force in 1975.
• (C) Egypt: Nile delta wetlands.
• (D) Turkey: Lake Van region.
tip: 💡 Wetlands Landmark: Ramsar is in IRAN. World Wetlands Day is celebrated on February 2. India has over 80+ Ramsar sites!

subject: Current Events
q: The Paris 2024 Summer Olympic Games featured the Olympic debut of which of the following sports?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Breaking (Breakdancing) • (A) Karate: Debuted at Tokyo 2020, but was dropped for Paris 2024.
• (B) Breaking (Breakdancing): Correct! Made its official Olympic debut at Place de la Concorde during Paris 2024.
• (C) Baseball: Excluded from Paris 2024, returns in LA 2028.
• (D) Cricket: Approved for inclusion at Los Angeles 2028 (T20 format).
tip: 💡 Olympic Roster Shift: Breaking debuted in Paris 2024! Cricket (T20), Baseball/Softball, Flag Football, and Lacrosse enter in Los Angeles 2028!

subject: Current Events
q: The 'Cyber Surakshit Bharat' initiative was launched by the Government of India in collaboration with industry partners to:
opts: Strengthen cybersecurity hygiene and resilience across government departments
Replace physical policing with automated drones
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Strengthen cybersecurity hygiene and resilience across government departments • (A) Regulate cryptocurrency: Handled under PMLA / FIU guidelines.
• (B) Strengthen cybersecurity resilience: Correct! Launched by MeitY and National e-Governance Division (NeGD) in public-private partnership to train Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs).
• (C) Drone policing: Autonomous surveillance.
• (D) Private chat monitoring: Restricted under surveillance jurisprudence.
tip: 💡 Police Tech Insight: Cyber Surakshit Bharat trains frontline government IT officers and CISOs on proactive threat detection, SOC operations, and incident response!

subject: Current Events
q: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is situated at:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) The Hague, Netherlands • (A) Geneva, Switzerland: Headquarters of WHO, ILO, UNHCR, WTO.
• (B) The Hague, Netherlands: Correct! The International Court of Justice (ICJ) sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague.
• (C) Vienna, Austria: Headquarters of IAEA, UNODC, OPEC.
• (D) New York, USA: UN General Assembly and Security Council.
tip: 💡 The Lone Outlier: Of the 6 principal organs of the United Nations, ICJ is the ONLY one located outside New York!

subject: Current Events
q: What is the theme of India's National Police Commemoration Day observed annually on October 21st?
opts: Remembering the brave CRPF personnel who sacrificed their lives at Hot Springs, Ladakh in 1959
Commemorating the establishment of IPS in 1948
Celebrating the integration of princely police
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Remembering the brave CRPF personnel who sacrificed their lives at Hot Springs, Ladakh in 1959 • (A) Hot Springs, Ladakh (Oct 21, 1959): Correct! Honors 10 CRPF patrolmen martyred fighting heavily armed Chinese PLA troops at Hot Springs.
• (B) Establishment of IPS in 1948: Celebrated as Civil Services Day on April 21.
• (C) Princely police integration.
• (D) Kargil War commemoration: Celebrated on July 26 (Kargil Vijay Diwas).
tip: 💡 Police SI Must-Know: Police Commemoration Day is observed across all state forces and CAPFs on OCTOBER 21 every year in memory of the 1959 Hot Springs martyrs!

subject: Current Events
q: The European Union's landmark legislation regulating the ethical usage and safety standards of Artificial Intelligence is known as:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) European AI Act • (A) Digital Services Act: Regulates content moderation and online platforms.
• (B) European AI Act: Correct! Landmark 2024 horizontal regulation banning unacceptable risk AI (social scoring, biometric categorisation) and setting strict compliance for high-risk AI.
• (C) General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR): EU personal data privacy law (2018).
• (D) Cyber Resilience Protocol.
tip: 💡 Global Tech Precedent: The EU AI Act is the world's FIRST comprehensive binding law on Artificial Intelligence, categorizing AI applications by risk levels!

subject: Current Events
q: Which Indian port became the first transshipment hub in the country to receive large motherships, located in Kerala?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Vizhinjam International Seaport • (A) Cochin Port: Home to Vallarpadam ICTT.
• (B) Vizhinjam International Seaport: Correct! Located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, it has a natural 20-meter draft capable of berthing ultra-large container vessels (ULCVs).
• (C) Beypore Port: Minor port in Kozhikode.
• (D) Kollam Port: Intermediate coastal port.
