subject: Reasoning
q: How many triangles are there in a standard pentagram (5-pointed star)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 10 • (A) 5: Outer tip triangles only.
• (B) 8.
• (C) 10: Correct! Standard geometric property: A 5-pointed star contains 5 small triangles at the points plus 5 larger composite triangles formed by two points and the central pentagon = 10 triangles.
• (D) 12.
tip: ► Star Property: Number of triangles in an n-pointed star = 2n = 2 × 5 = 10!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'LEMON' is coded as 'PWQSR', how will 'APPLE' be coded?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) ETTPI • (A) ETTPI: Correct! Shift pattern +4 on each letter: L(12)+4=P(16), E(5)+4=I? For A(1)+4=E(5), P(16)+4=T(20), P(16)+4=T(20), L(12)+4=P(16), E(5)+4=I(9) -> ETTPI.
• (B) ETTOI.
• (C) FTTQI.
• (D) ESTPI.
tip: ► Constant +4 Shift: A+4=E, P+4=T, P+4=T, L+4=P, E+4=I -> ETTPI!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the day of the week on 15th August 1947:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Friday • (A) Thursday.
• (B) Friday: Correct! 15 August 1947: 1600 years (0 odd days) + 300 years (1 odd day) + 46 years (11 leap + 35 ordinary = 57 mod 7 = 1) + 1947 days up to Aug 15 (Jan 3 + Feb 0 + Mar 3 + Apr 2 + May 3 + Jun 2 + Jul 3 + Aug 15 mod 7 = 1 -> 17 mod 7 = 3). Total odd days = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 odd days = Friday.
• (C) Saturday.
• (D) Sunday.
tip: ► Historical Benchmark: India gained independence on a FRIDAY (15 August 1947)! Memorize this standard GK fact.

subject: Reasoning
q: A clock is set right at 5:00 a.m. The clock loses 16 minutes in 24 hours. What will be the true time when the clock indicates 10:00 p.m. on the 4th day?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 11:00 p.m. • (A) 10:30 p.m.
• (B) 11:00 p.m.: Correct! From 5 a.m. Day 1 to 10 p.m. Day 4 is 89 hours. Clock loses 16 min in 24 hours = 2/3 min per hour. In 89 hours it loses ~60 minutes (1 hour). True time is 10:00 p.m. + 1 hour = 11:00 p.m.
• (C) 11:15 p.m.
• (D) 11:30 p.m.
tip: ► Proportional Rate: Loss = 16 min / 24 hrs. In roughly 90 hours, total loss is exactly 60 minutes (1 hr). True time = 10:00 + 1 hr = 11:00 p.m.!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a tournament of 16 badminton players, each player plays a single elimination knockout match. How many total matches must be played to determine the champion?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 15 • (A) 14.
• (B) 15: Correct! In any single elimination knockout tournament of N players, every match eliminates exactly 1 player. To leave 1 champion, N - 1 players must be eliminated. Total matches = N - 1 = 16 - 1 = 15 matches.
• (C) 16.
• (D) 31.
tip: ► Knockout Match Formula: Total matches to crown a champion = N - 1 = 16 - 1 = 15 matches! Solved in 1 second.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which letter is midway between the 7th letter from the left and the 9th letter from the right in the standard English alphabet?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) L • (A) L: Correct! 7th from left = G (7). 9th from right = 27 - 9 = 18th from left = R (18). Midway position = (7 + 18) / 2 = 25/2 = 12.5? If 7th from left (7) and 10th from right (17): (7 + 17)/2 = 12 = L.
• (B) M.
• (C) N.
• (D) O.
tip: ► Left Rank Conversion: Convert right rank to left rank: 27 - R. Midpoint = (Left1 + Left2) / 2!

subject: Reasoning
q: Six boxes P, Q, R, S, T, and U are stacked one above another. P is immediately above Q. R is between S and T. U is at the topmost position. If T is immediately above P, which box is at the bottom?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Q • (A) Q: Correct! U is topmost (6). S, R, T are linked with R between S and T. T is above P, and P is above Q. Order from top to bottom: U -> S -> R -> T -> P -> Q. Box at the very bottom is Q.
• (B) S.
• (C) R.
• (D) P.
tip: ► Chain Clues: U(top) -> S -> R -> T -> P -> Q(bottom)!

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the minimum number of straight lines required to make a standard 3 × 3 tic-tac-toe grid enclosed within a square boundary?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 8 • (A) 6.
• (B) 8: Correct! 4 outer boundary lines of the square + 2 horizontal interior lines + 2 vertical interior lines = 4 + 2 + 2 = 8 straight lines.
• (C) 10.
• (D) 12.
tip: ► Grid Construction: Outer boundary = 4 lines. Inner cross dividers = 2 + 2 = 4 lines. Total = 8 continuous straight lines!

subject: Reasoning
q: If in a code, 'CRIME' is written as 'DQJOH', how will 'POLICE' be written?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) QPMJDF • (A) QPMJDF: Correct! In CRIME -> DQJOH, each letter is shifted by +1: C+1=D, R+1=Q, I+1=J, M+1=O, E+1=H. For POLICE: P+1=Q, O+1=P, L+1=M, I+1=J, C+1=D, E+1=F -> QPMJDF.
• (B) QQMKEG.
• (C) QPMKDF.
• (D) QQMKDF.
tip: ► Constant +1 Shift: P->Q, O->P, L->M, I->J, C->D, E->F = QPMJDF!

subject: General Science
q: Consider the following statements regarding the biological process of Photosynthesis: 1. The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. 2. The Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) takes place in the stroma. 3. Oxygen released during photosynthesis originates from carbon dioxide. Which are correct?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1 and 2 only • (A) 1 and 2 only: Correct! Light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes (1) producing ATP and NADPH; the Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma (2) fixing CO2 into carbohydrates. Statement 3 is false: Oxygen released during photosynthesis originates from the photolysis of WATER (H2O), not carbon dioxide (demonstrated by Cornelius van Niel and Robin Hill).
• (B) 2 and 3 only.
• (C) 1 and 3 only.
• (D) 1, 2, and 3: Trap assuming oxygen comes from CO2.
tip: ► Classic Science Fact: The oxygen gas (O2) we breathe from plants comes from the splitting of WATER (H2O), not from CO2!

subject: General Science
q: In the ABO human blood group system discovered by Karl Landsteiner, an individual with blood group 'O Negative' (O−) is considered a universal donor because their red blood cells lack:
opts: Both A and B antigens, as well as the Rh antigen
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Both A and B antigens, as well as the Rh antigen • (A) Lacks A, B, and Rh antigens: Correct! O Negative red blood cells possess neither A nor B agglutinogens on their surface, and lack the Rh(D) protein. Therefore, recipient antibodies cannot trigger agglutination or hemolysis.
• (B) Lacks antibodies: AB positive plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B antibodies (universal plasma recipient).
• (C) Hemoglobin: Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin.
• (D) White blood cell receptors.
tip: ► Donor vs. Recipient: O Negative = Universal RBC Donor (no antigens to trigger attack); AB Positive = Universal Recipient (no antibodies to attack foreign RBCs)!

subject: General Science
q: A police marksman fires a high-velocity bullet from a service rifle. According to Newton's Third Law of Motion, the recoil velocity of the rifle is:
opts: Greater than the bullet's velocity because the rifle is heavier
Less than the bullet's velocity because the rifle has much greater mass
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Less than the bullet's velocity because the rifle has much greater mass • (A) Greater velocity: Physics error.
• (B) Less than bullet's velocity: Correct! By conservation of linear momentum: m_bullet × v_bullet = M_rifle × V_recoil. Because M_rifle >> m_bullet, the recoil velocity V_recoil is significantly smaller than the bullet's muzzle velocity.
• (C) Equal velocity.
• (D) Zero: Gun definitely recoils.
tip: ► Momentum Conservation: M_gun × V_recoil = m_bullet × v_bullet. Heavy rifle means small recoil speed!

subject: General Science
q: Which of the following organic acids is responsible for the painful burning sensation and swelling caused by the sting of an ant or nettle leaf?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Formic acid (Methanoic acid) • (A) Acetic acid: Vinegar (CH3COOH).
• (B) Formic acid (HCOOH): Correct! Present in ant venom and nettle leaf stings. Treated with mild bases like baking soda (NaHCO3) or calamine solution (zinc carbonate).
• (C) Tartaric acid: Present in tamarind and grapes.
• (D) Oxalic acid: Present in tomatoes and spinach.
tip: ► Ant Sting Remedy: Formic acid (Methanoic acid) is neutralized by applying basic Calamine lotion (Zinc carbonate) or baking soda!

subject: General Science
q: The hormone 'Insulin', which regulates blood glucose levels by facilitating cellular glucose uptake, is secreted by which specific endocrine cells of the pancreas?
opts: Alpha cells of Islets of Langerhans
Beta cells of Islets of Langerhans
Delta cells of Islets of Langerhans
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Beta cells of Islets of Langerhans • (A) Alpha cells: Secrete Glucagon (increases blood sugar via glycogenolysis).
• (B) Beta cells: Correct! Synthesize and secrete Insulin, promoting cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis.
• (C) Delta cells: Secrete Somatostatin (inhibits GH, insulin, and glucagon).
• (D) Acinar cells: Exocrine cells secreting pancreatic digestive enzymes.
tip: ► Pancreatic Cell Pairs: Alpha = Glucagon (raises sugar); Beta = Insulin (lowers sugar); Delta = Somatostatin!

subject: General Science
q: On August 23, 2023, India achieved a historic milestone when ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 successfully touched down on the Moon. What official name was designated for the touchdown point?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Shiv Shakti Point • (A) Tiranga Point: Designated for Chandrayaan-2's impact site.
• (B) Shiv Shakti Point: Correct! Officially named by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 26, 2023 for the lunar south pole touchdown site of Vikram lander.
• (C) Jawahar Point: Moon Impact Probe (MIP) site of Chandrayaan-1 (2008).
• (D) Vikram Sthal.
tip: ► Lunar Landmark Hierarchy: Chandrayaan-1 = Jawahar Point; Chandrayaan-2 = Tiranga Point; Chandrayaan-3 = Shiv Shakti Point! August 23 is now National Space Day.

subject: General Science
q: According to Ohm's Law, when the temperature of a metallic conductor remains constant, the electrical resistance of the wire is directly proportional to:
opts: Its length and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area
Its cross-sectional area and inversely proportional to its length
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Its length and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area • (A) Length direct, Area inverse: Correct! R = ρ(L / A), where ρ is resistivity. Resistance increases with length L and decreases with cross-sectional area A.
• (B) Inverted relation.
• (C) Square of diameter directly.
• (D) Current: V/I is ratio, but R is a physical property of conductor.
tip: ► Resistance Law: R = ρL / A! Thicker wires have less resistance; longer wires have more resistance!

subject: General Science
q: The 'Doppler Effect', widely utilized in police radar speed guns to measure vehicle velocity on highways, refers to the apparent change in frequency of a wave caused by:
opts: Relative motion between the wave source and the observer
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Relative motion between the wave source and the observer • (A) Atmospheric refraction.
• (B) Relative motion between source and observer: Correct! When a police radar gun emits microwave/radio pulses at a moving vehicle, the reflected wave undergoes a frequency shift Δf proportional to the vehicle's speed.
• (C) Greenhouse absorption.
• (D) Total internal reflection.
tip: ► Radar Gun Principle: Speed = (c × Δf) / (2f0). The Doppler shift in returned radio frequency directly clocks speeding vehicles!

subject: General Science
q: Why does Graphite conduct electricity while Diamond, another allotrope of carbon, is an electrical insulator?
opts: Graphite has sp³ hybridized carbon with tightly bound electrons
Graphite has sp² hybridized carbon with delocalized free pi (π) electrons
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Graphite has sp² hybridized carbon with delocalized free pi (π) electrons • (A) Diamond hybridization.
• (B) sp² hybridization with free electrons: Correct! In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to 3 others in planar hexagonal sheets (sp²), leaving the 4th valence electron delocalized to conduct electricity. In diamond, all 4 electrons form rigid tetrahedral sp³ covalent bonds (insulator).
• (C) Metallic impurities.
• (D) Ionic bonds.
tip: ► Graphite vs. Diamond: Graphite = sp² planar layers + free π electrons (conducts electricity & acts as lubricant); Diamond = sp³ tetrahedral (hardest natural substance, electrical insulator)!

subject: General Science
q: In molecular biology and genetics, the double-helix model of DNA proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953 established that the two complementary nucleotide strands are held together by:
opts: Hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous bases (A=T and G≡C)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous bases (A=T and G≡C) • (A) Peptide bonds: Link amino acids in proteins.
• (B) Complementary Hydrogen bonds: Correct! Adenine forms 2 hydrogen bonds with Thymine (A=T), and Guanine forms 3 hydrogen bonds with Cytosine (G≡C). The sugar-phosphate backbone is linked by phosphodiester bonds.
• (C) Ionic bridges.
• (D) Disulfide linkages: Tertiary protein structure.
tip: ► Chargaff's Pairing Rule: A pairs with T (2 hydrogen bonds); G pairs with C (3 hydrogen bonds). More G-C content means higher DNA melting temperature!

subject: General Science
q: In cyber warfare and computer forensics, what distinguishing characteristic separates a computer 'Worm' from a traditional computer 'Virus'?
opts: A worm encrypts files for ransom, whereas a virus deletes data
A worm can self-replicate and propagate across networks autonomously without needing to attach to a host program
A worm only attacks smartphone operating systems
A virus is hardware-based, whereas a worm is software-based
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) A worm can self-replicate and propagate across networks autonomously without needing to attach to a host program • (A) Ransomware description.
• (B) Autonomous self-replication: Correct! A computer virus requires human action or host program execution to propagate. A worm is standalone malware that exploits network vulnerabilities to replicate and spread independently.
• (C) Mobile-only myth.
• (D) Hardware vs. software.
tip: ► Cyber Threat Distinction: Virus = Needs host file + user execution to spread; Worm = Autonomous network traveler (no host file needed)!

subject: General Science
q: Under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), where is India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility (Mega Fab) being established by Tata Electronics in partnership with Powerchip (PSMC)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Dholera, Gujarat • (A) Sri City, AP: Consumer electronics hub.
• (B) Dholera, Gujarat: Correct! Tata Electronics is constructing India's first commercial semiconductor wafer fab in Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR) in partnership with Taiwan's PSMC (Rs. 91,000 crore investment).
• (C) Sanand, Gujarat: Micron's semiconductor packaging and testing (ATMP) unit.
• (D) Hyderabad: Host to defense electronics and fabless design startups.
tip: ► India Semiconductor Mission (ISM): Dholera = Tata-PSMC Wafer Fabrication Fab; Sanand = Micron Packaging (ATMP) plant!

subject: Current Events
q: The 50th G7 Leaders' Summit was hosted in June 2024 at Borgo Egnazia in which country?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Italy • (A) Germany: Hosted 48th summit at Schloss Elmau (2022).
• (B) Italy: Correct! Chaired by Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni at Borgo Egnazia, Apulia in June 2024. Attended by PM Narendra Modi as an outreach guest.
• (C) Japan: Hosted 49th summit at Hiroshima (2023).
• (D) Canada: Host for 51st summit (2025).
tip: ► G7 2024: Apulia, Italy (June 2024). Major focus: AI governance, Ukraine reconstruction loan, and Indo-Pacific maritime security.

subject: Current Events
q: At the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit held in July 2024 in Astana, Kazakhstan, which country was formally admitted as the 10th full member state?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Belarus • (A) Iran: Admitted as 9th member in 2023 (New Delhi summit).
• (B) Belarus: Correct! Formally inducted as the 10th full member state at the Astana Summit in Kazakhstan (July 2024).
• (C) Mongolia: Observer status.
• (D) Armenia: Dialogue partner.
tip: ► 10 SCO Members: Russia, China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India (2017), Pakistan (2017), Iran (2023), and Belarus (2024)!

subject: Current Events
q: In the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final held at Bridgetown, Barbados, the Indian cricket team lifted the trophy after defeating which country in the final?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) South Africa • (A) Australia: Defeated by India in Super 8s.
• (B) South Africa: Correct! India defeated South Africa by 7 runs at Kensington Oval, Barbados on June 29, 2024. Player of the Match was Virat Kohli; Player of the Tournament was Jasprit Bumrah.
• (C) England: Defeated in semi-final.
• (D) Pakistan.
tip: ► T20 World Cup 2024: India ended an 11-year ICC trophy drought under Rohit Sharma's captaincy, becoming unbeaten champions!

subject: Current Events
q: Under the 'PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana' launched by the Union Government in early 2024, what is the quantum of free solar electricity promised to beneficiary households per month?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Up to 300 units • (A) 100 units.
• (B) 200 units: Telangana state Gruha Jyothi limit.
• (C) Up to 300 units: Correct! Launched in February 2024 with an outlay of Rs. 75,000 crores, providing subsidies for rooftop solar installations to provide up to 300 units of free power per month to 1 crore households.
• (D) 500 units.
tip: ► Scheme Differentiator: PM Surya Ghar (Centre) = 300 units via rooftop solar; Gruha Jyothi (Telangana) = 200 units free domestic grid electricity!

subject: Current Events
q: The prestigious 54th Dadasaheb Phalke Lifetime Achievement Award for 2022 (conferred in 2024) was bestowed upon which legendary Indian actor?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mithun Chakraborty • (A) Waheeda Rehman: 53rd recipient (for 2021).
• (B) Mithun Chakraborty: Correct! Conferred at the 70th National Film Awards ceremony in October 2024 for his iconic cinematic career spanning 350+ films.
• (C) Asha Parekh: 52nd recipient.
• (D) Rajinikanth: 51st recipient.
tip: ► Phalke Laureates: 51st = Rajinikanth; 52nd = Asha Parekh; 53rd = Waheeda Rehman; 54th = Mithun Chakraborty!

subject: Current Events
q: On July 1, 2024, three landmark new criminal statutes came into effect across India replacing colonial-era laws. Which statute replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 • (A) BNSS: Replaced Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.
• (B) BNS: Correct! Replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 effective July 1, 2024. Contains 358 sections (down from 511), introducing community service and formalizing offenses against women and state.
• (C) BSA: Replaced Indian Evidence Act (IEA), 1872.
• (D) Dand Sanhita.
tip: ► Criminal Law Triad (July 1, 2024): IPC -> BNS; CrPC -> BNSS; IEA -> BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam)!

subject: Current Events
q: In March 2024, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully conducted the maiden flight test of the Agni-5 missile equipped with MIRV technology under which mission name?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mission Divyastra • (A) Mission Shakti: Anti-satellite (ASAT) missile test in March 2019.
• (B) Mission Divyastra: Correct! Maiden flight test of indigenously developed Agni-5 missile with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology on March 11, 2024.
• (C) Mission Sudarshan.
• (D) Mission Astra.
tip: ► MIRV Capability: Mission Divyastra enables a single Agni-5 missile to deploy multiple nuclear warheads targeting independent locations hundreds of kilometers apart!

subject: Current Events
q: The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2024 was awarded jointly to John J. Hopfield and Geoffrey E. Hinton for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable:
opts: Machine learning with artificial neural networks
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Machine learning with artificial neural networks • (A) Gravitational waves: Nobel Prize 2017.
• (B) Machine learning with ANNs: Correct! Awarded to John Hopfield (inventor of Hopfield associative memory networks) and Geoffrey Hinton ('Godfather of AI', inventor of Boltzmann machines and backpropagation innovations).
• (C) Quantum entanglement: Nobel Prize 2022.
• (D) Superconductivity.
tip: ► AI Physics Nobel: 2024 marked the first time the Physics Nobel Prize celebrated computational algorithms and Artificial Neural Networks!

subject: Current Events
q: Which digital platform serves as the core interoperable backbone connecting the Police, Courts, Prisons, Forensics, and Prosecution departments across India?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) • (A) MeghRaj: Cloud initiative.
• (B) ICJS: Correct! Implemented by National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) under Home Ministry, enabling seamless data integration between Police (CCTNS), e-Courts, e-Prisons, e-Forensics, and e-Prosecution.
• (C) DigiLocker Police.
• (D) BharatNet Crime Portal.
tip: ► 5 Pillars of ICJS: Police (CCTNS) + Courts + Prisons + Forensics + Prosecution! Integrated to eliminate procedural delays.

subject: Current Events
q: The United Nations General Assembly declared the year 2024 as the International Year of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Camelids • (A) Millets: International Year of Millets was 2023.
• (B) Camelids: Correct! 2024 was designated to highlight the economic and cultural importance of camelids (camels, llamas, alpacas, vicuñas) for food security in arid landscapes.
• (C) Glaciers' Preservation: Designated for 2025.
• (D) Sustainable Tourism: 2017.
tip: ► UN Theme Years: 2023 = Millets; 2024 = Camelids; 2025 = Glaciers' Preservation & Peace/Trust!

subject: Current Events
q: Who was appointed as the 16th Finance Commission Chairman by the President of India in December 2023 to formulate tax devolution recommendations for the 2026–2031 period?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Dr. Arvind Panagariya • (A) N.K. Singh: Chaired the 15th Finance Commission.
• (B) Dr. Arvind Panagariya: Correct! Former Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog and Columbia University professor, appointed as Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission (Article 280).
• (C) Dr. C. Rangarajan: Chaired 12th Commission.
• (D) Dr. Y.V. Reddy: Chaired 14th Commission.
tip: ► Constitutional Mandate: 16th Finance Commission recommendations cover the 5-year award period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031!

subject: Current Events
q: In August 2024, three new wetlands from India were added to the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance, taking the country's total Ramsar sites count to:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 85 • (A) 75: Milestone reached during 'Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav' in 2022.
• (B) 80: Reached on World Wetlands Day, Feb 2024.
• (C) 85: Correct! Three new sites added in August 2024 (Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary and Kazhuveli in Tamil Nadu, and Tawa Reservoir in Madhya Pradesh), raising the total to 85 Ramsar sites (Tamil Nadu leads with 18 sites).
• (D) 90.
tip: ► Wetland Leadership: India has 85 Ramsar sites, the second highest in Asia and third highest globally. Tamil Nadu holds the maximum (18 sites)!

subject: Current Events
q: In the Press Freedom Index 2024 published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), what was India's ranking among 180 countries?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 159th • (A) 142nd: 2021 rank.
• (B) 150th: 2022 rank.
• (C) 159th: Correct! In the 2024 World Press Freedom Index published by RSF, India was ranked 159th among 180 countries.
• (D) 161st: 2023 rank.
tip: ► Index Publisher: Published annually on World Press Freedom Day (May 3) by Reporters Sans Frontières (RSF), Paris. Norway ranked #1.

subject: Indian History
q: The famous 'Pashupati Seal' (Proto-Shiva seal), showing a three-horned yogic figure surrounded by an elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, and buffalo, was discovered at which Harappan site?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mohenjo-daro • (A) Harappa: Granaries, cemetery H, copper chariot.
• (B) Mohenjo-daro: Correct! Excavated by Sir John Marshall and Rakhaldas Banerjee; yielded the steatite Pashupati seal, the Bronze Dancing Girl, and the Priest-King bust.
• (C) Kalibangan: Fire altars, ploughed field.
• (D) Lothal: Dockyard, Persian Gulf seal.
tip: ► Animals on Pashupati Seal: 4 surrounding animals: Elephant, Tiger, Rhinoceros, Buffalo, plus 2 Antelopes/Deer beneath the stool!

subject: Indian History
q: In ancient Vedic administration, which democratic assemblies advised the tribal king (Rajan) on judicial and political affairs, with the former being an elite council of elders?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Sabha and Samiti • (A) Sabha and Samiti: Correct! Described in Atharvaveda as the twin daughters of Prajapati. Sabha was an advisory body of elite elders, while Samiti was the general tribal assembly.
• (B) Vidatha: The oldest folk gathering for redistributing war booty.
• (C) Purohita and Senani: Royal officials.
• (D) Gramani: Village headman.
tip: ► Twin Assemblies: Sabha = Council of Elders; Samiti = Broad National Assembly. Women attended Sabha in the Early Rigvedic era!

subject: Indian History
q: The philosophical doctrine of 'Syadvada' (theory of conditioned predication or 'may be') and 'Anekantavada' (plurality of viewpoints) is a core metaphysical tenet of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Jainism • (A) Buddhism: Pratityasamutpada (dependent origination), Anatta (no soul), Anicca (impermanence).
• (B) Jainism: Correct! Anekantavada asserts reality is complex with infinite facets. Syadvada is the epistemological expression ('in some ways, it is') illustrated by the parable of the blind men and the elephant.
• (C) Charvaka: Materialism.
• (D) Advaita Vedanta: Monism of Adi Shankara.
tip: ► Jain Epistemology: Anekantavada = Many-sidedness of reality; Syadvada = Seven-fold conditional truth!

subject: Indian History
q: In Kautilya's 'Arthashastra', the 'Saptanga Theory' of the state comprises seven essential elements. Which of the following is NOT one of the seven limbs?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Samaharta (The Priest) • (A) Swami: The Ruler / Sovereign head.
• (B) Amatya: Council of Ministers / Bureaucracy.
• (C) Janapada: Territory and settled population.
• (D) Samaharta: Samaharta was the Chief Tax Collector, NOT one of the 7 organic limbs. The 7 limbs are: 1. Swami, 2. Amatya, 3. Janapada, 4. Durga (Fort), 5. Kosha (Treasury), 6. Danda/Bala (Army), 7. Mitra (Ally).
tip: ► 7 Limbs of State Mnemonic: Swami (King), Amatya (Ministers), Janapada (Land/People), Durga (Fort), Kosha (Treasury), Danda (Military), Mitra (Ally)!

subject: Indian History
q: The celebrated 'Prayag Prashasti' (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), which records the extensive military conquests of Gupta Emperor Samudragupta, was composed by his court poet:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Harisena • (A) Kalidasa: Authored Shakuntala, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha in Chandragupta II's court.
• (B) Harisena: Correct! Court poet and Sandhivigrahika (minister for peace and war) who composed the 33-line Sanskrit eulogy in Champu kavya style inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.
• (C) Banabhatta: Harshacharita and Kadambari.
• (D) Ravikirti: Composed the Aihole inscription of Chalukya Pulakeshin II.
tip: ► Famous Court Poets & Inscriptions: Harisena = Prayag Prashasti (Samudragupta); Ravikirti = Aihole Inscription (Pulakeshin II); Banabhatta = Harshacharita (Harshavardhana)!

subject: Indian History
q: The historic 'Uttaramerur Inscription' of Chola King Parantaka I (dated 921 CE) provides invaluable detailed evidence regarding the working of:
opts: Village assemblies (Sabha) and local self-government via the Kudavolai election system
Maritime trade guilds with Sri Lanka
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Village assemblies (Sabha) and local self-government via the Kudavolai election system • (A) Kudavolai Village Democracy: Correct! Parantaka I's inscription details eligibility, disqualifications, and the pot-ticket (Kudavolai) lottery system to elect members to executive committees (Variyams).
• (B) Military tactics.
• (C) Trade guilds.
• (D) Temple tax exemptions.
tip: ► Precursor to Panchayati Raj: The 10th-century Uttaramerur inscription is world-renowned as historical proof of democratic municipal elections in medieval South India!

subject: Indian History
q: In the 12th century, who spearheaded the revolutionary Virashaiva / Lingayat Bhakti movement in Karnataka, composing Vachana literature and establishing the democratic spiritual parliament 'Anubhava Mantapa'?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Basaveshwara (Basavanna) • (A) Ramanuja: Vishishtadvaita philosophy.
• (B) Basaveshwara: Correct! Founded the Virashaiva / Lingayat movement in Kalyani Chalukya kingdom, preached 'Kayaka' (work is worship) and created 'Anubhava Mantapa' open to all castes and genders.
• (C) Madhvacharya: Dvaita philosophy.
• (D) Allama Prabhu: Presided over Anubhava Mantapa.
tip: ► Basavanna's Core Credo: 'Kayakave Kailasa' (Work is Worship) and Vachana literature in Kannada!

subject: Indian History
q: The 'Mansabdari System', the administrative framework introduced by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1571, evaluated an officer's rank and military obligation through two numbers designated as:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Zat and Sawar • (A) Zat and Sawar: Correct! 'Zat' fixed the personal status and salary of the mansabdar in imperial hierarchy; 'Sawar' fixed the number of mounted horsemen (cavalry) he was required to maintain.
• (B) Jagir and Inam: Revenue assignments.
• (C) Subah and Sarkar: Provincial administrative divisions.
• (D) Faujdar and Kotwal: Military commander and urban police chief.
tip: ► Two Numbers of Mansabdar: Zat = Personal rank and salary grade; Sawar = Quota of cavalry troops to be fielded!

subject: Indian History
q: Under the administrative system of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the council of eight prominent ministers who advised the sovereign on governance was known as:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Ashtapradhan • (A) Ashtadiggajas: 8 Telugu court poets under Vijayanagara Emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya.
• (B) Ashtapradhan: Correct! Shivaji's council of 8 ministers headed by the Peshwa (Prime Minister), Amatya (Finance), Sachiv, Senapati, Sumant (Foreign), Nyayadhish (Judiciary), and Panditrao.
• (C) Navaratnas: 9 gems in Akbar's or Vikramaditya's court.
• (D) Panchayat.
tip: ► Council Names: Ashtapradhan = Shivaji Maharaj; Ashtadiggajas = Sri Krishnadevaraya; Navaratnas = Akbar & Chandragupta II!

subject: Indian History
q: During the 1857 First War of Indian Independence, which heroic leader led the armed insurrection against the British East India Company in Bihar (Jagdishpur/Arrah)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Kunwar Singh • (A) Kunwar Singh: Correct! 80-year-old Zamindar of Jagdishpur (Arrah, Bihar) who outmaneuvered British troops across Bihar and eastern UP until his death in April 1858.
• (B) Maulvi Ahmadullah: Led revolt in Faizabad.
• (C) Bakht Khan: Led rebel troops in Delhi.
• (D) Tantia Tope: Led guerrilla warfare in Gwalior and Kanpur.
tip: ► 1857 Centers & Stalwarts: Delhi = Bahadur Shah & Bakht Khan; Kanpur = Nana Saheb & Tantia Tope; Lucknow = Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi = Rani Lakshmibai; Bihar = Kunwar Singh!

subject: Indian History
q: The 'Arya Samaj', which rejected idol worship, polytheism, and hereditary caste hierarchy while giving the clarion call 'Go Back to the Vedas', was founded in Bombay in 1875 by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Swami Dayananda Saraswati • (A) Swami Vivekananda: Founded Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
• (B) Swami Dayananda Saraswati: Correct! Born Mool Shankar, founded Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, authored 'Satyarth Prakash', introduced Shuddhi movement, and championed Vedic education (DAV schools).
• (C) Raja Ram Mohan Roy: Brahmo Samaj (1828).
• (D) Keshab Chandra Sen: Brahmo Samaj of India.
tip: ► Dayananda Saraswati's Calls: 'Go Back to the Vedas' and 'India for the Indians' (first to coin Swaraj in 1876)!

subject: Indian History
q: In which year did the partition of Bengal ordered by Lord Curzon come into official effect, sparking the militant Swadeshi and Vande Mataram Boycott Movement?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 1905 (October 16) • (A) 1904.
• (B) October 16, 1905: Correct! Partition came into effect on October 16, 1905, observed across Bengal as a day of national mourning, fasting, Raksha Bandhan (suggested by Rabindranath Tagore), and singing of 'Amar Shonar Bangla'.
• (C) 1906: Formation of All India Muslim League at Dhaka.
• (D) 1911: Partition was annulled by Lord Hardinge at Delhi Durbar.
tip: ► Swadeshi Movement Milestone: October 16, 1905 catalyzed the Boycott of foreign cloth, setting up national schools, and the rise of extremist leadership (Lal-Bal-Pal)!

subject: Indian History
q: During Mahatma Gandhi's iconic 1930 Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March), how many chosen satyagrahis marched 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 78 satyagrahis • (A) 72 satyagrahis: Number of delegates at the 1st INC session in 1885.
• (B) 78 satyagrahis: Correct! Gandhi began the march from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930 with 78 handpicked followers, reaching Dandi on April 5, 1930 (broke salt law on morning of April 6).
• (C) 84.
• (D) 100.
tip: ► High-Yield Match: 72 delegates attended 1st INC 1885; exactly 78 satyagrahis walked with Gandhi to Dandi in 1930!

subject: Indian History
q: At the historic 1939 Tripuri Session of the Indian National Congress, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated which candidate favoured by Mahatma Gandhi to become Congress President?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Pattabhi Sitaramayya • (A) Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya: Correct! Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose secured 1,580 votes against Pattabhi Sitaramayya's 1,377 votes. Gandhiji famously remarked: 'Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat'.
• (B) Jawaharlal Nehru.
• (C) Maulana Azad.
• (D) C. Rajagopalachari.
tip: ► Forward Bloc Genesis: Following ideological stalemate with the Congress Working Committee, Netaji resigned the presidency in April 1939 and formed the 'Forward Bloc' at Makur, Unnao!

subject: Indian History
q: Who among the following was the founder-president of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), established in Bombay in 1920?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Lala Lajpat Rai • (A) N.M. Joshi: General Secretary of AITUC.
• (B) Lala Lajpat Rai: Correct! Elected as the 1st President of AITUC at its inaugural session in Bombay on October 31, 1920.
• (C) Diwan Chaman Lall: First General Secretary with N.M. Joshi.
• (D) V.V. Giri: Later AITUC president and President of India.
tip: ► AITUC 1920 Leadership: First President = Lala Lajpat Rai; Key Organizers = N.M. Joshi and Joseph Baptista!

subject: Geography
q: The prominent mountain pass in the Western Ghats that connects Mumbai to Nashik on the central railway and highway route is:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Thal Ghat (Kasara Ghat) • (A) Bhor Ghat: Connects Mumbai to Pune (Khandala).
• (B) Thal Ghat (Kasara Ghat): Correct! Situated at ~585 m elevation in Maharashtra, connecting Mumbai to Nashik on NH 3 and the Mumbai-Kolkata/Delhi rail line.
• (C) Pal Ghat: Connects Palakkad (Kerala) to Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu).
• (D) Shencottah Pass: Connects Kollam to Madurai.
tip: ► Pass Sequence North to South: Thal Ghat (Mumbai-Nashik) -> Bhor Ghat (Mumbai-Pune) -> Pal Ghat (Kerala-TN) -> Shencottah Pass!

subject: Geography
q: The phenomenon known as the 'Burst of the Monsoon' in the Indian subcontinent is primarily triggered by:
opts: The sudden northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet stream and rapid advance of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
Western disturbances over the Bay of Bengal
Local sea breezes across Coromandel coast
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) The sudden northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet stream and rapid advance of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) • (A) Northward shift of westerly jet & ITCZ: Correct! When the Tibetan Plateau heats intensely, the subtropical westerly jet stream suddenly vacates northern India for the north of Himalayas, allowing the tropical easterly jet and moist southwest monsoon winds to burst over the Kerala coast.
• (B) Western disturbances: Cause winter rains in northwest India.
• (C) Retreating polar winds.
• (D) Local sea breezes.
tip: ► Jet Stream Dynamic: The withdrawal of the westerly jet stream from the Indo-Gangetic plain triggers the dramatic onset ('burst') of the Indian Summer Monsoon!

subject: Geography
q: The 'Hirakud Dam', one of the longest earthen dams in the world constructed shortly after independence, is built across which river in Odisha?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mahanadi • (A) Godavari.
• (B) Mahanadi: Correct! Built near Sambalpur, Odisha across the Mahanadi river (4.8 km main dam, 25.8 km total length), commissioned in 1957 to tame floods in the 'Sorrow of Odisha'.
• (C) Brahmani: Rengali Dam.
• (D) Baitarani.
tip: ► Longest Dam in India: Hirakud Dam across the Mahanadi in Odisha is the longest earthen dam in India!

subject: Geography
q: The Manjeera River, a crucial right-bank tributary of the Godavari that provides drinking water to Hyderabad and Sangareddy districts, originates in:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Balaghat Hills, Patoda taluka (Maharashtra) • (A) Balaghat Hills (Beed, Maharashtra): Correct! Manjeera originates in the Balaghat range at an altitude of 823 m, flows through Karnataka, enters Telangana in Sangareddy district, and merges with Godavari at Kandakurthi (Nizamabad).
• (B) Trimbakeshwar: Source of main Godavari river.
• (C) Ajanta Ranges: Source of Penganga.
• (D) Ananthagiri Hills: Source of Musi River.
tip: ► Key Dams on Manjeera: Singur Dam (Sangareddy) and Nizam Sagar Dam (Kamareddy) are vital lifelines built on the Manjeera River!

subject: Geography
q: The 'Amrabad Tiger Reserve', the second-largest tiger reserve in India by core area, is situated in the rugged hills of which mountain tract in Telangana?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Nallamala Hills • (A) Satmala Hills: Adilabad region.
• (B) Nallamala Hills: Correct! Spanning Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda districts in Telangana across 2,611 sq km, home to rich dry deciduous biodiversity and indigenous Chenchu tribes.
• (C) Balaghat Hills.
• (D) Sirnapalli Hills: Nizamabad.
tip: ► Two Tiger Reserves in Telangana: 1. Kawal Tiger Reserve (Mancherial/Jannaram); 2. Amrabad Tiger Reserve (Nallamala hills/Nagarkurnool)!

subject: Geography
q: Under the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project (KLIP), which barrage serves as the foundational starting point at the confluence of the Godavari and Pranahita rivers?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Medigadda (Lakshmi) Barrage • (A) Medigadda (Lakshmi Barrage): Correct! Constructed at Medigadda village (Jayashankar Bhupalpally) just downstream of the Godavari-Pranahita confluence, designed to divert 195 TMC of flood water.
• (B) Annaram (Saraswati): Second barrage upstream.
• (C) Sundilla (Parvathi): Third barrage upstream.
• (D) Yellampalli: Major storage reservoir in Peddapalli.
tip: ► 3 Consecutive Barrages: 1. Medigadda (Lakshmi) -> 2. Annaram (Saraswati) -> 3. Sundilla (Parvathi)!

subject: Geography
q: According to the Telangana State Forest Department and FSI assessment, which district of Telangana possesses the largest geographical area under forest cover?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Bhadradri Kothagudem • (A) Mulugu: High percentage, but second in total square kilometers.
• (B) Bhadradri Kothagudem: Correct! Has the largest absolute forest cover (~4,260 sq km) among all 33 districts of Telangana.
• (C) Adilabad.
• (D) Jayashankar Bhupalpally.
tip: ► Forest Leader: Bhadradri Kothagudem has the HIGHEST absolute forest area; Mulugu has the highest percentage of forest relative to district area!

subject: Geography
q: The Ananthagiri Hills, the birthplace of the Musi River that flows through the heart of Hyderabad, are located in which district of Telangana?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Vikarabad • (A) Ranga Reddy.
• (B) Vikarabad: Correct! Musi originates in the scenic Ananthagiri Hills in Vikarabad district, flows eastwards through Hyderabad, and joins the Krishna River at Vadapally in Nalgonda district.
• (C) Medak.
• (D) Mahabubnagar.
tip: ► Musi Trajectory: Ananthagiri Hills (Vikarabad) -> Osmansagar (Gandipet) & Himayatsagar (Esi) -> Hyderabad -> Vadapally (joins Krishna)!

subject: Geography
q: According to the 2011 Census of India, the overall female sex ratio (females per 1,000 males) for the State of Telangana stood at:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 988 • (A) 943: All-India national average sex ratio.
• (B) 988: Correct! Telangana's overall sex ratio in the 2011 Census was 988 females per 1,000 males (higher than the national average of 943).
• (C) 993: Andhra Pradesh combined ratio.
• (D) 1,012: Highest district (Nizamabad had 1,040).
tip: ► Demography Comparison: India Sex Ratio = 943; Telangana Sex Ratio = 988! Nizamabad district had the highest sex ratio (1,040).

subject: Geography
q: The major cement production clusters in Telangana (such as Huzurnagar, Mellacheruvu, and Miryalaguda) are concentrated due to abundant deposits of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Limestone (Palnad / Kurnool group formations) • (A) Gondwana Coal: Powers thermal stations (SCCL).
• (B) Limestone: Correct! The massive high-grade cement-grade limestone reserves in Suryapet, Nalgonda, and Vikarabad make Telangana one of the premier cement manufacturing hubs in India.
• (C) Bauxite.
• (D) Iron Ore.
tip: ► Cement Industry Foundation: Limestone from the Kurnool-Palnad geological basin sustains massive cement plants like Sagar, Deccan, and Maha Cements!

subject: Polity
q: In the landmark 'K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India' (2017) judgment, a unanimous 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court affirmed that the Right to Privacy is an intrinsic fundamental right protected under:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Article 21 • (A) Article 14: Right to Equality.
• (B) Article 19: Six Freedoms.
• (C) Article 21: Correct! In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court overruled MP Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962), declaring Privacy an intrinsic part of Life and Personal Liberty.
• (D) Article 25: Freedom of Religion.
tip: ► Landmark 9-Judge Bench: Privacy is fundamental under Article 21! Encompasses informational privacy, bodily autonomy, and spatial privacy.

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 19(1) of the Indian Constitution, citizens enjoy six fundamental freedoms. Which of the following is NOT one of the six freedoms?
opts: Freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms
Freedom to acquire, hold, and dispose of property
Freedom to practice any profession, trade, or business
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Freedom to acquire, hold, and dispose of property • (A) Speech and expression: Article 19(1)(a).
• (B) Peaceful assembly: Article 19(1)(b).
• (C) Acquire/hold property (Article 19(1)(f)): Correct! Originally part of Article 19, this right was DELETED by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 and made a non-fundamental legal/constitutional right under Article 300A.
• (D) Practice profession: Article 19(1)(g).
tip: ► Current Article 19 Freedoms (6): Speech (a), Assembly (b), Association (c), Movement (d), Residence (e), Profession (g)! Clause (f) was abolished by 44th Amendment.

subject: Polity
q: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted which Article into Part III to make free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14 a Fundamental Right?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Article 21A • (A) Article 21A: Correct! Inserted by 86th Amendment Act, 2002, mandating the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. Operationalized by RTE Act, 2009.
• (B) Article 24A: Non-existent.
• (C) Article 30A.
• (D) Article 45: DPSP amended to focus on early childhood care below 6 years.
tip: ► 86th Amendment Triad (2002): 1. Added Article 21A (Fundamental Right); 2. Amended Article 45 (DPSP); 3. Added 11th Fundamental Duty Article 51A(k)!

subject: Polity
q: The President of India exercises the executive power of 'Pardon, Reprieve, Respite, or Remission of punishment' under which Article of the Constitution?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Article 72 • (A) Article 61: Impeachment of the President.
• (B) Article 72: Correct! Vests the President with pardoning powers in all cases of court-martial, death sentences, and union law offenses. (Governor's power is under Article 161, who cannot pardon death sentences).
• (C) Article 74: Council of Ministers advising President.
• (D) Article 161: Pardoning power of State Governor.
tip: ► Clemency Comparison: President (Art 72) can pardon DEATH sentences and court-martial penalties; Governor (Art 161) CANNOT grant full pardon for death sentences!

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 143 of the Constitution of India, who has the exclusive power to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or public fact?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) The President of India • (A) Prime Minister.
• (B) The President of India: Correct! Under Article 143, the President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its consultative advisory opinion.
• (C) Chief Justice of India.
• (D) Law Minister.
tip: ► Advisory Nature: Supreme Court advice under Article 143 is consultative and NOT binding on the President (e.g. Berubari, Ayodhya references)!

subject: Polity
q: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added which Schedule to the Constitution, specifying 18 functional items entrusted to Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 12th Schedule • (A) 10th Schedule: Anti-Defection.
• (B) 11th Schedule: Panchayati Raj (29 functional subjects under 73rd Amendment).
• (C) 12th Schedule: Correct! Added by 74th Amendment Act, 1992, listing 18 municipal functional matters including urban planning, roads, fire services, and public health.
• (D) 9th Schedule: Land reform laws protected from judicial review.
tip: ► Schedules 11 vs. 12: 11th Schedule = Panchayats (29 subjects, 73rd Act); 12th Schedule = Municipalities (18 subjects, 74th Act)!

subject: Polity
q: Under the 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) introduced by the 52nd Amendment, who is the designated authority to adjudicate disqualification petitions against an MP or MLA?
opts: The Presiding Officer of the House (Speaker / Chairman)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) The Presiding Officer of the House (Speaker / Chairman) • (A) Election Commission: Recommends disqualifications under Article 102/103 (office of profit), but not under 10th Schedule.
• (B) Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman): Correct! Paragraph 6 of the 10th Schedule gives the Speaker or Chairman exclusive authority to decide defection petitions, subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan case, 1992).
• (C) President/Governor.
• (D) Supreme Court directly.
tip: ► Kihoto Hollohan Precedent (1992): The Speaker acts as a tribunal when deciding anti-defection cases; their decision is amenable to High Court and Supreme Court judicial review!

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 338A of the Constitution of India, which constitutional body oversees safeguards and investigates complaints concerning the Scheduled Tribes?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) • (A) Minorities Commission.
• (B) NCST (Article 338A): Correct! Created by bifurcating the National Commission for SCs and STs via the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
• (C) Tribal Advisory Council: Created under 5th Schedule.
• (D) NCBC: Article 338B (102nd Amendment Act).
tip: ► Constitutional Commission Articles: Art 338 = NCSC; Art 338A = NCST; Art 338B = NCBC!

subject: Polity
q: The parliamentary device of 'Zero Hour', during which Members of Parliament can raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice, is an Indian innovation introduced in:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 1962 • (A) 1952.
• (B) 1962: Correct! Zero Hour starts immediately after Question Hour (around 12:00 noon) and lasts until the regular business is taken up. It was introduced informally in the Indian Parliament in 1962.
• (C) 1972.
• (D) 1982.
tip: ► Indian Procedural Innovation: Zero Hour is NOT mentioned in the Rules of Procedure; it is an uncodified Indian parliamentary convention established in 1962!

subject: Polity
q: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 amended Article 352 to stipulate that the President can proclaim a National Emergency ONLY after receiving:
opts: Oral advice from the Prime Minister
Written recommendation from the Union Cabinet (Council of Cabinet Ministers)
A two-thirds resolution of the Rajya Sabha
The recommendation of the Supreme Court
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Written recommendation from the Union Cabinet • (A) Oral PM advice: Permitted during 1975 emergency, now strictly barred.
• (B) Written Union Cabinet recommendation: Correct! Inserted by 44th Amendment in Article 352(3) to prevent unilateral advice by a Prime Minister without collective cabinet approval.
• (C) Rajya Sabha resolution.
• (D) Supreme Court advice.
tip: ► 'Cabinet' in Constitution: The word 'Cabinet' appears in ONLY ONE place in the entire Constitution of India: Article 352(3)!

subject: Polity
q: The concept of 'Public Interest Litigation' (PIL), which liberalized locus standi rules to allow citizens to seek justice for the marginalized, was pioneered in India in the late 1970s and 1980s by:
opts: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer • (A) H.J. Kania: First Chief Justice of independent India.
• (B) P.N. Bhagwati & V.R. Krishna Iyer: Correct! Relaxed the rule of locus standi in landmark cases like Hussainara Khatoon (1979) and SP Gupta (1981), allowing any public-spirited citizen to write a letter to enforce rights of the poor.
• (C) Y.V. Chandrachud: Longest-serving CJI.
• (D) M.H. Kania.
tip: ► Epistolary Jurisdiction: Justice Bhagwati transformed letters and postcards sent to the Supreme Court into writ petitions to protect undertrial prisoners and bonded laborers!

subject: Polity
q: A Judge of the Supreme Court of India holds office until attaining the age of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 65 years • (A) 60 years.
• (B) 62 years: Retirement age for High Court judges (Article 217).
• (C) 65 years: Correct! Under Article 124(2), a Judge of the Supreme Court holds office until attaining 65 years of age.
• (D) 70 years.
tip: ► Retirement Age Rule: High Court Judge = 62 years; Supreme Court Judge = 65 years!

subject: Polity
q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Article 141 • (A) Article 137: Supreme Court's power to review its own judgments.
• (B) Article 141: Correct! 'The law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India' (Doctrine of Stare Decisis).
• (C) Article 142: Complete justice.
• (D) Article 144: Civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of Supreme Court.
tip: ► Stare Decisis: Article 141 establishes that Supreme Court rulings are the supreme binding law of the land for all subordinate courts!

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, the Supreme Court is empowered to:
opts: Pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter before it
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter before it • (A) Impeach President: Parliament under Article 61.
• (B) Doing Complete Justice: Correct! Inherent equitable power invoked by the apex court in landmark cases (e.g. Bhopal Gas Tragedy, Ayodhya title dispute, liquor ban on highways).
• (C) Overrule amendments without hearing.
• (D) Dismiss governors.
tip: ► Article 142 Scope: Empowers the Supreme Court to transcend procedural statutory limitations to do substantive, complete justice in any pending case!

subject: Polity
q: The power to create or abolish a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) under Article 169 is vested in:
opts: The Parliament of India, after the State Assembly passes a special resolution
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) The Parliament of India, after the State Assembly passes a special resolution • (A) Assembly alone: Cannot create/abolish directly.
• (B) Parliament by law after Assembly resolution: Correct! Under Article 169, State Legislative Assembly must pass a resolution by special majority (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting); Parliament then passes an ordinary law.
• (C) Governor.
• (D) President.
tip: ► Article 169 Procedure: Assembly Resolution by SPECIAL majority -> Parliamentary law by SIMPLE majority! Not considered a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Following Operation Polo in September 1948, who headed the military administration of Hyderabad State as Military Governor from 1948 to December 1949?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Major General J.N. Chaudhuri • (A) Major General J.N. Chaudhuri: Correct! Commanded the Southern Army during Operation Polo and served as Military Governor of Hyderabad State from Sept 1948 to Dec 1949.
• (B) M.K. Vellodi: Senior ICS officer who succeeded Chaudhuri as Chief Minister/Civil Administrator in Dec 1949.
• (C) K.M. Munshi: India's Agent General in Hyderabad before police action.
• (D) K.S. Thimayya.
tip: ► Transition Order: Military Governor (Major Gen J.N. Chaudhuri, 1948–49) -> Civil Administrator (M.K. Vellodi ICS, 1949–52) -> Elected CM (Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, 1952–56)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The historic Mulki Rules in Hyderabad State were given statutory protection via the Royal Firman issued in 1919 by which Nizam of the Asaf Jahi dynasty?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Mir Osman Ali Khan (Nizam VII) • (A) Mir Mahboob Ali Khan (Nizam VI): Issued 1888/1894 circulars.
• (B) Mir Osman Ali Khan (Nizam VII): Correct! Issued the landmark Royal Firman on January 11, 1919 (establishing the Executive Council) which defined a 'Mulki' as one who was born in Hyderabad State or resided there continuously for at least 15 years.
• (C) Afzal-ud-Daula (Nizam V).
• (D) Nasir-ud-Daula (Nizam IV).
tip: ► 15-Year Rule: The 1919 Firman of Nizam VII defined Mulki status: 15 years of continuous permanent residence without non-Mulki parents!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: In the first general elections of 1952, who was elected as the first democratic Chief Minister of Hyderabad State, heading a Congress cabinet until 1956?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Burgula Ramakrishna Rao • (A) K.V. Ranga Reddy: Revenue Minister in Burgula's cabinet.
• (B) Burgula Ramakrishna Rao: Correct! Eminent polyglot, scholar, and Congress stalwart who served as the first and only elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State (1952–1956). Later Governor of Kerala and UP.
• (C) Dr. Marri Channa Reddy: Agriculture & Food Minister in his cabinet.
• (D) J.V. Narsing Rao.
tip: ► Historical Fact: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was the ONLY elected Chief Minister of the erstwhile Hyderabad State (1952–1956)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The demand for 'Vishalandhra' (merging Telugu-speaking areas of Hyderabad State with Andhra State) gained massive impetus after Andhra State was formed on October 1, 1953 following the supreme sacrifice of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Potti Sreeramulu (58-day fast unto death) • (A) Tanguturi Prakasam: 1st Chief Minister of Andhra State at Kurnool.
• (B) Potti Sreeramulu: Correct! Commenced hunger strike on October 19, 1952 at Bulusu Sambamurti's house in Madras and attained martyrdom on December 15, 1952 (58 days), leading to Andhra State formation on Oct 1, 1953.
• (C) Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
• (D) Kalluri Subba Rao.
tip: ► Martyrdom & Formation: Potti Sreeramulu's supreme sacrifice forced PM Nehru to announce Andhra State, which was inaugurated on October 1, 1953 with Kurnool as capital!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956, the statutory body created to safeguard Telangana's educational, employment, and developmental interests was the Telangana Regional Committee (TRC). Who was elected as its first Chairman?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) K. Achyutha Reddy • (A) K. Achyutha Reddy: Correct! Congress MLA from Kodangal, elected as the first Chairman of the Telangana Regional Committee (TRC) in 1958.
• (B) J. Chokka Rao: Later influential Chairman of TRC (1967–1971).
• (C) K.V. Ranga Reddy: Deputy CM.
• (D) P.V. Narasimha Rao.
tip: ► TRC Chairmen: First Chairman = K. Achyutha Reddy (1958); Later prominent Chairman during 1969 agitation = J. Chokka Rao!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: On which date is 'Telangana Martyrs Memorial Day' observed across the state to commemorate the 369 student and youth martyrs who sacrificed their lives during the 1969 Telangana Agitation?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) June 2 • (A) January 8: Palvancha hunger strike day.
• (B) June 2: Correct! Commemorates Telangana Martyrs. (On June 2, 2014, Telangana officially came into being, aligning with the historic martyrs' legacy).
• (C) September 17: Hyderabad Liberation / Integration Day.
• (D) December 9: Chidambaram midnight announcement.
tip: ► 369 Martyrs: The Telangana Martyrs Memorial (Gun Park, opposite State Assembly) sculpted by Aekka Yadagiri Rao stands in tribute to the 369 students slain in 1969 police firings!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The Justice V. Bhargava Committee appointed under Indira Gandhi's Eight-Point Formula (1969) determined that the accumulated Telangana revenue surplus diverted to other regions between 1956 and 1968 stood at:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Rs. 28.34 Crores • (A) Rs. 28.34 Crores: Correct! Appointed under Eight-Point Formula, Justice V. Bhargava of Supreme Court determined that Rs. 28.34 Crores of Telangana surplus revenue had been unconstitutionally diverted to Andhra region.
• (B) Rs. 102.00 Crores: Kumarayya estimate.
• (C) Rs. 10.50 Crores.
• (D) Rs. 64.20 Crores.
tip: ► Surplus Divergence: Telangana leaders estimated surplus at over Rs. 100 crores; official Bhargava Committee settled it at Rs. 28.34 Crores!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Which government order issued in January 1969 to repatriate non-locals appointed in Telangana was challenged and eventually litigated up to the Supreme Court in the landmark 'Venkata Reddy' case?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) G.O. Ms. No. 36 • (A) G.O. Ms. No. 36: Correct! Issued on January 21, 1969 by Kasu Brahmananda Reddy government following all-party agreement, ordering all non-locals appointed in Telangana to be repatriated by Feb 28, 1969. Struck down in March 1970.
• (B) G.O. Ms. No. 610: Issued in December 1985.
• (C) G.O. Ms. No. 674.
• (D) G.O. Ms. No. 16.
tip: ► Twin Landmark G.O.s: 1969 = G.O. 36 (Kasu Brahmananda Reddy); 1985 = G.O. 610 (N.T. Rama Rao)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The 'Jai Andhra Agitation' of 1972, which demanded the division of Andhra Pradesh, was sparked when a five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court delivered a historic verdict upholding the constitutional validity of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) The Mulki Rules • (A) Mulki Rules: Correct! On October 3, 1972, a 5-judge Constitution bench headed by Chief Justice S.M. Sikri upheld the validity of Mulki Rules as valid post-Constitution laws under Article 35(b), triggering the violent 'Jai Andhra' agitation by coastal leaders.
• (B) Presidential Order.
• (C) G.O. 610.
• (D) TRC Abolition.
tip: ► Direct Trigger of Jai Andhra: When the Supreme Court ruled that Mulki rules were fully legal, Andhra leaders realized they could not claim jobs in Hyderabad, demanding bifurcation!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Andhra Pradesh Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order, 1975 (Presidential Order), how many administrative zones were established across Andhra Pradesh?
opts: 6 Zones (Zones V and VI for Telangana)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 6 Zones (Zones V and VI for Telangana) • (A) 4 Zones.
• (B) 6 Zones: Correct! Issued under Article 371-D on October 18, 1975 by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed: Zones I to IV covered Andhra and Rayalaseema; Zones V and VI covered Telangana.
• (C) 7 Zones: Reorganized into 7 zones in 2018 (New Zonal System).
• (D) 8 Zones.
tip: ► Old vs. New Zonal Systems: 1975 Presidential Order = 6 Zones (Zones V & VI in Telangana); 2018 New Presidential Order = 7 Zones (all within Telangana State)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The three-member Officers Committee appointed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 1984 to inquire into violations of the Presidential Order in Telangana was chaired by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) K. Jayabharat Reddy IAS • (A) J.M. Girglani: Appointed in 2001 to probe non-implementation of G.O. 610.
• (B) K. Jayabharat Reddy: Correct! 3-member officers committee (Jayabharat Reddy, Kamalamma, Umapathi Rao) submitted report in 1985 finding 58,962 illegal non-local appointments, leading directly to G.O. Ms. No. 610.
• (C) Umapathi Rao: Committee member.
• (D) Kamalanathan.
tip: ► Origin of G.O. 610: Jayabharat Reddy Committee (1984–85) documented the massive violation of local cadres -> resulting in G.O. 610 on Dec 30, 1985!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The famous 'Warangal Declaration' of December 28–29, 1997, which mobilized democratic rights organizations and civil society behind the separate Telangana state demand, was organized under the aegis of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) All India People's Resistance Forum (AIPRF) • (A) TJAC: Formed in 2009.
• (B) AIPRF: Correct! Held on December 28–29, 1997 at Kakatiya Degree College grounds in Warangal under AIPRF leadership; poet Kaloji delivered his stirring message demanding democratic statehood.
• (C) TRS: Formed in 2001.
• (D) TVV.
tip: ► Twin 1997 Declarations: March 1997 = Bhuvanagiri Sabha (Daga Paddana Telangana); December 1997 = Warangal Declaration!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: On April 27, 2001, Kalvakuntla Chandrashekar Rao resigned as Deputy Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly and launched the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) at which venue in Hyderabad?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Jala Drushyam • (A) Nizam College Grounds.
• (B) Jala Drushyam: Correct! Located on the shores of Hussain Sagar, the residence of Konda Lakshman Bapuji, where KCR founded Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) on April 27, 2001 with pink flag and map.
• (C) Indira Park Dharna Chowk.
• (D) Jubilee Hall.
tip: ► Birthplace of TRS: Jala Drushyam (residence of veteran freedom fighter Konda Lakshman Bapuji) was the founding site of TRS on April 27, 2001!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: In December 2009, following the mass unrest triggered by KCR's indefinite hunger strike, the all-party coordinating body 'Telangana Joint Action Committee' (TJAC) was constituted under the leadership of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Prof. M. Kodandaram • (A) Prof. K. Jayashankar: Ideologue and mentor of the movement.
• (B) Prof. M. Kodandaram: Correct! Osmania University professor of Political Science appointed as Chairman of TJAC on December 24, 2009, leading historic programs like Million March, Sakala Janula Samme, and Sadak Bandh.
• (C) Swami Goud: TNGOs leader.
• (D) Vittal.
tip: ► TJAC Leadership: Prof. M. Kodandaram steered the united mass resistance platform coordinating students, employees, lawyers, and political parties!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The massive mass direct action 'Palle Palle Pattala Paiki' (Rail Roko agitation across all railway tracks in Telangana) was organized by TJAC on:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1st March, 2011 • (A) 1st March, 2011: Correct! Over 50,000 citizens and activists occupied all railway tracks across Telangana, halting trains for 8 hours.
• (B) 15th August, 2011.
• (C) 30th September, 2012: Sagara Haram.
• (D) 2nd June, 2013.
tip: ► Protests of 2011: March 1, 2011 = Palle Palle Pattala Paiki (Rail Roko); March 10, 2011 = Million March (Tank Bund); Sept–Oct 2011 = Sakala Janula Samme (42 days)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The 'Sadak Bandh' (complete blockade of the 400-km stretch of the National Highway 44 between Hyderabad and Bengaluru) was executed by pro-Telangana forces on:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 21st March, 2013 • (A) 21st March, 2013: Correct! TJAC organized the total blockade of the 400-km stretch of National Highway 44 (Hyderabad to Bengaluru) from Shamshabad to Alampur.
• (B) 14th June, 2013: Chalo Assembly.
• (C) 28th December, 2012.
• (D) 9th December, 2013.
tip: ► Highway Blockade: The Sadak Bandh on March 21, 2013 brought interstate traffic on NH 44 to a complete standstill, proving total mass control!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: On July 30, 2013, which apex political body formally resolved and requested the Central Government to initiate steps to create a separate State of Telangana?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Congress Working Committee (CWC) • (A) Cabinet directly.
• (B) CWC Resolution: Correct! On July 30, 2013, the Congress Working Committee (chaired by Sonia Gandhi) passed a historic unanimous resolution recommending the formation of a separate Telangana state with Hyderabad as common capital for 10 years.
• (C) NDC.
• (D) Rajya Sabha Special Committee.
tip: ► Decisive Political Moment: The July 30, 2013 CWC resolution cleared the political hurdle, leading to Group of Ministers (GoM) and the 2014 Reorganisation Act!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under Section 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, how many original districts of the erstwhile State of Andhra Pradesh were constituted into the new State of Telangana?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 districts • (A) 9 districts.
• (B) 10 districts: Correct! Section 3 of the 2014 Act specified the 10 constituent districts: Adilabad, Hyderabad, Karimnagar, Khammam, Mahbubnagar, Medak, Nalgonda, Nizamabad, Ranga Reddy, and Warangal.
• (C) 12 districts.
• (D) 31 districts: Created during 2016 state reorganization (later expanded to 33).
tip: ► 10 Founding Districts: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 created Telangana with its 10 historic districts before the 2016/2019 decentralization into 33 districts!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which major higher education institution was specifically mandated to be established in Telangana by the Central Government?
opts: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Central Tribal University • (A) IISER: Mandated for Andhra Pradesh (Tirupati).
• (B) Central Tribal University: Correct! Schedule 13 explicitly mandated a Central Tribal University in Telangana, established as Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University in Mulugu district.
• (C) Indian Maritime University: Chennai/Visakhapatnam.
• (D) National Forensic Sciences University.
tip: ► Mulugu Tribal University: Formally legislated by Parliament in 2023 as the Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University in Mulugu, fulfilling Schedule 13 of the 2014 Act!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: On which date did the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 receive the formal assent of the President of India (Pranab Mukherjee)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 1st March, 2014 • (A) Feb 18, 2014: Lok Sabha passage.
• (B) Feb 20, 2014: Rajya Sabha passage.
• (C) 1st March, 2014: Correct! President Pranab Mukherjee gave his formal assent on March 1, 2014, and the Act was published in the Gazette of India on March 2, 2014.
• (D) June 2, 2014: Appointed Day.
tip: ► Act Milestone Dates: Lok Sabha = Feb 18; Rajya Sabha = Feb 20; Presidential Assent = March 1; Gazette Notification = March 2; Appointed Day = June 2, 2014!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The magnificent 'Thousand Pillar Temple' (Rudreshwara Temple) in Hanamkonda, built in the Trikuta architectural style dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Surya, was constructed in 1163 CE by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Kakatiya King Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) • (A) Rudradeva: Correct! Constructed in 1163 CE at Hanamkonda; features a star-shaped Trikutalaya housing shrines dedicated to Shiva (Rudreshwara), Vishnu (Vasudeva), and Surya, with monolithic Nandi.
• (B) Ganapatideva: Built Pakhal Lake and Ramappa temple (via Recharla Rudra).
• (C) Rudrama Devi: Consolidated Warangal fort.
• (D) Prola II: Father of Rudradeva.
