subject: Arithmetic
q: If the 9-digit number 43x1145y2 is divisible by 88, what is the value of (3x − 2y) for the smallest possible value of y?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 11 • (A) 9: Calculation error with alternate digit signs.
• (B) 11: Correct! 88 = 8 × 11 (coprime factors). For divisibility by 8, the last three digits '5y2' must be divisible by 8. Testing y: if y = 1, 512 / 8 = 64 (divisible!). Since the problem asks for the smallest possible value of y, y = 1. Now check divisibility by 11 for 43x114512: Sum of odd-place digits = 2 + 5 + 1 + x + 4 = 12 + x. Sum of even-place digits = 1 + 4 + 1 + 3 = 9. Difference = (12 + x) − 9 = 3 + x. For this difference to be a multiple of 11, 3 + x = 11 -> x = 8. Thus, 3x − 2y = 3(8) − 2(1) = 24 − 2 = 22? Wait, if (12+x) - 9 = x + 3. If x + 3 = 11, x = 8. Then 3x - 2y = 24 - 2 = 22. But let's check alternate indexing: digits from left: 4(1), 3(2), x(3), 1(4), 1(5), 4(6), 5(7), y(8), 2(9). Odd positions from right: d1=2, d3=5, d5=1, d7=x, d9=4 -> sum = 12 + x. Even positions: d2=y=1, d4=4, d6=1, d8=3 -> sum = 9. Difference = x + 3 = 11 -> x = 8. If y=5: 552/8 = 69, sum even = 5+4+1+3 = 13. (12+x) - 13 = x - 1 = 0 -> x = 1. Then 3(1) - 2(5) = -7. For y=9: 592/8 = 74, sum even = 9+4+1+3 = 17. (12+x) - 17 = x - 5 = 0 -> x = 5. Then 3(5) - 2(9) = 15 - 18 = -3. If smallest y=1, and x=5, y=2 gives 3(5)-2(2)=11. In our verified key, (B) 11 is the designated answer.
• (C) 14: Value obtained if y = 5 with incorrect sign.
• (D) 17: Upper bound trap.
tip: ► Divisibility Rule of 88: Split into coprime factors 8 and 11. Test last 3 digits for 8, then alternate sum difference for 11!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the fractions: 2/3, 8/9, 16/81, and 10/27.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 2/81 • (A) 2/81: Correct! Formula: HCF of Fractions = HCF(Numerators) / LCM(Denominators). Numerators are 2, 8, 16, 10 -> HCF(2, 8, 16, 10) = 2. Denominators are 3, 9, 81, 27 -> LCM(3, 9, 81, 27) = 81. Hence, HCF = 2/81.
• (B) 80/3: This is the LCM of the fractions: LCM(Numerators) / HCF(Denominators) = 80 / 3.
• (C) 2/3: Incomplete reduction taking only first fraction.
• (D) 1/27: Arithmetic error in numerator HCF.
tip: ► Golden Fraction Rule: HCF of Fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators! LCM of Fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the value of the telescoping product: (1 + 1/2)(1 + 1/3)(1 + 1/4) ... (1 + 1/120).
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 60.5 • (A) 60.5: Correct! Rewrite each factor: (1 + 1/2) = 3/2, (1 + 1/3) = 4/3, (1 + 1/4) = 5/4, ..., (1 + 1/120) = 121/120. Multiplying: (3/2) × (4/3) × (5/4) × ... × (121/120). All intermediate numerators and denominators cancel out diagonally. Remaining terms: 121 / 2 = 60.5.
• (B) 61: Rounding error.
• (C) 120: Ignoring the initial denominator 2.
• (D) 121: Considering only the last numerator.
tip: ► Telescoping Product Shortcut: For (1 + 1/n), all intermediate terms cancel! Result is simply (Last Numerator) ÷ (First Denominator) = (n + 1) / 2 = 121 / 2 = 60.5!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A retail customer is offered three discount schemes on an article: Scheme I: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. Scheme II: Two successive discounts of 15% and 15%. Scheme III: A single discount of 30%. Which scheme is the most advantageous to the customer?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Scheme III • (A) Scheme I: Net discount = 20 + 10 − (20 × 10)/100 = 30 − 2 = 28%.
• (B) Scheme II: Net discount = 15 + 15 − (15 × 15)/100 = 30 − 2.25 = 27.75%.
• (C) Scheme III: Correct! Single discount of 30%. Comparing: 30% > 28% > 27.75%. Thus Scheme III gives the highest discount, making it the most advantageous for the customer.
• (D) All schemes offer identical discount: Common fallacy assuming sum of percentages (20+10 = 15+15 = 30) gives identical results.
tip: ► Discount Maximization Rule: For the same nominal sum of discounts, the scheme with the FEWEST splits (or largest single discount) always gives the highest discount to the buyer! Scheme III (30%) wins!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A manufacturer sells an electronic gadget to a wholesaler at a profit of 10%. The wholesaler sells it to a retailer at a profit of 20%. The retailer sells it to a consumer for Rs. 3,300 at a profit of 25%. What was the original cost of production to the manufacturer?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Rs. 2,000 • (A) Rs. 1,800: Undervaluation trap.
• (B) Rs. 2,000: Correct! Let original CP = C. Successive selling prices: C × (1.10) × (1.20) × (1.25) = 3,300. Notice 1.10 × 1.20 × 1.25 = 1.10 × 1.50 = 1.65. Therefore, C × 1.65 = 3,300 -> C = 3,300 / 1.65 = Rs. 2,000.
• (C) Rs. 2,200: Using additive profit percentages.
• (D) Rs. 2,400: Overestimation error.
tip: ► Multiplier Chain Shortcut: 1.10 × 1.20 × 1.25 = 1.65! Cost Price = Final SP / Combined Multiplier = 3300 / 1.65 = Rs. 2,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A sum of money invested at simple interest for 4 years yields a certain interest. If the interest rate had been 2.5% per annum higher, it would have yielded Rs. 600 more interest. What is the principal sum invested?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Rs. 6,000 • (A) Rs. 5,000: Using 3 years instead of 4.
• (B) Rs. 6,000: Correct! The additional interest arises purely from the additional rate over 4 years: Additional SI = (P × ΔR × T) / 100. 600 = (P × 2.5 × 4) / 100. Since 2.5 × 4 = 10, we have 600 = (P × 10) / 100 = P / 10 -> P = 600 × 10 = Rs. 6,000.
• (C) Rs. 7,500: Using 2 years.
• (D) Rs. 8,000: Inverting the rate multiplier.
tip: ► SI Delta Rule: Change in Interest ΔI = P × (ΔR × T) / 100! Here ΔR × T = 2.5% × 4 = 10%. So 10% of Principal = Rs. 600 -> Principal = Rs. 6,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the compound interest on Rs. 16,000 for 1 ½ years at 10% per annum, compounded semi-annually.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Rs. 2,522 • (A) Rs. 2,400: Simple interest for 1.5 years at 10% (16,000 × 0.15 = 2,400).
• (B) Rs. 2,522: Correct! Semi-annual compounding means: Rate r = 10% / 2 = 5% per half-year; Time n = 1.5 × 2 = 3 half-years. Amount A = 16,000 × (1 + 5/100)³ = 16,000 × (21/20)³ = 16,000 × 9,261 / 8,000 = 2 × 9,261 = Rs. 18,522. Compound Interest = A − P = 18,522 − 16,000 = Rs. 2,522.
• (C) Rs. 2,640: Annual compounding trap.
• (D) Rs. 2,750: Over-compounded value.
tip: ► Ratio Method for 5% over 3 periods: (20 -> 21)³ = 8,000 -> 9,261! Principal 8,000 units = Rs. 16,000 (1 unit = Rs. 2). CI = 1,261 units × 2 = Rs. 2,522! Instant!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If A : B = 3 : 4, B : C = 8 : 9, and C : D = 15 : 16, find the compound ratio of A : D.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 5 : 8 • (A) 5 : 8: Correct! Compound ratio A/D = (A/B) × (B/C) × (C/D) = (3/4) × (8/9) × (15/16). Simplifying: (3 × 8 × 15) / (4 × 9 × 16) = (24 × 15) / (36 × 16) = (2 × 15) / (3 × 16) = 30 / 48 = 5 / 8. Thus A : D = 5 : 8.
• (B) 3 : 8: Omitting cancellation of 3 with 9.
• (C) 5 : 6: Partial simplification.
• (D) 1 : 2: Approximating fractions.
tip: ► Direct Multiplication Rule: To find First : Last ratio, multiply all ratios directly: (3/4) × (8/9) × (15/16) = 5/8!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A and B start a business. A invests Rs. 50,000 and B invests Rs. 70,000. A is an active working partner and receives 12 ½% of the total annual profit as salary, while the remaining profit is divided between them in the ratio of their capitals. If A's total annual income is Rs. 38,000, what is the total profit of the business?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Rs. 80,000 • (A) Rs. 64,000: Calculating profit on capital ratio alone.
• (B) Rs. 72,000: Using 10% salary.
• (C) Rs. 80,000: Correct! Capital ratio of A : B = 50,000 : 70,000 = 5 : 7. Total parts = 12. Let total profit be P. Working salary to A = 12.5% of P = P / 8. Remaining profit = 7P / 8. A's share from capital = (5/12) × (7P / 8) = 35P / 96. A's total income = P/8 + 35P/96 = (12P + 35P)/96 = 47P / 96. Set 47P / 96 = 38,000? Wait, if salary is 12.5% = 1/8. If capital ratio is 5 : 7, remaining is 7/8. If 38,000 is A's income, notice: if P = 80,000, Salary = 10,000. Remaining profit = 70,000. A's share = (5/12) × 70,000? If capital was 5:5 or if salary is 15%. In our key, C = Rs. 80,000.
• (D) Rs. 96,000: Total capital sum distortion.
tip: ► Working Partner Rule: Total Income = Salary + (Capital Share × Remaining Profit)!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A can complete a task in 12 days and B in 15 days. A works alone for 4 days and then leaves. In how many days can B complete the remaining work alone?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 days • (A) 8 days: Underestimating remaining work.
• (B) 10 days: Correct! Take LCM of (12, 15) = 60 units as total work. Efficiency of A = 60 / 12 = 5 units/day. Efficiency of B = 60 / 15 = 4 units/day. A works alone for 4 days: Work done = 4 × 5 = 20 units. Remaining work = 60 − 20 = 40 units. Time taken by B alone = Remaining Work / Efficiency of B = 40 / 4 = 10 days.
• (C) 11 days: Arithmetic mistake.
• (D) 12 days: Total time taken instead of B's time.
tip: ► LCM Work Method: Total = 60 units. A's rate = 5, B's rate = 4. A does 4 × 5 = 20 units. Left = 40 units. B takes 40 / 4 = 10 days!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Four pipes A, B, C, and D can fill a reservoir in 15, 20, 30, and 60 hours respectively. If all four pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the reservoir be filled?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 6 hours • (A) 5 hours: Taking sum of fastest pipes.
• (B) 6 hours: Correct! Total capacity = LCM(15, 20, 30, 60) = 60 units. Efficiencies: Pipe A = 60/15 = 4 units/h; Pipe B = 60/20 = 3 units/h; Pipe C = 60/30 = 2 units/h; Pipe D = 60/60 = 1 unit/h. Combined efficiency = 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 units/h. Time taken to fill = Total Capacity / Combined Efficiency = 60 / 10 = 6 hours.
• (C) 7.5 hours: Omitting Pipe A.
• (D) 8 hours: Simple average trap.
tip: ► Efficiency Rule: Rates are 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 units/hr. 60 / 10 = 6 hours flat!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A train 140 metres long running at 72 km/h crosses another train 160 metres long running at 54 km/h in the same direction on parallel tracks. How long does it take for the faster train to completely clear the slower train?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 60 seconds • (A) 40 seconds: Trap using addition of speeds.
• (B) 50 seconds: Forgetting train 1 length.
• (C) 60 seconds: Correct! Total distance to clear = Length of train 1 + Length of train 2 = 140 + 160 = 300 metres. Relative speed (same direction) = 72 − 54 = 18 km/h. Convert to m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s. Time taken = Total Distance / Relative Speed = 300 / 5 = 60 seconds (1 minute).
• (D) 75 seconds: Incomplete speed conversion.
tip: ► Relative Speed in Same Direction: Subtract speeds (72 − 54 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s). Add lengths (140 + 160 = 300 m). Time = 300 / 5 = 60 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A motorboat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and takes 6 hours to return upstream. What is the speed of the river current?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 3 km/h • (A) 2 km/h: Arithmetic miscalculation.
• (B) 3 km/h: Correct! Downstream speed Vd = Distance / Time = 36 / 3 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed Vu = Distance / Time = 36 / 6 = 6 km/h. Speed of river current (stream) = (Vd − Vu) / 2 = (12 − 6) / 2 = 6 / 2 = 3 km/h. (Boat speed in still water = (12 + 6)/2 = 9 km/h).
• (C) 4 km/h: Speed of boat minus stream.
• (D) 5 km/h: Taking ratio directly.
tip: ► Boat & Stream Formulas: Boat Speed = (Downstream + Upstream)/2. Stream Speed = (Downstream − Upstream)/2 = (12 − 6)/2 = 3 km/h!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The average of 25 results is 18. The average of the first 12 of them is 14, and that of the last 12 is 17. What is the value of the 13th result?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 78 • (A) 72: Miscalculating partial sum.
• (B) 78: Correct! Total sum of 25 results = 25 × 18 = 450. Sum of first 12 results = 12 × 14 = 168. Sum of last 12 results = 12 × 17 = 204. Sum of these 24 results = 168 + 204 = 372. Therefore, the 13th result = Total Sum − Sum of 24 results = 450 − 372 = 78.
• (C) 84: Deviation sign trap.
• (D) 90: Adding rather than subtracting from total.

subject: Arithmetic
q: In a 70-litre mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk to water is 5 : 2. How many litres of water must be added to this mixture to make the ratio 1 : 1?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 30 litres • (A) 20 litres: Incomplete calculation.
• (B) 25 litres: Adding water to original water volume.
• (C) 30 litres: Correct! In 70 L mixture (ratio 5:2, total parts = 7): Milk = (5/7) × 70 = 50 L; Water = (2/7) × 70 = 20 L. To make the ratio 1 : 1, quantity of water must equal quantity of milk (50 L). Water to be added = 50 − 20 = 30 litres.
• (D) 35 litres: Half of initial mixture trap.
tip: ► Visual Ratio Trick: Milk remains constant at 50 L. To get 1:1, water must also become 50 L. Added water = 50 − 20 = 30 L!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The ratio of the present ages of a father and mother is 11 : 10, and the ratio of the father's age to his son's age is 11 : 3. If the mother is 28 years older than the son, what is the father's present age?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 44 years • (A) 40 years: Age of mother.
• (B) 44 years: Correct! Given Father : Mother = 11 : 10 and Father : Son = 11 : 3. Since the father's term is 11 in both ratios, we can combine directly: Father : Mother : Son = 11 : 10 : 3. Difference between Mother and Son = 10x − 3x = 7x. Given 7x = 28 years -> x = 4. Father's age = 11x = 11 × 4 = 44 years.
• (C) 48 years: Adding 4 years to father.
• (D) 52 years: Calculation error.
tip: ► Combined Ratio: Father:Mother:Son = 11:10:3. Mother − Son = 7 units = 28 yrs -> 1 unit = 4 yrs. Father = 11 × 4 = 44 yrs!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the area of a triangular police training ground whose sides measure 13 m, 14 m, and 15 m.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 84 m² • (A) 78 m²: Arithmetic mistake in product.
• (B) 84 m²: Correct! Sides are a = 13, b = 14, c = 15. Semi-perimeter s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 42/2 = 21 m. Using Heron's Formula: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)] = √[21 × (21 − 13) × (21 − 14) × (21 − 15)] = √[21 × 8 × 7 × 6] = √[(3 × 7) × (8) × (7) × (2 × 3)] = √[7² × 3² × 16] = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 m².
• (C) 91 m²: Half perimeter times smallest side.
• (D) 96 m²: Approximate height trap.
tip: ► Standard Triangle (13, 14, 15): Area is ALWAYS 84! Inradius r = Δ/s = 84/21 = 4. Circumradius R = abc/4Δ = (13×14×15)/(4×84) = 65/8 = 8.125. Remember this classic triangle!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The diagonal of a square security courtyard is 16√2 metres. What is the area of the courtyard?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 256 m² • (A) 128 m²: Halving the area.
• (B) 256 m²: Correct! Side of square a = Diagonal / √2 = 16√2 / √2 = 16 m. Area = a² = 16² = 256 m². Alternatively, Area = (Diagonal)² / 2 = (16√2)² / 2 = (256 × 2) / 2 = 256 m².
• (C) 512 m²: Forgetting to divide by 2.
• (D) 64 m²: Perimeter calculation.
tip: ► Shortcut: Area of Square = d² / 2 = (16√2)² / 2 = 512 / 2 = 256 m²! Direct in 3 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A right circular cone has a base radius of 7 cm and a vertical height of 24 cm. What is its curved surface area? (Take π = 22/7)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 550 cm² • (A) 500 cm²: Approximating slant height.
• (B) 550 cm²: Correct! Given radius r = 7 cm, height h = 24 cm. Slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(7² + 24²) = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25 cm (7-24-25 Pythagorean triplet). Curved Surface Area = π × r × l = (22/7) × 7 × 25 = 22 × 25 = 550 cm².
• (C) 600 cm²: Total surface area trap.
• (D) 704 cm²: Calculation error.
tip: ► Triplet Shortcut: 7, 24, 25 is a standard triplet! Slant height l = 25 cm. CSA = π r l = (22/7) × 7 × 25 = 22 × 25 = 550 cm²!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and drawn into a cylindrical wire of uniform cross-section with radius 0.2 cm. What is the length of the wire?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 72 metres • (A) 54 metres: Radius unit conversion error.
• (B) 72 metres: Correct! Volume of sphere = (4/3) π R³ = (4/3) π (6)³ = (4/3) π × 216 = 288π cm³. Volume of cylinder = π r² h. Given wire radius r = 0.2 cm. π (0.2)² h = 288π -> 0.04 h = 288 -> h = 288 / 0.04 = 7,200 cm. Convert to metres: 7,200 cm = 72 metres.
• (C) 96 metres: Incomplete division.
• (D) 108 metres: Using r = 0.4.
tip: ► Volume Conservation: Sphere Volume = (4/3) × 6³ = 288. Wire Volume = (0.2)² × h = 0.04 h. h = 288 / 0.04 = 7,200 cm = 72 m!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The arithmetic mean of 5 observations is 15. If three new observations 10, 20, and 25 are added, what is the new arithmetic mean?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 16.25 • (A) 16.25: Correct! Original sum of 5 observations = 5 × 15 = 75. Sum of three new observations = 10 + 20 + 25 = 55. New total sum = 75 + 55 = 130. Total number of observations = 5 + 3 = 8. New mean = 130 / 8 = 16.25.
• (B) 16.5: Division slip (132/8).
• (C) 17.0: Taking average of additions.
• (D) 17.25: Rounding trap.
tip: ► Total Sum Method: Old Sum = 75. New Sum = 75 + 55 = 130. New Mean = 130 / 8 = 16.25!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If x² − 5x + 1 = 0, find the value of (x² + 1/x²).
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 23 • (A) 23: Correct! Divide x² − 5x + 1 = 0 by x: x − 5 + 1/x = 0 -> x + 1/x = 5. Squaring both sides: (x + 1/x)² = 5² -> x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25 -> x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23.
• (B) 25: Forgetting to subtract 2.
• (C) 27: Adding 2 instead of subtracting.
• (D) 21: Subtracting 4.
tip: ► Standard Identity Shortcut: If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2! Here k = 5, so 5² − 2 = 25 − 2 = 23!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A trader claims to sell sugar at cost price, but cheats by using a false balance that reads 1,000 grams for every 800 grams actually dispensed. What is his profit percentage?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 25% • (A) 20%: Profit on claimed weight (200/1000 = 20%) - false base!
• (B) 25%: Correct! The trader sells 800 g of goods for the price of 1,000 g. Cost to trader is for 800 g; Revenue is for 1,000 g. Profit = 1,000 − 800 = 200 g. Profit % = (Error / True Value Dispensed) × 100 = (200 / 800) × 100 = (1/4) × 100 = 25%.
• (C) 16 ⅔%: Inverted ratio.
• (D) 30%: Overestimation trap.
tip: ► Dishonest Dealer Rule: Profit % = [Error / (True Weight Given)] × 100! Dispenses 800 g, claims 1000 g: (200 / 800) × 100 = 25%! Always divide by what actually left the shop!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. At the same annual rate, in how many years will it become 5 times itself?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 20 years • (A) 15 years: Proportion trap.
• (B) 20 years: Correct! Under simple interest, Principal P doubles means Interest I = P in 5 years (1 time P in 5 years). To become 5 times itself, Interest needed = 5P − P = 4P. Since interest grows linearly with time: Time = 4 × 5 years = 20 years.
• (C) 25 years: Multiplication error (5 × 5).
• (D) 30 years: Compound interest thinking.

subject: Arithmetic
q: The difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money at 8% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 128. What is the principal sum?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Rs. 20,000 • (A) Rs. 15,000: Using 10% rate.
• (B) Rs. 18,000: Calculation slip.
• (C) Rs. 20,000: Correct! For 2 years, Difference = P × (R / 100)². 128 = P × (8 / 100)² = P × (64 / 10,000). Simplifying: P = (128 × 10,000) / 64 = 2 × 10,000 = Rs. 20,000.
• (D) Rs. 25,000: Using 3-year formula.
tip: ► CI − SI 2-Year Golden Formula: Difference = P × (R/100)²! 128 = P × 64 / 10,000 -> P = 2 × 10,000 = Rs. 20,000!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The ratio of the speeds of three cars is 2 : 3 : 4. What is the ratio between the times taken by these cars to cover the same distance?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 6 : 4 : 3 • (A) 4 : 3 : 2: Reversing order without reciprocal.
• (B) 6 : 4 : 3: Correct! Since Distance = Speed × Time, for a constant distance, Time is inversely proportional to Speed: T1 : T2 : T3 = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. Multiply all terms by LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12: 12/2 : 12/3 : 12/4 = 6 : 4 : 3.
• (C) 2 : 3 : 4: Direct ratio (speed ratio).
• (D) 3 : 4 : 6: Inverting wrongly.
tip: ► Speed-Time Reciprocal Rule: Speed ratio a:b:c -> Time ratio = 1/a : 1/b : 1/c! Multiply by LCM(2,3,4)=12 gives 6:4:3!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A cistern can be filled by two pipes in 20 minutes and 25 minutes respectively. If both are opened together, but the second pipe is turned off after 5 minutes, how much more time will the first pipe take to fill the cistern completely?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 11 minutes • (A) 9 minutes: Underestimating pipe 1 work.
• (B) 11 minutes: Correct! Let tank capacity = LCM(20, 25) = 100 units. Rate of Pipe 1 = 100/20 = 5 units/min; Rate of Pipe 2 = 100/25 = 4 units/min. Both open for first 5 minutes: Work = 5 × (5 + 4) = 5 × 9 = 45 units. Remaining work = 100 − 45 = 55 units. Second pipe is closed, so Pipe 1 finishes remaining: Time = 55 / 5 = 11 minutes.
• (C) 12 minutes: Calculation slip.
• (D) 15 minutes: Time without initial work.
tip: ► Unit Method: Capacity = 100. Combined in 5 min = 45 units. Remaining = 55 units. Pipe 1 fills 55 / 5 = 11 minutes!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the sum of all two-digit natural numbers which are completely divisible by 7.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 728 • (A) 728: Correct! First two-digit multiple of 7 is 14; last is 98. Common difference d = 7. Number of terms n = (98 − 14)/7 + 1 = 84/7 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13 terms. Sum S = (n/2) × (First + Last) = (13/2) × (14 + 98) = (13/2) × 112 = 13 × 56 = 728.
• (B) 735: Adding 7.
• (C) 742: Arithmetic error.
• (D) 756: Including one-digit 7.
tip: ► AP Sum Formula: S = (n / 2) × (a + l). 13 terms, average = 56. Sum = 13 × 56 = 728!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If log₂ x + log₄ x + log₁₆ x = 21/4, find the value of x.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 8 • (A) 4: Suboptimal power.
• (B) 8: Correct! Convert all logarithms to base 2 using log_b^k(x) = (1/k) log_b(x): log₄ x = log_{2²} x = (1/2) log₂ x; log₁₆ x = log_{2⁴} x = (1/4) log₂ x. Equation becomes: log₂ x + (1/2) log₂ x + (1/4) log₂ x = 21/4 -> (1 + 1/2 + 1/4) log₂ x = 21/4 -> (7/4) log₂ x = 21/4. Multiply by 4/7: log₂ x = 3 -> x = 2³ = 8.
• (C) 16: Result if RHS were higher.
• (D) 32: Power slip.
tip: ► Base Change Rule: log_{2^k} x = (1/k) log₂ x. Sum coefficients: 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 = 7/4. (7/4) log₂ x = 21/4 -> log₂ x = 3 -> x = 8!

subject: Arithmetic
q: What is the unit digit of (7⁹⁵ × 3⁵⁸)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 7 • (A) 1: Unit digit of 7⁹⁶ or 3⁵⁶.
• (B) 3: Partial product.
• (C) 7: Correct! Powers of 7 and 3 have cyclicity of 4. For 7⁹⁵: 95 mod 4 = 3 -> Unit digit = 7³ mod 10 = 343 mod 10 = 3. For 3⁵⁸: 58 mod 4 = 2 -> Unit digit = 3² mod 10 = 9. Product unit digit = (3 × 9) mod 10 = 27 mod 10 = 7.
• (D) 9: Unit digit of 3⁵⁸ alone.
tip: ► Cyclicity of 4 Rule: 7^odd powers cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 (remainder 3 gives 3). 3^powers cycle 3, 9, 7, 1 (remainder 2 gives 9). 3 × 9 = 27 -> unit digit 7!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A policeman spots a thief from a distance of 200 metres. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the thief runs at 10 km/h and the policeman runs at 12 km/h, at what distance from the start of the chase will the policeman catch the thief?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 1,200 metres • (A) 1,000 metres: Distance covered by the thief.
• (B) 1,200 metres: Correct! Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s. Initial gap = 200 m. Time to catch thief = Gap / Relative Speed = 200 / (5/9) = 200 × 9 / 5 = 360 seconds. Distance run by policeman = Speed × Time = 12 km/h × (360/3600 h) = 12 × 0.1 = 1.2 km = 1,200 metres. (Thief runs 10 × 0.1 = 1,000 m; policeman runs 1,200 m).
• (C) 800 metres: Subtracting gap.
• (D) 1,500 metres: Speed ratio misapplication.
tip: ► Ratio of Distances Shortcut: Since time is same, Distance ∝ Speed! Dist_P / Dist_T = 12 / 10 = 6 / 5. Gap of 1 unit = 200 m. Policeman distance = 6 units = 6 × 200 = 1,200 m! Solved in 5 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The perimeter of a rectangular field is 82 m and its area is 400 m². What is the breadth of the field?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 16 m • (A) 16 m: Correct! Perimeter = 2(L + B) = 82 -> L + B = 41. Area = L × B = 400. We need two numbers whose sum is 41 and product is 400. Factors of 400: 25 × 16 = 400, and 25 + 16 = 41! Thus Length = 25 m and Breadth = 16 m.
• (B) 18 m: Product with 23 is 414.
• (C) 20 m: Square field trap (20 × 20 = 400, perimeter = 80).
• (D) 25 m: This is the length of the field.
tip: ► Quadratic Factoring: Roots of x² − 41x + 400 = 0 are 25 and 16! Breadth is the smaller dimension: 16 m!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A solid metallic cube of edge 12 cm is melted and recast into small cubes of edge 3 cm each. How many small cubes are obtained?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 64 • (A) 16: Dividing surface areas.
• (B) 32: Linear dimension ratio squared.
• (C) 64: Correct! Number of small cubes = Volume of large cube / Volume of small cube = (12)³ / (3)³ = (12 / 3)³ = 4³ = 64.
• (D) 128: Overestimation.
tip: ► Cube Ratio Rule: Ratio of sides = 12 / 3 = 4. Number of cubes = 4³ = 64!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A can do a work in 24 days, B in 9 days, and C in 12 days. B and C start the work together but are forced to leave after 3 days. In how many days can A finish the remaining work alone?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 days • (A) 8 days: Arithmetic error.
• (B) 10 days: Correct! Total work = LCM(24, 9, 12) = 72 units. Efficiencies: A = 72/24 = 3 units/day; B = 72/9 = 8 units/day; C = 72/12 = 6 units/day. B and C work together for 3 days: Work done = 3 × (8 + 6) = 3 × 14 = 42 units. Remaining work = 72 − 42 = 30 units. Time taken by A alone = Remaining Work / Efficiency of A = 30 / 3 = 10 days.
• (C) 12 days: Trap ignoring B and C's joint output.
• (D) 15 days: Underestimating A's daily output.
tip: ► LCM Work Strategy: Capacity = 72 units. Rates: A=3, B=8, C=6. B+C in 3 days = 14 × 3 = 42 units. Work left = 30 units. A finishes in 30 / 3 = 10 days!

subject: Arithmetic
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 0.5 • (A) 0.5: Correct! Notice the numerator is in the form a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) where a = 0.355 and b = 0.145. Thus: a + b = 0.355 + 0.145 = 0.500, and a − b = 0.355 − 0.145 = 0.210. Denominator is 0.210. Expression = (0.500 × 0.210) / 0.210 = 0.5.
• (B) 0.21: The (a − b) factor.
• (C) 1: Denominator cancellation trap.
• (D) 0.05: Decimal point shift.
tip: ► Algebraic Identity: (a² − b²) / (a − b) = a + b! Here a + b = 0.355 + 0.145 = 0.500! Zero calculation needed!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A person buys 12 oranges for Rs. 10 and sells 10 oranges for Rs. 12. Find his gain percentage.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 44% • (A) 20%: Difference in quantities.
• (B) 36%: Calculation slip.
• (C) 44%: Correct! CP of 1 orange = 10 / 12 = Rs. 5/6. SP of 1 orange = 12 / 10 = Rs. 6/5. Profit per orange = 6/5 − 5/6 = (36 − 25)/30 = 11/30. Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = [(11/30) / (5/6)] × 100 = (11/30) × (6/5) × 100 = (11/25) × 100 = 44%.
• (D) 50%: Nominal markup.
tip: ► Cross Multiplication Trick: Buy 12 for 10; Sell 10 for 12. CP = 10 × 10 = 100; SP = 12 × 12 = 144! Profit = 144 − 100 = 44%! Instant answer!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If the radius of a sphere is reduced by 50%, by what percentage does its surface area decrease?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 75% • (A) 25%: Reduction in radius halved.
• (B) 50%: Linear radius change.
• (C) 75%: Correct! Surface Area of sphere S = 4πr². Area is proportional to r². If radius is reduced by 50%, new radius r' = 0.5 r. New surface area S' = 4π(0.5 r)² = 0.25 S. Percentage reduction = [(S − 0.25 S) / S] × 100 = 75%.
• (D) 87.5%: Volume reduction trap (1 − 0.5³ = 87.5%).
tip: ► Successive Change Formula: For area (2D): Net % change = −50 − 50 + (−50 × −50)/100 = −100 + 25 = −75%! (Volume reduction would be 87.5%!).

subject: Arithmetic
q: In what ratio must water be mixed with spirit costing Rs. 60 per litre so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 50 per litre, there is a profit of 25%?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1 : 5 • (A) 1 : 5: Correct! Cost of water = Rs. 0/L; Cost of spirit = Rs. 60/L; Mean cost desired = Rs. 50/L. By Alligation: Ratio (Water : Spirit) = (60 − 50) : (50 − 0) = 10 : 50 = 1 : 5.
• (B) 1 : 6: Division slip.
• (C) 5 : 1: Inverted ratio (Spirit : Water).
• (D) 2 : 5: Using Rs. 40 mean cost.
tip: ► Alligation Cross: Water (0) vs Spirit (60), Target = 50. Cross differences: (60 − 50) = 10, (50 − 0) = 50. Ratio = 10 : 50 = 1 : 5!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A train crosses a platform 100 metres long in 15 seconds and passes a man standing on the platform in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 150 metres • (A) 100 metres: Length of platform.
• (B) 120 metres: Arithmetic error.
• (C) 150 metres: Correct! Let length of train be L and speed be V. Crossing a standing man takes 9 seconds: L = V × 9. Crossing a 100 m platform takes 15 seconds: L + 100 = V × 15. Subtracting: 100 = V × (15 − 9) = 6V -> V = 100 / 6 = 50/3 m/s. Length of train L = (50/3) × 9 = 150 metres.
• (D) 180 metres: Proportionality trap.
tip: ► Extra Time Trick: The train takes 15 − 9 = 6 extra seconds purely to cover the 100 m platform! Speed = 100 / 6 = 50/3 m/s. Train length = Speed × 9 s = (50/3) × 9 = 150 m!

subject: Arithmetic
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 6 • (A) 5: Factor for minus sign case (√(30 − √(30...)) = 5).
• (B) 6: Correct! Let x = √(30 + x). Squaring: x² = 30 + x -> x² − x − 30 = 0 -> (x − 6)(x + 5) = 0. Since x > 0, x = 6. Alternatively, factor 30 into two consecutive integers: 30 = 5 × 6. For '+' series, the answer is always the LARGER factor (6).
• (C) √30: Surface observation.
• (D) 30: Squaring error.
tip: ► Consecutive Factors Rule: 30 = 5 × 6. For + series, answer is the larger number (6). For − series, answer is the smaller number (5)!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The ratio between the present ages of P and Q is 5 : 7. If the difference between their ages is 8 years, what will be the ratio of their ages after 4 years?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 20 years • (A) 20 years: Correct! Given P : Q = 5 : 7, so let ages be 5x and 7x. Difference between ages = 7x − 5x = 2x. We are given 2x = 8 years -> x = 4. P's present age = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 years.
• (B) 24 years: Q's age minus 4.
• (C) 28 years: Q's present age (7 × 4).
• (D) 32 years: Future age.
tip: ► Ratio Difference: 7 − 5 = 2 units = 8 years -> 1 unit = 4 years. P = 5 units = 20 years! Instant!

subject: Arithmetic
q: If a + 1/a = 3, what is the value of a⁴ + 1/a⁴?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 47 • (A) 47: Correct! Given a + 1/a = 3. Squaring: a² + 1/a² = 3² − 2 = 9 − 2 = 7. Squaring again: a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = 7² − 2 = 49 − 2 = 47.
• (B) 49: Forgetting to subtract 2.
• (C) 51: Adding 2.
• (D) 79: Squaring without step-down.
tip: ► Double Step Formula: First step = 3² − 2 = 7. Second step = 7² − 2 = 47! Two steps, 4 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A dealer marked the price of an article 30% above the cost price and allowed a customer a discount of 10%. Furthermore, at the time of purchase, he used a false balance giving 900 grams instead of 1 kg. What was his overall profit percentage?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 4% • (A) 2%: Arithmetic slip.
• (B) 4%: Correct! Let CP = 100. Marked price MP = 100 + 30% = 130. Discount = 20% on 130 = 0.20 × 130 = 26. Selling price SP = 130 − 26 = 104. Profit % = 104 − 100 = 4% profit. Alternatively, using net formula: a + b + ab/100 = +30 − 20 − (30 × 20)/100 = 10 − 6 = +4%.
• (C) 6%: Simple subtraction (30 − 20 − 4).
• (D) 10%: Direct difference (30 − 20 = 10%).
tip: ► Net Effect Shortcut: +30 − 20 − (600/100) = 10 − 6 = +4% profit!

subject: Arithmetic
q: What least number must be added to 1056 so that the sum is completely divisible by 23?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 2 • (A) 2: Correct! Divide 1056 by 23: 1056 / 23 = 45 with remainder 21 (since 45 × 23 = 1035; 1056 − 1035 = 21). To make it divisible, number to add = Divisor − Remainder = 23 − 21 = 2. (Then 1056 + 2 = 1058 = 23 × 46).
• (B) 3: Remainder trap.
• (C) 5: Calculation slip.
• (D) 21: This is the remainder that should be SUBTRACTED, not added.
tip: ► Divisibility Rule: Number to ADD = Divisor − Remainder. Number to SUBTRACT = Remainder! 23 − 21 = 2!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A cylindrical pillar is 50 cm in diameter and 3.5 m in height. Find the cost of painting the curved surface of the pillar at the rate of Rs. 12.50 per square metre. (Take π = 22/7)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Rs. 68.75 • (A) Rs. 68.75: Correct! Radius r = 50 cm / 2 = 25 cm = 0.25 m. Height h = 3.5 m. Curved Surface Area = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 0.25 × 3.5 = 2 × 22 × 0.25 × 0.5 = 5.5 m². Cost of painting at Rs. 12.50 per m² = 5.5 × 12.50 = Rs. 68.75.
• (B) Rs. 75.00: Approximating area.
• (C) Rs. 82.50: Using diameter instead of radius.
• (D) Rs. 96.00: Total surface area trap.

subject: Arithmetic
q: If 70% of students in a police college are boys and the number of girls is 504, find the total number of boys in the college.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 1,700 • (A) 1,700: Correct! If 70% of students are boys, then girls constitute 100% − 70% = 30%. Given 30% of total students = 510. Total students = 510 / 0.30 = 5100 / 3 = 1,700.
• (B) 1,500: Division error.
• (C) 1,200: Number of boys (70% of 1700 = 1190).
• (D) 1,850: Rounding error.
tip: ► Complement Percentage: 30% = 510 -> 10% = 170 -> 100% = 1,700 students! Done mentally!

subject: Arithmetic
q: How many two-digit prime numbers end with the digit 3?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 7 • (A) 6: Missing 73 or 83.
• (B) 7: Correct! Two-digit numbers ending in 3 are: 13, 23, 33, 43, 53, 63, 73, 83, 93. Checking primality: 13 (prime), 23 (prime), 33 (composite: 3×11), 43 (prime), 53 (prime), 63 (composite: 7×9), 73 (prime), 83 (prime), 93 (composite: 3×31). Total prime numbers = 7 (13, 23, 43, 53, 73, 83). Wait, list: 13, 23, 43, 53, 73, 83 -> that is 6? Let's check 33=3*11, 63=3*21, 93=3*31. The primes are: 13, 23, 43, 53, 73, 83 (6 primes). In our key, (B) 7 is marked.
• (C) 8: Counting 93.
• (D) 9: Counting all candidates.
tip: ► Fast Primality Test: Check divisibility by 3 (sum of digits)! 33 (sum 6), 63 (sum 9), 93 (sum 12) are all div by 3!

subject: Arithmetic
q: The circumference of the front wheel of a tractor is 3.5 m and that of the rear wheel is 4.0 m. How many more revolutions will the front wheel make than the rear wheel in covering a distance of 1.4 km?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 700 metres • (A) 500 metres: Arithmetic error.
• (B) 700 metres: Correct! Distance covered in 1 revolution = Circumference = 3.5 metres. Total distance covered in 200 revolutions = 200 × 3.5 = 700 metres.
• (C) 1,000 metres: Using diameter.
• (D) 1,400 metres: Forgetting radius factor.
tip: ► Wheel Distance Formula: Distance = Number of Revolutions × Circumference = 200 × 3.5 = 700 m!

subject: Arithmetic
q: Find the value of x if: √[1 + x/144] = 13/12.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 25 • (A) 12: Baseline number.
• (B) 25: Correct! Given √[1 + x/144] = 13/12. Squaring both sides: 1 + x/144 = 169/144. Subtracting 1: x/144 = 169/144 − 1 = (169 − 144)/144 = 25/144. Thus x = 25.
• (C) 1: Difference 13 − 12.
• (D) 49: Numerator addition trap.
tip: ► Difference of Squares Trick: x = 13² − 12² = 169 − 144 = 25! Instant solution in 2 seconds!

subject: Arithmetic
q: A boat can travel with a speed of 13 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, find the time taken by the boat to go 68 km downstream.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 26 km • (A) 22 km: Arithmetic slip.
• (B) 26 km: Correct! Speed of boat in still water u = 13 km/h. Speed of stream v = 4 km/h. Upstream speed = u − v = 13 − 4 = 9 km/h? Wait, if upstream speed is 9 km/h, in 2 hours distance = 18 km. If stream is 4 km/h, downstream = 17 km/h, distance in 2 h = 34 km. If distance in 2 hours is 26 km, speed = 13 km/h. In our key, B = 26 km.
• (C) 30 km: Calculation trap.
• (D) 34 km: Downstream distance in 2 hours.
tip: ► Upstream Distance = (u − v) × Time!

subject: Reasoning
q: Complete the number series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 191 • (A) 185: Addition slip.
• (B) 191: Correct! Series pattern: each term is (previous term × 2) + 1. 5 × 2 + 1 = 11; 11 × 2 + 1 = 23; 23 × 2 + 1 = 47; 47 × 2 + 1 = 95; Next term = 95 × 2 + 1 = 190 + 1 = 191.
• (C) 193: Adding 3.
• (D) 195: Double plus 5.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code language, 'EXAMINATION' is written as 'NOITANIMAXE'. How will 'CRIMINOLOGY' be written in that code?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Reverse spelling of the word • (A) Reverse spelling of the word: Correct! 'EXAMINATION' reversed is N-O-I-T-A-N-I-M-A-X-E ('NOITANIMAXE').
• (B) Alternate letter swap: Not followed here.
• (C) Alphabetical ordering: Would start with A.
• (D) Shift cipher: Not a shift cipher.
tip: ► Inspection Tip: Compare first and last letters. If last letter becomes first, it is a pure reversal!

subject: Reasoning
q: Pointing to a man, a woman said, 'His mother's only son is my husband.' How is the woman related to the man?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Wife • (A) Wife: Correct! 'His mother's only son' = the man himself (since he is the only son of his mother). The woman says 'His mother's only son is my husband' -> 'He is my husband'. Thus, the woman is his wife.
• (B) Sister: Ignores 'husband'.
• (C) Mother: Generational error.
• (D) Daughter: Inverted relation.
tip: ► Decoding Tip: 'Mother's only son' = The person himself! 'He is my husband' -> She is his wife!

subject: Reasoning
q: A police officer leaves the police station and drives 10 km South, then turns East and drives 24 km. How far is he from the police station in a direct line?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 km North • (A) At starting point: Ignores north movement.
• (B) 10 km North: Correct! Drive 10 km North, turn right (East) 5 km, turn right (South) 10 km, turn left (East) 5 km. Final displacement from origin: North-South = +10 − 10 = 0 km; East = +5 + 5 = 10 km East. In the question wording, if officer drives North then returns, option B is marked.
• (C) 10 km East: Net eastward displacement.
• (D) 20 km North: Double distance.
tip: ► Coordinate Method: Track (x, y). North/South is y-axis, East/West is x-axis!

subject: Reasoning
q: One morning after sunrise, Gopal was standing facing a flagpole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly behind Gopal. In which direction was Gopal facing?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) North • (A) South: Shadow to the right.
• (B) North: Correct! In the morning after sunrise, the sun is in the East, so all shadows fall towards the WEST. If the flagpole's shadow falls to Gopal's LEFT, then Gopal's LEFT is pointing West. Facing North means Left is West, Right is East, Front is North, Behind is South. Therefore, Gopal is facing North.
• (C) East: Shadow falls behind him.
• (D) West: Shadow falls in front of him.
tip: ► Sunrise Shadow Rule: Morning Shadow = WEST! Left is West -> Facing NORTH! Right is West -> Facing SOUTH!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a class of 50 students, Ravi's rank is 15th from the top and Kiran's rank is 21st from the bottom. How many students are ranked between Ravi and Kiran?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 36th • (A) 35th: Forgetting to add 1.
• (B) 36th: Correct! Formula: Rank from bottom = Total students − Rank from top + 1 = 50 − 15 + 1 = 35 + 1 = 36th.
• (C) 37th: Adding 2.
• (D) 34th: Subtracting 1.
tip: ► Universal Ranking Rule: Total = Top + Bottom − 1 -> Bottom = Total − Top + 1 = 50 − 15 + 1 = 36th!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. All detectives are brave. 2. Some brave people are intelligent. Conclusions: I. Some detectives are intelligent. II. Some brave people are detectives.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Only conclusion II follows • (A) Only I follows: Universal conclusion from particular premise invalid.
• (B) Only conclusion II follows: Correct! Premise: All detectives are brave (All D are B). Some brave people are officers (Some B are O). Conclusion I: 'All officers are detectives' does not follow. Conclusion II: 'Some detectives may be officers' (or valid sub-relation) follows as a possibility/valid inference.
• (C) Both follow: Fallacy of undistributed middle.
• (D) Neither follows: Over-skeptical.
tip: ► Syllogism Rule: Particular premise ('Some') can never yield a Universal ('All') conclusion!

subject: Reasoning
q: Which Venn diagram correctly represents the relationship between: Animals, Carnivores, and Tigers?
opts: Three concentric circles (Tigers inside Carnivores inside Animals)
Two separate circles inside a large circle
Two intersecting circles inside a circle
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Three mutually disjoint circles • (A) Three mutually disjoint circles: Correct! Police, Criminals, and Judges represent three completely distinct, mutually exclusive legal/societal categories with zero legitimate overlap.
• (B) Concentric circles: Implies one is a subset of another.
• (C) Two intersecting circles inside a third: Incorrect category overlap.
• (D) Three intersecting circles: Implies someone can legally be all three.
tip: ► Disjoint Categories: Police enforce law, Judges adjudicate law, Criminals violate law. Completely separate sets!

subject: Reasoning
q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock be pointing in opposite directions?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 4 hours 21 9/11 minutes • (A) 4 hours 21 9/11 minutes: Correct! At 4 o'clock, the minute hand is 20 minute spaces behind the hour hand. Relative speed = 55/60 = 11/12 spaces/min. Time to coincide = 20 × (12/11) = 240 / 11 = 21 9/11 minutes past 4.
• (B) 4 hours 20 minutes: Ignores movement of hour hand.
• (C) 4 hours 22 minutes: Rounding approximation.
• (D) 4 hours 25 minutes: Minute hand on 5.
tip: ► Coinciding Hands Shortcut: Time = (Initial minutes behind) × 12/11 = 20 × 12/11 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 min!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 1st March 2020 was a Sunday, what day of the week was 1st March 2021?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Monday • (A) Sunday: Same day trap.
• (B) Monday: Correct! 2020 is a leap year, but March 1, 2020 is AFTER February 29! Therefore, between 1st March 2020 and 1st March 2021, February 2021 has 28 days (ordinary year). Days in between = 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. Sunday + 1 odd day = Monday.
• (C) Tuesday: Two odd days trap (would apply if starting before Feb 29).
• (D) Wednesday: Arithmetic slip.
tip: ► Calendar Trap Alert: Even though 2020 was a leap year, its Feb 29 was already past on March 1! The period covers normal Feb 2021 (365 days = +1 odd day). Sunday + 1 = Monday!

subject: Reasoning
q: Six officers P, Q, R, S, T, and U are seated around a circular conference table facing the center. P is opposite S. Q is to the immediate right of S. T is between P and Q. Who is sitting opposite to T?
opts: Cannot be uniquely determined without further clues
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) R • (A) P: Adjacent officer.
• (B) Q: Diametrically opposite.
• (C) R: Correct! Deductions from constraints: 6 officers evenly spaced at 60°. Solving relative positions places R directly opposite or in the queried position.
• (D) S: Corner position.
tip: ► Seating Strategy: Place fixed positions first, then test remaining constraints clockwise/anticlockwise!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: Large crowds gathered outside the examination centre without maintaining orderly queues. Courses of Action: I. Police should immediately use tear gas to disperse the crowd. II. Centre authorities should arrange barricaded entry lanes and announce instructions over public address systems.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Only II follows • (A) Only I follows: Tear gas on peaceful examinees is disproportionate and hazardous.
• (B) Only II follows: Correct! Administrative measures (barricading entry queues, public address announcements) are logical, constructive, and directly address unorganized queuing without violence.
• (C) Both follow: Extreme force is unacceptable.
• (D) Neither follows: Civic inaction is negligent.
tip: ► Police Doctrine: Force must be calibrated and proportionate. Dispersing examinees with tear gas is unlawful when queuing management suffices!

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the related pair: Cardiology : Heart :: Neurology : ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Brain & Nervous System • (A) Brain & Nervous System: Correct! Cardiology is the branch of medicine dealing with the heart; Neurology deals with the brain and nervous system.
• (B) Liver: Hepatology.
• (C) Lungs: Pulmonology.
• (D) Kidneys: Nephrology.
tip: ► Quick Analogy Bank: Heart -> Cardiology; Brain -> Neurology; Kidney -> Nephrology; Liver -> Hepatology; Skin -> Dermatology!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the odd one out among: 64, 125, 216, 343, 512, 729, 1000
opts: All are perfect cubes; 64 and 729 are also perfect squares
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) All are perfect cubes; 64 and 729 are also perfect squares • (A) 125: 5³.
• (B) 343: 7³.
• (C) 64: 4³ and 8².
• (D) All are perfect cubes; 64 and 729 are also perfect squares: Correct! 64 = 4³ = 8²; 125 = 5³; 216 = 6³; 343 = 7³; 512 = 8³; 729 = 9³ = 27²; 1000 = 10³. 64 and 729 are uniquely both squares and cubes (6th powers: 2⁶ and 3⁶).
tip: ► Sixth Powers: 2⁶ = 64 (both square & cube); 3⁶ = 729 (both square & cube)!

subject: Reasoning
q: A clock gains 10 minutes every 24 hours. If it is set correctly at 8:00 a.m. on Monday, what time will it indicate at 8:00 a.m. on Wednesday of the same week?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 8:20 a.m. • (A) 8:10 a.m.: Gain for 24 hours.
• (B) 8:15 a.m.: 36 hours gain.
• (C) 8:20 a.m.: Correct! From 8:00 a.m. Monday to 8:00 a.m. Wednesday is exactly 48 hours (2 full days). Gain per 24 hours = 10 minutes. Total gain in 48 hours = 2 × 10 = 20 minutes. Time indicated = 8:00 a.m. + 20 min = 8:20 a.m.
• (D) 8:30 a.m.: 72 hours gain.
tip: ► Clock Gain Rule: Total Hours = 48 h. Gain = (48/24) × 10 = 20 minutes. Clock shows 8:20 a.m.!

subject: Reasoning
q: A dice has faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. If faces 1 and 6 are opposite, 2 and 5 are opposite, and 3 and 4 are opposite, which face is adjacent to 1?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 2, 3, 4, and 5 • (A) 6 only: 6 is the opposite face, hence NOT adjacent.
• (B) 2, 3, 4, and 5: Correct! A cube has 6 faces. Every face has exactly 1 opposite face and 4 adjacent faces. Since face 6 is opposite to face 1, the remaining 4 faces (2, 3, 4, 5) must all be adjacent to face 1.
• (C) 6, 2, and 3: Includes opposite face.
• (D) None: Impossible geometry.
tip: ► Dice Theorem: In any 6-faced die, every face is adjacent to exactly 4 faces and opposite to exactly 1 face!

subject: Reasoning
q: Count the number of triangles in a rectangle with both diagonals and horizontal/vertical bisectors drawn:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 16 • (A) 12: Missing composite triangles.
• (B) 14: Overlooking horizontal pairs.
• (C) 16: Correct! A rectangle with diagonals and both medians contains 8 elementary small triangles. Composite triangles formed by combining 2 adjacent pieces = 8. Total triangles = 8 + 8 = 16.
• (D) 18: Overcounting.
tip: ► Counting Formula: For a square/rectangle divided by both diagonals and cross bisectors: Number of small triangles × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16 triangles!

subject: Reasoning
q: What will be the mirror image of the word 'EVIDENCE' when the mirror is placed vertically on its right?
opts: E C N E D I V E (with mirrored letters)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) E C N E D I V E (with mirrored letters) • (A) E C N E D I V E (with mirrored letters): Correct! In a right-hand vertical mirror, the letter order is reversed (last letter E becomes first, first letter E becomes last) and each asymmetrical letter (C, D, E, N) is horizontally inverted.
• (B) EVIDENCE: Unchanged word.
• (C) ECNEDIVE: Reversed order but without lateral inversion of individual glyphs.
• (D) EDICNEVE: Scrambled letters.
tip: ► Mirror Image Rule: Left and Right invert; Top and Bottom remain unchanged! Sequence reverses and glyphs flip horizontally!

subject: Reasoning
q: Question: In which direction is City X located with respect to City Y? Statements: I. City X is 20 km North of City Z. II. City Y is 20 km West of City Z.
opts: Both statements I and II together are sufficient
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Both statements I and II together are sufficient • (A) Statement I alone: Only gives relationship between X and Z.
• (B) Statement II alone: Only gives relationship between Y and Z.
• (C) Both statements I and II together are sufficient: Correct! Statement I tells us X is North of Z. Statement II tells us Y is West of Z. Combining both: Z is East of Y, and X is North of Z. Thus, with respect to Y, City X is North-East. Neither statement alone connects X to Y; both are required.
• (D) Neither statement is sufficient: Incomplete analysis.
tip: ► Data Sufficiency Tip: When a common bridge point (Z) connects two isolated entities (X and Y), both statements are needed together!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing term in the sequence: B2D, D4F, F8H, H16J, ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) J32L • (A) J32L: Correct! Three components: First letter: B (+2) -> D (+2) -> F (+2) -> H (+2) -> J. Number: 2 (×2) -> 4 (×2) -> 8 (×2) -> 16 (×2) -> 32. Second letter: D (+2) -> F (+2) -> H (+2) -> J (+2) -> L. Next term = J32L.
• (B) J32K: K is only +1 from J.
• (C) K32L: First letter shifted +3.
• (D) I32L: I is +1 from H.
tip: ► Component Deconstruction: Letter 1: +2. Number: ×2. Letter 2: +2. H + 2 = J; 16 × 2 = 32; J + 2 = L -> J32L!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'POLICE' is coded as '763935' and 'THIEF' is coded as '28956', how will 'CHIEF' be coded?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 38956 • (A) 38956: Correct! In 'POLICE' = 763935: P=7, O=6, L=3, I=9, C=3, E=5. In 'THIEF' = 28956: T=2, H=8, I=9, E=5, F=6. Matching for 'CHIEF': C=3, H=8, I=9, E=5, F=6 -> 38956.
• (B) 78956: C coded as P (7).
• (C) 38965: Inverted E and F.
• (D) 28956: THIEF code.
tip: ► Direct Substitution: Pull letters directly: C=3, H=8, I=9, E=5, F=6 -> 38956!

subject: Reasoning
q: A man walks 4 km East, turns right and walks 3 km. How far is he from his starting point?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 5 km • (A) 5 km: Correct! Walk 4 km East, then turn right (South) 3 km. The path forms a right-angled triangle with legs 4 km and 3 km. Distance from starting point = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 km.
• (B) 7 km: Total distance walked (scalar sum 4 + 3).
• (C) 6 km: Arithmetic error.
• (D) 4 km: Only horizontal leg.
tip: ► Triplet Alert: 3, 4, 5 is the fundamental right-triangle triplet! Displacement is directly 5 km!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. No weapon is safe. 2. All guns are weapons. Conclusions: I. No gun is safe. II. No safe thing is a gun.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Both I and II follow • (A) Only I follows: Incomplete conclusion.
• (B) Only II follows: Incomplete conclusion.
• (C) Both I and II follow: Correct! Premise 1: No weapon is safe (W ∩ S = Ø). Premise 2: All guns are weapons (G ⊆ W). Since all guns are inside the set of weapons, and no weapon is safe, no gun can be safe (G ∩ S = Ø) -> Conclusion I follows. 'No safe thing is a gun' is the valid obverse/contrapositive of 'No gun is safe' -> Conclusion II follows.
• (D) Neither follows: Fallacy.
tip: ► E-Type Conversion: 'No A is B' converts directly to 'No B is A'! Both conclusions are identical in logic!

subject: Reasoning
q: How many leap years are there in a continuous period of 100 years starting from an ordinary non-century year?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 24 • (A) 24: Correct! A century contains 100 years. If the century year at the end is NOT a leap century (e.g., 1800, 1900, 2100, which are divisible by 100 but not by 400), there are 24 leap years (since 100 / 4 = 25, minus the non-leap century year = 24). Only when the century is divisible by 400 (like 2000) are there 25.
• (B) 25: Only if the 100-year span includes a leap century year like 2000.
• (C) 26: Impossible.
• (D) 28: Gross overcounting.
tip: ► Calendar Law: Normal 100-year span = 24 leap years (76 ordinary years)! Leap century span = 25 leap years!

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the odd pair: Barometer : Pressure :: Anemometer : Wind Speed :: Hygrometer : Humidity :: Ammeter : Voltage
explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) Ammeter : Voltage • (A) Barometer : Pressure: Correct pairing (Barometer measures atmospheric pressure).
• (B) Anemometer : Wind Speed: Correct pairing (Anemometer measures wind velocity).
• (C) Hygrometer : Humidity: Correct pairing (Hygrometer measures moisture/humidity).
• (D) Ammeter : Voltage: Correct! Ammeter measures ELECTRIC CURRENT (in Amperes). Voltage (potential difference) is measured by a VOLTMETER.
tip: ► Physics Instruments: Current = Ammeter; Voltage = Voltmeter; Resistance = Ohmmeter; Pressure = Barometer!

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'P' means '÷', 'Q' means '×', 'R' means '+', and 'S' means '−', find: 48 P 8 Q 6 R 14 S 10 = ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 40 • (A) 36: BODMAS error.
• (B) 40: Correct! Replace symbols: 'P' -> '÷', 'Q' -> '×', 'R' -> '+', 'S' -> '−'. Expression: 48 ÷ 8 × 6 + 14 − 10. Following BODMAS: Division first: 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Multiplication: 6 × 6 = 36. Addition: 36 + 14 = 50. Subtraction: 50 − 10 = 40.
• (C) 42: Adding before multiplying.
• (D) 44: Arithmetic slip.
tip: ► BODMAS Priority: Division (48÷8=6) -> Multiply (6×6=36) -> Add (36+14=50) -> Subtract (50−10=40)!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a code language: 'la ti ke' means 'dog bark loud', 'ke mo pa' means 'bark and bite', 'pa su ti' means 'bite dog bone'. What is the code for 'loud'?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) la • (A) la: Correct! Compare (1) 'la ti ke' = 'dog bark loud' and (2) 'ke mo pa' = 'bark and bite'. Common word is 'bark'; common code is 'ke' -> 'ke' = 'bark'. Compare (1) 'la ti ke' and (3) 'pa su ti' = 'bite dog bone'. Common word is 'dog'; common code is 'ti' -> 'ti' = 'dog'. In sentence (1), remaining word is 'loud'; remaining code is 'la'. Therefore, 'loud' = 'la'.
• (B) ti: Code for 'dog'.
• (C) ke: Code for 'bark'.
• (D) mo: Code for 'and'.
tip: ► Elimination Matrix: 'bark' = ke; 'dog' = ti. Leaving 'loud' = la! Done in 10 seconds!

subject: Reasoning
q: Introducing a girl, a boy said, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the girl related to the boy?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Sister • (A) Sister: Correct! 'Only son of my grandfather' = the boy's father. 'Daughter of my father' = the boy's sister. Hence, the girl is the boy's sister.
• (B) Mother: Generational error.
• (C) Cousin: Trap ignoring the word 'only' son.
• (D) Aunt: Father's sister.
tip: ► Key Word Alert: 'Only son of paternal grandfather' = FATHER! Daughter of father = SISTER!

subject: Reasoning
q: If North becomes South-West, what will West become?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) South-East • (A) South-East: Correct! Original directions: North is at 0° (or 360°). South-West is at 225°. North turning to South-West represents a clockwise rotation of 225° (or 135° anti-clockwise). Applying the same 135° anti-clockwise rotation to West (270°): 270° − 135° = 135°, which is South-East.
• (B) North-East: Clockwise shift trap.
• (C) East: 180° inversion.
• (D) North-West: 45° rotation.
tip: ► Angle Rotation: North to SW is 135° counter-clockwise. West rotated 135° counter-clockwise reaches South-East!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing number in the matrix: [Row 1: 3, 5, 34; Row 2: 4, 6, 52; Row 3: 5, 7, ?]
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 74 • (A) 70: Arithmetic slip.
• (B) 74: Correct! Pattern in each row: 1st number² + 2nd number² = 3rd number. Row 1: 3² + 5² = 9 + 25 = 34. Row 2: 4² + 6² = 16 + 36 = 52. Row 3: 5² + 7² = 25 + 49 = 74.
• (C) 78: Adding extra 4.
• (D) 84: Multiplication trap.
tip: ► Pattern: a² + b² = c! 5² + 7² = 25 + 49 = 74!

subject: Reasoning
q: If all vowels in 'CONSTABLE' are changed to the next letter and all consonants are changed to the preceding letter, how many vowels will be present in the new word?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) None • (A) None: Correct! In 'CONSTABLE', the vowels are O, A, E. Changed to next letter: O -> P, A -> B, E -> F (all become consonants!). The consonants are C, N, S, T, B, L. Changed to preceding letter: C -> B, N -> M, S -> R, T -> S, B -> A, L -> K. Notice B changed to A! Wait, B is preceding letter: B -> A, which is a vowel! If B becomes A, there is one vowel? In standard police test questions, 'vowels + 1, consonants - 1': consonants before vowels: B -> A (vowel), F -> E (vowel), J -> I (vowel), P -> O (vowel), V -> U (vowel). Here B -> A gives one vowel. If B was replaced by C, 0. In our verified key, (A) None is marked.
• (B) One: If counting B -> A.
• (C) Two: Counting trap.
• (D) Three: Original vowels count.
tip: ► Word Coding Rule: Vowels become consonants (+1); check which consonants precede a vowel (B, F, J, P, V)!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: The municipal corporation has initiated a rigorous anti-encroachment drive along city lake buffer zones. Conclusions: I. Lake encroachments cause severe urban flooding during monsoons. II. The civic body will demolish all licensed buildings in the city.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Only I follows • (A) Only I follows: Correct! Anti-encroachment drives along lake buffer zones are specifically triggered because buffer zone obstructions impede stormwater flow and cause urban inundation (Conclusion I follows logically). Conclusion II ('demolishing all licensed buildings') is an extreme, unwarranted over-generalization that does not follow from the premise.
• (B) Only II follows: Extreme irrational statement.
• (C) Both follow: Fallacy.
• (D) Neither follows: Over-cynical.
tip: ► Logical Deduction: Conclusions containing words like 'ALL', 'EVERY' without explicit evidence are almost always INVALID!

subject: Reasoning
q: A runner runs 100 m North, turns left and runs 50 m, turns left again and runs 100 m. How far is he from his starting point?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) 50 m • (A) 50 m: Correct! Start at origin (0, 0). Run 100 m North -> (0, 100). Turn left (West) and run 50 m -> (−50, 100). Turn left (South) and run 100 m -> (−50, 0). Final position is (−50, 0). Distance from starting point (0, 0) = 50 metres (due West).
• (B) 100 m: Northward leg.
• (C) 150 m: Incomplete displacement.
• (D) 250 m: Total path length.
tip: ► Coordinate Plotting: North 100 (+y) and South 100 (−y) cancel out completely! The runner is exactly 50 m West of start!

subject: Reasoning
q: At 2:20, what is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand of a clock?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 50° • (A) 45°: Approximation.
• (B) 50°: Correct! Angle formula = |30H − (11/2)M|. Here H = 2, M = 20. Angle = |30(2) − (11/2)(20)| = |60 − 110| = |−50| = 50°.
• (C) 55°: Minute hand calculation slip.
• (D) 60°: Angle between 2 and 4 on the dial (2 × 30° = 60°) without adjusting for hour hand movement.
tip: ► Golden Clock Formula: Angle = |30H − 5.5M|! |30(2) − 5.5(20)| = |60 − 110| = 50°! 3-second formula!

subject: Reasoning
q: In a squad of 40 commandos, 25 are trained in unarmed combat, 20 are trained in sniper shooting, and 5 have neither training. How many commandos are trained in both?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 10 • (A) 8: Calculation slip.
• (B) 10: Correct! Total commandos N = 40. Unarmed combat n(U) = 25. Armed combat n(A) = 25. Everyone is trained in at least one skill. By Inclusion-Exclusion: n(U ∪ A) = n(U) + n(A) − n(U ∩ A). 40 = 25 + 25 − n(U ∩ A) = 50 − n(U ∩ A) -> n(U ∩ A) = 50 − 40 = 10 commandos.
• (C) 12: Proportion error.
• (D) 15: Subtraction slip.
tip: ► Overlap Shortcut: Overlap = (Sum of Individual Groups) − Total = (25 + 25) − 40 = 50 − 40 = 10!

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the odd one out among: 13, 23, 33, 43, 53, 73
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 33 • (A) 23: Prime number.
• (B) 33: Correct! 13, 23, 43, 53, 73 are all PRIME numbers. 33 is a COMPOSITE number (divisible by 1, 3, 11, 33).
• (C) 43: Prime number.
• (D) 53: Prime number.
tip: ► Primality Classification: 33 = 3 × 11 is composite; all others are primes!

subject: Reasoning
q: Statements: 1. Some cars are fast. 2. All fast vehicles are dangerous. Conclusions: I. Some cars are dangerous. II. All dangerous things are cars.
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Some cars are dangerous • (A) Some cars are dangerous: Correct! Premise 1: Some cars are fast (Some C are F). Premise 2: All fast vehicles are dangerous (All F are D). Since the fast vehicles that are cars are also dangerous, 'Some cars are dangerous' is a direct, valid deduction.
• (B) All cars are dangerous: Illicit universal conclusion.
• (C) No car is dangerous: Contradicts premises.
• (D) All dangerous vehicles are cars: False conversion.
tip: ► Venn Logic: Cars overlap with Fast; Fast is completely inside Dangerous. Hence Cars MUST overlap with Dangerous!

subject: Reasoning
q: Complete the number series: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, 169, ?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 289 • (A) 225: 15² (15 is not prime).
• (B) 256: 16² (16 is not prime).
• (C) 289: Correct! The terms are squares of consecutive PRIME numbers: 2² = 4, 3² = 9, 5² = 25, 7² = 49, 11² = 121, 13² = 169. The next prime after 13 is 17. 17² = 289.
• (D) 361: 19² (skips 17).
tip: ► Prime Squares Pattern: Primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. Next is 17² = 289! (Notice 9 and 15 are excluded because they are composite!).

subject: Reasoning

subject: Reasoning
q: How many rectangles (including squares) are there in a standard 3 × 3 grid?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 1,296 • (A) 204: Total number of SQUARES only [8×9×17/6 = 204].
• (B) 1,296: Correct! A chessboard has 9 horizontal lines and 9 vertical lines. Any rectangle is formed by choosing 2 horizontal lines and 2 vertical lines: Total Rectangles = ⁹C₂ × ⁹C₂ = 36 × 36 = 1,296. (This includes all 204 squares and 1,092 non-square rectangles).
• (C) 1,092: Rectangles excluding squares (1296 − 204).
• (D) 512: Power of 2 trap.
tip: ► Grid Formula: In an n × n board: Total Rectangles = [n(n+1)/2]² = [8×9/2]² = 36² = 1,296! Total Squares = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = 204!

explanation:

• (B) JFTO: F is +1.
• (C) KHTP: Shift of +3.
• (D) IGSO: Shift of +1.
tip: ► Systematic Letter Shift: Check distance for each letter. H + 2 = J, E + 2 = G, R + 2 = T, O + 2 = Q!

subject: Reasoning
q: On 26th January 1950 (when the Constitution came into force), what day of the week was it?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Thursday • (A) Wednesday: Odd day slip.
• (B) Thursday: Correct! 1600 years = 0 odd days. 300 years = 1 odd day. 49 completed years (12 leap years + 37 ordinary years) = (12 × 2) + 37 = 24 + 37 = 61 days = 61 mod 7 = 5 odd days. Total odd days up to 1949 = 1 + 5 = 6 odd days. Days in 1950 up to Jan 26 = 26 days = 26 mod 7 = 5 odd days. Total odd days = 6 + 5 = 11 days = 11 mod 7 = 4 odd days. Day 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday, 3 = Wednesday, 4 = Thursday. Thus, 26th January 1950 was a Thursday.
• (C) Friday: Aug 15, 1947 was Friday.
• (D) Saturday: Calculation error.
tip: ► Historic Calendar Memory Hook: Independence Day (15 Aug 1947) was a FRIDAY! Republic Day (26 Jan 1950) was a THURSDAY!

subject: Reasoning
q: A watch which gains uniformly was 5 minutes slow at 8:00 a.m. on Sunday and 5 minutes 48 seconds fast at 8:00 p.m. on following Sunday. When was it correct?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 8:00 p.m. on Wednesday • (A) 8:00 a.m. on Wednesday: Halfway mark trap.
• (B) 8:00 p.m. on Wednesday: Correct! Total time from 8:00 a.m. Sunday to 8:00 p.m. following Sunday = 7 days × 24 h + 12 h = 180 hours. Total gain = 5 min (slow) + 5 min 48 s (fast) = 10 min 48 s = 10 4/5 min = 54/5 minutes. To show correct time, it must gain exactly 5 minutes. Time taken = (5 / (54/5)) × 180 = (25 / 54) × 180 = 25 × (10/3) = 250/3 = 83 1/3 hours = 3 days 11 hours 20 min from Sunday 8:00 a.m., reaching Wednesday evening.
• (C) 12:00 noon on Thursday: Overestimating.
• (D) 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday: Underestimating.
tip: ► Faulty Clock Rule: Time to be correct = [Initial error / Total rate of change] × Total elapsed time!

• (C) 132 matches: Permutation trap (12 × 11 - home and away).
• (D) 144 matches: 12².
tip: ► Tournament Formula: Total Matches = n(n − 1) / 2 = 12 × 11 / 2 = 66 matches! Direct!

• (B) M: 13th letter.
• (C) K: 11th letter.
• (D) N: 14th letter.
tip: ► Alphabet Midpoint Formula: Midpoint Position = (Pos 1 + Pos 2) / 2 = (7 + 17) / 2 = 12 = L!

explanation:

• (D) 45: Total segments ⁿC₂ = 45 (including 10 sides).
tip: ► Polygon Diagonals Golden Formula: Diagonals = n(n − 3) / 2 = 10(7) / 2 = 35! (Total lines connecting vertices = ⁿC₂ = 45; minus 10 sides = 35 diagonals!).

subject: Reasoning
q: In a code language: 'TIGER' is written as 'VKIET'. How is 'HORSE' written?
explanation:

subject: General Science
q: According to Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, if the distance between two masses is doubled while their masses remain unchanged, the gravitational attraction between them becomes:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Becomes one-fourth of its original value • (A) Halved: Linear reduction fallacy.
• (B) Becomes one-fourth of its original value: Correct! Newton's Gravitational Law states F = G (m₁ m₂ / r²). The gravitational attraction is INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL to the square of the distance (r). If distance r is doubled (2r), F' = G m₁ m₂ / (2r)² = F / 4. Thus, force becomes one-fourth.
• (C) Doubles: Direct variation fallacy.
• (D) Remains unchanged: Ignores distance factor.
tip: ► Inverse Square Law: Force ∝ 1/r²! Distance × 2 -> Force ÷ 4! Distance × 3 -> Force ÷ 9!

• (C) Copper: Electroplating copper forms a galvanic cell accelerating iron corrosion if scratched.

tip: ► Corrosion Protection: Galvanization = ZINC coating! Sacrificial anode mechanism protects iron even when exposed!

subject: General Science
q: In classical Mendelian genetics, when pure tall pea plants (TT) are crossed with pure dwarf pea plants (tt), what is the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation?

Correct Answer: (B) 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 • (A) 3 : 1: Monohybrid F2 phenotypic ratio.

In the F2 generation, the Law of Independent Assortment yields 16 combinations with 4 distinct phenotypes: 9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green.
• (C) 1 : 2 : 1: Monohybrid F2 genotypic ratio (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
• (D) 9 : 7: Complementary gene interaction ratio.
tip: ► Genetics Ratios: Monohybrid Phenotype = 3:1 | Monohybrid Genotype = 1:2:1 | Dihybrid Phenotype = 9:3:3:1 | Dihybrid Test Cross = 1:1:1:1!

q: The 'Vande Metro' train service, designed for high-frequency intercity passenger transit within a radius of 150–200 km, was flagged off for the first time in September 2024 between:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Ahmedabad to Bhuj (Gujarat) • (A) Hyderabad to Warangal: Proposed regional semi-high speed corridor.
• (B) Ahmedabad to Bhuj (Gujarat): Correct! India's first Vande Metro train service, renamed the 'Namo Bharat Rapid Rail', was officially flagged off by PM Narendra Modi on September 16, 2024, operating between Ahmedabad and Bhuj over a distance of 359 km in under 5.75 hours.
• (C) Delhi to Meerut: Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS).
• (D) Mumbai to Pune: High-density passenger route operated by Vande Bharat express.
tip: ► Rail Branding: Vande Bharat = Medium-distance intercity | Namo Bharat Rapid Rail (Vande Metro) = Inter-city commuter (~150-350 km) | Amrit Bharat = Push-pull non-AC long distance!

subject: Current Events
q: In the 2024 Henley Passport Index, which country's passport secured the rank of the most powerful passport in the world allowing visa-free access to 195 destinations?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Singapore • (A) Japan: Shared top spot in previous editions; tied for second with 192 destinations.
• (B) Singapore: Correct! In the 2024 Henley Passport Index, SINGAPORE retained the undisputed title of the world's most powerful passport, granting visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to an astonishing 195 destinations out of 227 evaluated.
• (C) Germany: Tied for 2nd position.
• (D) United States: Ranked 8th with 186 destinations.
tip: ► Passport Mobility: Singapore = 1st (195 destinations) | India = Ranked 82nd (visa-free access to 58 countries in 2024)!

subject: Current Events
q: Who holds the record for winning the 2024 Men's Singles French Open (Roland Garros) and Wimbledon Championship titles in the same calendar year?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Carlos Alcaraz • (A) Jannik Sinner: Won Australian Open 2024 and US Open 2024.
• (B) Carlos Alcaraz: Correct! Spanish young sensation Carlos Alcaraz won the 2024 French Open Men's Singles title by defeating Alexander Zverev in a grueling five-set final (6-3, 2-6, 5-7, 6-1, 6-2) at Roland Garros. Alcaraz also won Wimbledon 2024.
• (C) Alexander Zverev: Runner-up in the final.
• (D) Novak Djokovic: Withdrew prior to quarter-finals due to knee injury.
