subject: Indian History
q: The prehistoric rock shelters of Bhimbetka, celebrated for their Upper Paleolithic and Mesolithic cave paintings of animals and hunting scenes, were discovered in 1957 by archaeologist:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh • (A) Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh: Famous for Belan Valley prehistoric rock art sites.
• (B) Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh: Correct! The Bhimbetka Rock Shelters, discovered in 1957 by archaeologist Dr. V.S. Wakankar, are situated in Raisen district at the foothills of the Vindhyan Mountains in Madhya Pradesh. Exhibiting rock paintings from Upper Paleolithic through Mesolithic to Chalcolithic eras, Bhimbetka was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
• (C) Hampi, Karnataka: Vijayanagara capital.
• (D) Ajanta, Maharashtra: Famous for Buddhist rock-cut caves and murals.
tip: ► Prehistoric Sites: Bhimbetka (MP) = Mesolithic cave paintings (hunting scenes, dancers) | Discovery = V.S. Wakankar (1957)!

subject: Indian History
q: In the Rigveda, the sacred river 'Parushni', on whose banks the famous Battle of the Ten Kings (Dasarajna) was fought, is identified with which modern river?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Ravi • (A) Sindhu: Indus River.
• (B) Vitasta: Jhelum River.
• (C) Ravi: Correct! In the Rigveda (Mandala 7), the epic 'Dasarajna' (Battle of Ten Kings) was fought on the banks of river PARUSHNI, modern-day RAVI. King Sudas of the Bharata tribe (guided by sage Vashistha) decisively defeated the confederacy of ten kings (five Aryan and five non-Aryan tribes guided by sage Vishwamitra).
• (D) Asikni: Chenab River.
tip: ► Rigvedic River Names: Parushni = Ravi | Vitasta = Jhelum | Asikni = Chenab | Vipas = Beas | Sutudri = Sutlej | Kubha = Kabul!

subject: Indian History
q: According to early Buddhist and Jain canonical texts (such as the Anguttara Nikaya), how many 'Mahajanapadas' (great oligarchic/monarchical realms) flourished in northern India during the 6th century BCE?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra • (A) Arthashastra and Indica: Detail the later Mauryan Empire.
• (B) Tripitaka and Divyavadana: General Buddhist monastic and narrative texts.
• (C) Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra: Correct! The definitive list of the 16 Great Kingdoms (Sodasa Mahajanapadas) of the 6th century BCE is chronicled in the Buddhist text 'Anguttara Nikaya' (part of Sutta Pitaka) and corroborated in the Jain canonical work 'Bhagavati Sutra'. The only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas was ASSAKA (Asmaka) on the Godavari (Telangana region).
• (D) Rajatarangini: Kalhana's chronicle of Kashmir.
tip: ► Telangana Connection: Assaka (capital Potali/Bodhan in Nizamabad) was the sole southern Mahajanapada out of the 16!

subject: Indian History
q: Under the centralized Mauryan administration detailed in Kautilya's Arthashastra, senior superintendents in charge of state departments (such as mining, tolls, and commerce) were designated as:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Superintendent of Crown Lands and Agriculture • (A) Collector General of Revenue: Samaharta.
• (B) Superintendent of Crown Lands and Agriculture: Correct! In Kautilya's 'Arthashastra', SITADHYAKSHA was the official in charge of crown agricultural lands ('Sita' referred to state-owned farmland). He supervised cultivation, state irrigation, seed distribution, and agricultural labor.
• (C) Chief Treasurer: Sannidhata.
• (D) Superintendent of Mints: Lakshnadhyaksha.
tip: ► Mauryan Administrative Portfolios: Samaharta = Revenue Collection | Sannidhata = Chief Treasury Custodian | Sitadhyaksha = Agriculture | Pautavadhyaksha = Weights & Measures!

subject: Indian History
q: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien (Faxian) visited India and left vivid accounts of social harmony and Buddhist monasteries during the reign of which Gupta emperor?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Chandragupta II Vikramaditya • (A) Chandragupta Maurya: Megasthenes visited his court.
• (B) Samudragupta: Celebrated conqueror ('Napoleon of India') commemorated in Allahabad Pillar (Prayag Prashasti).
• (C) Chandragupta II Vikramaditya: Correct! The Chinese Buddhist monk Fa-Hien (Faxian) travelled through northern India during the reign of Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II (399–414 CE). In his travelogue 'Fo-Kwo-Ki' (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms), he documented the peace, low crime, absence of capital punishment, and prosperity of the Gupta golden age.
• (D) Harshavardhana: Visited by Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).
tip: ► Chinese Pilgrims Chronology: Fa-Hien (Gupta: Chandragupta II) -> Hiuen Tsang (Harsha / Pulakeshin II) -> I-Tsing (late 7th century)!

subject: Indian History
q: King Harshavardhana of Kannauj was famously defeated on the banks of the Narmada River around 618 CE by which southern monarch?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Aihole Inscription composed by Ravikirti • (A) Aihole Inscription composed by Ravikirti: Correct! The Aihole stone inscription (634 CE) at the Meguti Jain temple in Bagalkot, Karnataka, was composed in ornate Sanskrit by court poet RAVIKIRTI. It chronicles the victories of Chalukya King Pulakeshin II, emphasizing his epic victory over King Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River, forcing Harsha to halt his southward expansion.
• (B) Allahabad Pillar Inscription: Composed by Harisena for Samudragupta.
• (C) Hathigumpha Inscription: Chronicles King Kharavela of Kalinga.
• (D) Junagadh Rock Inscription: Rudradaman I (Sanskrit inscription on Sudarshana Lake).
tip: ► Battle of Narmada (618-619 CE): Pulakeshin II assumed the title 'Parameshwara' after defeating 'Sakalottarapathanatha' Harsha! Verified by Aihole Inscription!

subject: Indian History
q: The majestic Brihadisvara Temple (Rajarajesvaram) at Thanjavur, an architectural masterpiece of Dravidian granite construction, was consecrated in 1010 CE by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Rajaraja Chola I • (A) Rajendra Chola I: Built the Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
• (B) Rajaraja Chola I: Correct! The magnificent Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, consecrated in 1010 CE, was constructed entirely of granite by the great Chola monarch RAJARAJA CHOLA I (Arunmozhi Varman). Dedicated to Lord Shiva, its towering 13-storey Vimana (66 m) and 80-tonne monolithic cupola represent the pinnacle of Dravidian temple architecture.
• (C) Kulottunga Chola I: Known for tax reforms ('Sungam Thavirtha Cholan').
• (D) Aditya Chola I: Early Chola ruler who defeated the Pallavas.
tip: ► Twin Temples: Thanjavur Brihadisvara = Rajaraja I (1010 CE) | Gangaikonda Cholapuram = Rajendra I! Both are UNESCO 'Great Living Chola Temples'!

subject: Indian History
q: Who among the following Delhi Sultans ordered the construction of the celebrated 'Alai Darwaza' (the southern gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque) utilizing red sandstone and the true pointed horseshoe arch?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Alauddin Khalji • (A) Qutb-ud-din Aibak: Commenced construction of Qutb Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
• (B) Iltutmish: Completed the original 3 storeys of Qutb Minar.
• (C) Alauddin Khalji: Correct! ALAUDDIN KHALJI built the ALAI DARWAZA in 1311 CE as the southern ceremonial gateway to the extended Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque at the Qutb complex in Delhi. Built of red sandstone with inlaid white marble, it is the earliest surviving building in India displaying authentic Islamic true arches and a true dome.
• (D) Firoz Shah Tughlaq: Repaired the top storeys of Qutb Minar after lightning damage.
tip: ► Indo-Islamic Architecture: Alai Darwaza introduced the horseshoe arch and true dome with squinches!

subject: Indian History
q: The Italian merchant and explorer Nicolo de Conti visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of which Sangama dynasty monarch in 1420 CE?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Deva Raya I • (A) Harihara II: Early Sangama ruler.
• (B) Deva Raya I: Correct! The Italian merchant and traveler NICOLO DE CONTI visited the Vijayanagara capital around 1420–1421 CE during the reign of Sangama ruler DEVA RAYA I. He left vivid accounts of the city's massive fortifications, festivals (Navaratri, Deepavali), and large army.
• (C) Krishnadevaraya: Visited by Portuguese travelers Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa.
• (D) Achyuta Deva Raya: Visited by Fernao Nuniz.
tip: ► Vijayanagara Travelers Timeline: Nicolo de Conti (Italian) = Deva Raya I (1420) | Abdur Razzak (Persian) = Deva Raya II (1443) | Domingo Paes & Barbosa (Portuguese) = Krishnadevaraya | Fernao Nuniz = Achyuta Deva Raya!

subject: Indian History
q: Under Mughal Emperor Jahangir's reign, which court artist achieved legendary fame for his lifelike paintings of rare birds, animals, and flowers (such as the Siberian crane and Dodo)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Ustad Mansur • (A) Daswanth: Renowned painter under Akbar (illustrated Razmnama).
• (B) Ustad Mansur: Correct! USTAD MANSUR was the celebrated court artist during Jahangir's reign, conferred with the title 'Nadir-ul-Asr' (Wonder of the Age). He specialized in botanical studies, wildlife, and exquisite bird portraits, famously painting the Siberian crane, dodo, and Kashmiri flowers.
• (C) Abul Hasan: Portrait master conferred with the title 'Nadir-uz-Zaman' (Wonder of the Time).
• (D) Bishandas: Portrait painter sent by Jahangir to Persia to paint Shah Abbas.
tip: ► Jahangir's Golden Era: Jahangir was a naturalist patron: Ustad Mansur = Flora & Fauna (Nadir-ul-Asr) | Abul Hasan = Portraiture (Nadir-uz-Zaman)!

subject: Indian History
q: On March 29, 1857, which sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry revolted against the introduction of greased cartridges at Barrackpore parade ground, wounding his British officers?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Barrackpore (near Kolkata) • (A) Barrackpore (near Kolkata): Correct! On March 29, 1857, Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry revolted against British officers (Lieutenant Baugh and Major Hewson) at BARRACKPORE parade ground, protesting the grease-smeared Enfield rifle cartridges containing cow and pig fat. He was court-martialed and executed on April 8, 1857.
• (B) Meerut: Scene of the general military rebellion on May 10, 1857.
• (C) Jhansi: Led by Rani Lakshmibai.
• (D) Kanpur: Led by Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope.
tip: ► 1857 Spark Timeline: Barrackpore (March 29 - Mangal Pandey executed) -> Meerut (May 10 - open rebellion begins) -> Delhi (May 11 - Bahadur Shah Zafar declared Emperor)!

subject: Indian History
q: The 'Indian Association of Calcutta', founded in 1876 to create a strong body of public opinion and unify Indian races on a common political program, was established by:
opts: Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose • (A) Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose: Correct! The INDIAN ASSOCIATION OF CALCUTTA was founded on July 26, 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose to represent educated middle-class aspirations and protest against lowering the maximum age limit for the Indian Civil Service (ICS) from 21 to 19. It merged with the Indian National Congress in 1886.
• (B) Dadabhai Naoroji and Pherozeshah Mehta: Associated with the Bombay Presidency Association and East India Association.
• (C) Sisir Kumar Ghosh: Founded the Indian League in 1875.
• (D) Gopal Krishna Gokhale: Founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
tip: ► Pre-Congress National Bodies: Indian Association (1876) = Surendranath Banerjee | Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) = M.G. Ranade | Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884) = Rangaiya Naidu, Anandacharlu!

subject: Indian History
q: In April 1916, Bal Gangadhar Tilak established his Indian Home Rule League at the Bombay Provincial Conference held at:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Belgaum / Pune • (A) Madras: Headquarters of Annie Besant's All-India Home Rule League (Adyar).
• (B) Belgaum / Pune: Correct! Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak established his Indian Home Rule League in April 1916 at the Bombay Provincial Conference held at BELGAUM, with its central headquarters at PUNE. His league operated in Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces, and Berar, with its famous slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.
• (C) Calcutta: Moderate political center.
• (D) Bombay city: Specifically assigned to Annie Besant's league to avoid jurisdictional friction.
tip: ► Home Rule Leagues (1916): Tilak's League = April 1916 (HQ Pune/Belgaum, 6 branches, MH/KA/CP/Berar) | Besant's League = Sep 1916 (HQ Adyar, Madras, covered rest of India)!

subject: Indian History
q: Why did the nationalist leadership across India boycott the Indian Statutory Commission (Simon Commission) appointed by the British Government in November 1927?
opts: It refused to consider Indian independence
It was an all-white commission without a single Indian member
It was chaired by Lord Birkenhead
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) It was an all-white commission with zero Indian members • (A) Rejection of separate electorates: Not the stated grievance.
• (B) It was an all-white commission with zero Indian members: Correct! Appointed in November 1927 by the British Conservative Government (two years ahead of schedule) to review the working of the Government of India Act 1919, the 7-member Indian Statutory Commission headed by Sir John Simon contained NOT A SINGLE INDIAN MEMBER. This deliberate insult to Indian self-determination provoked nationwide boycott under the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.
• (C) Relocation of national capital: Capital moved in 1911.
• (D) Partition of Bengal: Occurred in 1905.
tip: ► Simon Commission (1927): 7 British MPs, chaired by Sir John Simon. Boycotted by Congress, Muslim League, and Liberal Federation! Led to the Nehru Report (1928)!

subject: Indian History
q: During the anti-Simon Commission demonstrations at Lahore in October 1928, which national leader sustained severe lathi-blows from British police led by J.A. Scott, succumbing to injuries weeks later?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Saunders assassinated by Bhagat Singh and Rajguru • (A) General Dyer: Assassinated in London by Udham Singh in 1940.
• (B) Saunders assassinated by Bhagat Singh and Rajguru: Correct! On October 30, 1928, during anti-Simon Commission protests at Lahore, police superintendent J.A. Scott ordered a brutal lathi charge during which Lala Lajpat Rai ('Sher-e-Punjab') was grievously injured, succumbing on November 17, 1928. To avenge his death, HSRA revolutionaries Bhagat Singh, Shivaram Rajguru, and Sukhdev shot assistant superintendent of police J.P. Saunders on December 17, 1928.
• (C) Curzon Wyllie: Assassinated by Madan Lal Dhingra in London (1909).
• (D) Jackson: Collector of Nashik shot by Anant Kanhere.
tip: ► Revolutionary Revenge: Lala Lajpat Rai martyred -> HSRA targets J.A. Scott, mistakenly shoots Assistant Superintendent J.P. Saunders outside Lahore police HQ!

subject: Geography
q: Under the historic Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan, which three 'Eastern Rivers' were allocated for unrestricted use by India?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan • (A) Complete Indian control: Factually inaccurate.
• (B) Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan: Correct! Brokered by the World Bank and signed on September 19, 1960 by PM Jawaharlal Nehru and President Ayub Khan, the treaty allocated exclusive rights over the three EASTERN RIVERS (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej - ~33 MAF) to India, while the three WESTERN RIVERS (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab - ~135 MAF) were allocated to Pakistan, with India permitted limited run-of-the-river hydroelectric usage.
• (C) 50:50 equal division of volume: Treaty is river-partition based.
• (D) Southern rivers allocation: Geographic error.
tip: ► IWT 1960 Mnemonic: India got 'RBS' (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej)! Pakistan got 'IJC' (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab)!

subject: Geography
q: The largest brackish water coastal lagoon in India, recognized as India's first designated Ramsar wetland in 1981, is:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Odisha • (A) Andhra Pradesh: Home to Kolleru (freshwater) and Pulicat (brackish) lakes.
• (B) Odisha: Correct! CHILIKA LAKE in Odisha is India's largest coastal brackish water lagoon (and second largest in the world after the New Caledonian barrier reef). Spread across Puri, Khordha, and Ganjam districts, it is home to endangered Irrawaddy dolphins and was designated as India's FIRST RAMSAR WETLAND SITE in 1981.
• (C) Kerala: Renowned for Vembanad Lake (longest lake in India).
• (D) Tamil Nadu: Home to Kaliveli wetland.
tip: ► Wetland Champions: Chilika (Odisha) = Largest brackish lagoon & 1st Ramsar site! Vembanad (Kerala) = Longest lake! Wular (J&K) = Largest freshwater lake!

subject: Geography
q: National Waterway 1 (NW-1), the longest inland waterway route in India, operates on the river system connecting Prayagraj to Haldia along the:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Prayagraj to Haldia (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system, 1,620 km) • (A) Sadiya to Dhubri: National Waterway 2 (Brahmaputra River, 891 km).
• (B) Prayagraj to Haldia (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system, 1,620 km): Correct! National Waterway 1 (NW-1), enacted in 1986, runs across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal along the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river system. Stretching 1,620 km from Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia, it is India's longest operational national waterway.
• (C) Kollam to Kottapuram: National Waterway 3 (West Coast Canal, Kerala).
• (D) Kakinada to Puducherry: National Waterway 4 (Godavari-Krishna canal network).
tip: ► Waterways Hierarchy: NW-1 = Ganga (Prayagraj to Haldia, 1620 km) | NW-2 = Brahmaputra (Sadiya to Dhubri, 891 km) | NW-3 = West Coast Canal (Kerala, 205 km) | NW-4 = Krishna-Godavari canals!

subject: Geography
q: Which soil type is renowned for its high moisture-retention capacity and 'self-ploughing' characteristic due to wide cracks developing during the dry hot season?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Montmorillonite clay mineral and self-ploughing capacity • (A) High leaching in heavy rainfall: Characteristic of Laterite soil.
• (B) Montmorillonite clay mineral and self-ploughing capacity: Correct! BLACK SOIL (Regur), derived from Deccan trap basalt lava, has high clay content dominated by montmorillonite. It exhibits intense swelling and stickiness when wet, and contracts sharply upon drying to form deep, wide cracks. This natural crumbling and aeration is termed 'self-ploughing', allowing excellent moisture retention ideal for rainfed cotton cultivation.
• (C) Sandy texture with low humus: Desert/Arid soil.
• (D) Acidic forest floor soil: Mountain/Forest soil.
tip: ► Soil Features: Black Soil = Montmorillonite, deep cracks ('self-ploughing'), best for Cotton! Red Soil = Ferric oxide! Laterite = Intense leaching of silica!

subject: Geography
q: The 'Kawal Tiger Reserve' in Telangana, declared as the state's 41st Project Tiger reserve, is situated in which district tract?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Jannaram (Mancherial, Nirmal, and Adilabad districts) • (A) Jannaram (Mancherial, Nirmal, and Adilabad districts): Correct! KAWAL TIGER RESERVE, notified in April 2012 as the 42nd Tiger Reserve of India, is situated in the northern part of Telangana along the Godavari and Kadam river catchment. Headquartered at Jannaram, its core and buffer areas span Mancherial, Nirmal, Adilabad, and KB Asifabad districts.
• (B) Nallamala Hills: Amrabad Tiger Reserve (Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda).
• (C) Pakhal Lake: Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary in Warangal.
• (D) Kinnerasani basin: Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary in Bhadradri Kothagudem.
tip: ► Telangana Tiger Reserves: 1. Kawal Tiger Reserve (North TG - Adilabad/Mancherial/Nirmal) | 2. Amrabad Tiger Reserve (South TG - Nallamala Hills, 2nd largest tiger reserve in India)!

subject: Geography
q: Which agricultural commodity from Telangana received the prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2022 for its superior protein content and high nutritional value?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Vikarabad district • (A) Adilabad district: Known for Dokra craft and Nirmal toys.
• (B) Vikarabad district: Correct! TANDUR RED GRAM (Tandur Kandulu) from Vikarabad district received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in December 2022. The fertile black basalt soils of Tandur region containing rich attapulgite clay deposits impart an exceptionally high protein content (nearly 24%), distinct aroma, and superior boiling quality.
• (C) Mahabubnagar district: Renowned for Bijjapuri jowar and Narayanpet handlooms.
• (D) Nizamabad district: Famous for turmeric and Armoor red gram.
tip: ► Telangana GI Products: Tandur Red Gram (Vikarabad), Pochampally Ikkat (Yadadri), Gadwal Sarees (Jogulamba), Cheriyal Paintings (Siddipet), Pembarthi Metal (Jangaon), Telia Rumal (Nalgonda)!

subject: Geography
q: Approximately what percentage of the total annual precipitation in Telangana is contributed by the Southwest Monsoon (June to September)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Approximately 80% • (A) 50%: Understated.
• (B) 65%: Moderate monsoon baseline.
• (C) Approximately 80%: Correct! Telangana receives an average annual rainfall of approximately 900 to 950 mm. Nearly 80% (around 750 mm) is received during the SOUTH-WEST MONSOON period (June to September), driven by Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches. The North-East retreating monsoon contributes around 13-15% (mainly to southern districts).
• (D) 95%: Overstatement.
tip: ► Climate Breakdown: June–September (SW Monsoon) = ~80% rain | October–December (NE Monsoon) = ~14% | Summer thunderstorms = ~6%! Northern districts (Adilabad) receive maximum rainfall (>1000 mm).

subject: Geography
q: The historic reservoir 'Osmansagar' (popularly called Gandipet) was engineered following the devastating Musi floods of 1908 on the advice of which legendary statesman-engineer?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Musi River • (A) Manjeera River: Singur and Nizam Sagar reservoirs.
• (B) Musi River: Correct! OSMANSAGAR, commissioned in 1920 by the 7th Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan on the advice of legendary engineer Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya following the disastrous September 1908 Hyderabad floods, was constructed by building a masonry dam across the MUSI RIVER at Gandipet. Himayatsagar was built across its tributary, Esa.
• (C) Godavari River: Sriram Sagar Project (SRSP).
• (D) Krishna River: Nagarjuna Sagar and Jurala projects.
tip: ► Twin Flood Control Lakes: Osmansagar (Gandipet) = Dam on MUSI River! Himayatsagar = Dam on ESA River! Designed by Sir M. Visvesvaraya after 1908 Great Musi Flood!

subject: Geography
q: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) jurisdiction spans an extensive planned urban territory covering approximately:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) 7,257 sq. km • (A) 2,500 sq. km: Old HUDA jurisdiction (urban core).
• (B) 5,000 sq. km: Approximate GHMC peripheral belt.
• (C) 7,257 sq. km: Correct! The Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA), established in 2008 by merging HUDA, BMRDA, and special development authorities, exercises planning and infrastructure development authority over an area of 7,257 sq. km, encompassing Hyderabad and parts of 6 adjoining districts.
• (D) 10,000 sq. km: Future regional master plan projection.
tip: ► Metropolitan Scale: GHMC area = 650 sq km | HMDA planning jurisdiction = 7,257 sq km (one of India's largest urban planning zones)!

subject: Geography
q: The 158-km long, 8-lane expressway encircling Hyderabad, functioning as the vital outer transport spine of the capital region, is the:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 158 km • (A) 116 km: Inner ring road / intermediate ring road.
• (B) 158 km: Correct! The Jawaharlal Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR) is an access-controlled, 8-lane ring expressway spanning exactly 158 km around Hyderabad. With a design speed of 100-120 km/h, it connects major national highways (NH-44, NH-65, NH-163, NH-765) and Rajiv Gandhi International Airport at Shamshabad.
• (C) 200 km: Regional Ring Road (RRR) northern part length.
• (D) 340 km: Proposed total circumference of Regional Ring Road (RRR).
tip: ► Expressway Hierarchy: ORR = 158 km (8 lanes, fully operational) | RRR (Regional Ring Road) = ~340 km (proposed outer expressway ring)!

subject: Polity
q: The 'Objective Resolution', which provided the ideological philosophy and guiding framework for the Preamble of the Constitution of India, was moved in the Constituent Assembly on December 13, 1946 by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946 • (A) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on November 4, 1948: Introduced the Draft Constitution.
• (B) Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946: Correct! JAWAHARLAL NEHRU moved the historic 'OBJECTIVE RESOLUTION' in the Constituent Assembly on DECEMBER 13, 1946, laying down the fundamental philosophy, ideals of justice, equality, and sovereignty. It was unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947, and subsequently formed the modified text of the PREAMBLE.
• (C) Dr. Rajendra Prasad: Assembly President who presided.
• (D) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel: Chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights.
tip: ► Constituent Assembly Dates: Dec 9, 1946 = 1st Meeting (Sachchidananda Sinha temporary chairman) | Dec 11, 1946 = Rajendra Prasad elected President | Dec 13, 1946 = Nehru moves Objective Resolution | Jan 22, 1947 = Adopted!

explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) December 31, 2014 • (A) January 26, 1950: Commencement of the Constitution.
• (B) December 31, 2014: Correct! The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides an expedited pathway to Indian citizenship for persecuted religious minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India on or before DECEMBER 31, 2014.
• (C) August 15, 1947: Independence date.
• (D) March 24, 1971: Cut-off date under the Assam Accord for citizenship identification.

subject: Polity
q: In Indian constitutional jurisprudence, the concept of 'Equality before the Law' incorporated in Article 14 is borrowed from the British legal system, while the concept of 'Equal Protection of the Laws' is borrowed from:
opts: The Constitution of the United States
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) American Constitution (14th Amendment) • (A) American Constitution (14th Amendment): Correct! In Article 14, 'Equality before the law' is a negative British concept (no special privileges). In contrast, 'EQUAL PROTECTION OF THE LAWS' is a positive concept borrowed from Section 1 of the 14th Amendment of the US CONSTITUTION, meaning equal treatment under equal circumstances and permitting reasonable classification.
• (B) British Common Law: Source of 'Equality before Law' (A.V. Dicey's Rule of Law).
• (C) Irish Constitution: Source of Directive Principles of State Policy.
• (D) Canadian Constitution: Source of Federation with a strong Centre and residual powers.
tip: ► Article 14 Dual Doctrine: 'Equality before Law' -> UK (Negative concept) | 'Equal Protection of Laws' -> USA (Positive concept, permits affirmative action)!

subject: Polity
q: Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides three vital procedural protections against arbitrary penal actions. Which of the following is NOT protected under Article 20?
opts: Protection against Preventive Detention without trial
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) No ex-post facto criminal law, no double jeopardy, and no self-incrimination • (A) Protection against preventive detention: Covered under Article 22.
• (B) Abolition of untouchability: Covered under Article 17.
• (C) No ex-post facto criminal law, no double jeopardy, and no self-incrimination: Correct! Article 20 protects accused persons: Clause (1) prohibits ex-post facto penal legislation; Clause (2) bars double jeopardy ('no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once'); Clause (3) guarantees immunity against self-incrimination ('no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself'). Cannot be suspended even during Emergency (Article 359).
• (D) Freedom of speech and assembly: Covered under Article 19.
tip: ► Non-Suspendable Fundamental Rights: Articles 20 and 21 CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment Act, 1978)!

subject: Polity
q: Which Directive Principles of State Policy under Article 39 were given constitutional supremacy over Fundamental Rights in Articles 14 and 19 by the 25th Constitutional Amendment (upheld in Kesavananda Bharati)?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 25th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 • (A) 24th Amendment Act: Affirmed Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.
• (B) 25th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971: Correct! The 25th Amendment inserted ARTICLE 31C, which provided that any law enacted to give effect to Directive Principles under Article 39(b) (distribution of material resources) and Article 39(c) (prevention of concentration of wealth) shall not be deemed void on the ground that it violates Article 14 or Article 19.
• (C) 42nd Amendment Act: Attempted to extend immunity to ALL DPSPs (struck down in Minerva Mills, 1980).
• (D) 44th Amendment Act: Deleted Right to Property from Fundamental Rights.
tip: ► Landmark Balance: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) upheld the first part of Article 31C giving supremacy to Art 39(b) & (c) over Arts 14 & 19!

subject: Polity
q: The Electoral College that elects the President of India under Article 54 of the Constitution consists of:
opts: All members of both Houses of Parliament and State Assemblies
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States, including Delhi and Puducherry
Elected members of Lok Sabha alone
Nominated and elected members of Parliament
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Elected members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi & Puducherry) • (A) All members including nominated members: Nominated members cannot vote in Presidential elections.
• (B) Elected members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies: Correct! Under Article 54, the Electoral College consists solely of: (1) ELECTED members of both Houses of Parliament; (2) ELECTED members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States; and (3) ELECTED members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry (70th Amendment). Nominated members and State Legislative Council (MLC) members do NOT participate.
• (C) Includes Legislative Councils: Legislative Councils (MLCs) have zero voting rights in Presidential polls.
• (D) Lok Sabha members only: Incomplete.
tip: ► Presidential Voting Key: ONLY ELECTED MLAs & MPs! NO Nominated members! NO MLCs! (Nominated MPs vote only in Vice-Presidential elections!).

subject: Polity
q: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC), the oldest parliamentary financial committee in India, consists of how many members, and who heads it by established convention?
opts: 30 members from Lok Sabha alone; headed by Speaker
22 members (15 LS + 7 RS); headed by an Opposition party member
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha), chaired by an Opposition member • (A) 30 members all from Lok Sabha: Estimates Committee.
• (B) 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha), chaired by an Opposition member: Correct! Established in 1921 under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, PAC audits CAG reports. It comprises 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha) elected via proportional representation. By established convention since 1967, its chairman is appointed by the Speaker from the OPPOSITION.
• (C) Chaired by Finance Minister: Ministers cannot be elected to PAC.
• (D) 15 members all from Rajya Sabha: Erroneous.
tip: ► Financial Committees: Estimates Committee = 30 members (ALL Lok Sabha, largest committee) | PAC = 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS, Opposition Chair) | Committee on Public Undertakings = 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS)!

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 163 of the Constitution, in which of the following areas does the State Governor exercise sole constitutional discretion?
opts: Dismissing the Speaker of the Assembly
Reserving a State Bill for the consideration of the President under Article 200
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Article 163 • (A) Article 153: Provides for a Governor for each State.
• (B) Article 163: Correct! Article 163(1) mandates a Council of Ministers with the CM to aid and advise the Governor, 'except in so far as he is by or under this Constitution required to act in his DISCRETION'. Article 163(2) declares that if any question arises whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion, the Governor's decision is FINAL and cannot be questioned.
• (C) Article 174: Prorogation and dissolution of legislative assembly.
• (D) Article 200: Assent to bills.
tip: ► Constitutional Nuance: The President has NO explicit constitutional discretionary powers; the GOVERNOR has explicit constitutional discretion under Article 163!

subject: Polity
q: The original and exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India to adjudicate any federal dispute between the Government of India and one or more States is governed by:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Article 131 • (A) Article 32: Writ jurisdiction for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
• (B) Article 131: Correct! ARTICLE 131 confers exclusive and original jurisdiction on the Supreme Court to adjudicate federal disputes: (a) between the Government of India and one or more States; (b) between the Government of India and any State(s) on one side and other State(s) on the other; or (c) between two or more States.
• (C) Article 136: Special Leave Petition (SLP).
• (D) Article 143: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
tip: ► Supreme Court Jurisdictions: Art 131 = Federal Disputes (Original & Exclusive) | Art 136 = Special Leave Petition | Art 143 = Advisory (Presidential Reference) | Art 32 = Constitutional Writs!

subject: Polity
q: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 limited the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister (or Chief Minister in States), in the Council of Ministers to:
opts: 10% of total membership of the House
15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha (or State Legislative Assembly)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha / State Legislative Assembly (minimum 12 in states) • (A) 10%: Understated.
• (B) 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha / State Legislative Assembly: Correct! The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Clause (1A) into Article 75 and Article 164, stipulating that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister / Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha / State Legislative Assembly. For States, the minimum strength is 12 ministers.
• (C) 20%: Excessive.
• (D) Unlimited: Pre-2003 situation.
tip: ► Ministry Ceiling: 15% limit on Lower House! (For Telangana Assembly of 119 MLAs: 15% of 119 = 17.85 -> Maximum 18 Ministers including Chief Minister!).

subject: Polity
q: Under the 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), a merger of an existing political party with another is recognized as immune from disqualification only if at least what proportion of its elected members agree to the merger?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Two-thirds of the elected members of the legislative party • (A) One-third: Original threshold under 52nd Amendment (1985) for 'splits', which was completely DELETED by the 91st Amendment.
• (B) Two-thirds of the elected members of the legislative party: Correct! Under Paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule (as amended by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003), disqualification on grounds of defection does not apply in case of a MERGER, provided that not less than TWO-THIRDS (2/3) of the elected members of the legislative party agree to such merger.
• (C) One-half: Fifty percent threshold.
• (D) Three-fourths: Overstated.
tip: ► 10th Schedule Rule: 91st Amendment (2003) abolished the 1/3rd split exemption! Now, ONLY a 2/3rd merger is protected from anti-defection disqualification!

subject: Polity
q: The National Development Council (NDC), created to review national plans prepared by the Planning Commission, was established in which year?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) August 1952 • (A) March 1950: Establishment of the Planning Commission.
• (B) August 1952: Correct! The National Development Council (NDC) was established on AUGUST 6, 1952 by an executive resolution of the Union Government to strengthen and mobilize national effort in support of Five-Year Plans. Chaired by the Prime Minister, its members included all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, and Planning Commission members.
• (C) January 1956: Second Five-Year Plan launch.
• (D) August 1947: Independence.

subject: Polity
q: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), which replaced the 65-year-old Planning Commission as the apex policy think-tank of the Union Government, came into existence on:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 1 January 2015 • (A) 15 August 2014: Announcement of replacement by PM Modi from Red Fort.
• (B) 1 January 2015: Correct! NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established via a Union Cabinet resolution on JANUARY 1, 2015, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission. It serves as the apex public policy think tank fostering 'cooperative federalism' and bottom-up planning.
• (C) 1 April 2015: Commenced financial year operations.
• (D) 1 January 2017: Discontinuation of Five-Year Plans.

subject: Polity
q: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees the 'Freedom of Conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion', subject to public order, morality, and health?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Article 19(1)(a) • (A) Article 21: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.
• (B) Article 19(1)(a): Correct! Unlike the US Constitution (1st Amendment), the Indian Constitution does not explicitly mention 'Freedom of the Press'. However, in landmark rulings like Romesh Thappar (1950), Sakal Papers (1962), and Bennett Coleman (1972), the Supreme Court ruled that Freedom of the Press is an implicit, integral component of Freedom of Speech and Expression under ARTICLE 19(1)(a).
• (C) Article 14: Equality before law.
• (D) Article 22: Protection against arrest and detention.
tip: ► Press Freedom Law: Implicit under Article 19(1)(a); subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) (sovereignty, integrity, public order, decency, contempt of court)!

subject: Polity
q: The Supreme Court collegium system for appointing judges to the higher judiciary (Supreme Court and High Courts) was evolved through which famous series of cases?
opts: Golaknath, Kesavananda, and Minerva Mills cases
Berubari, Sajjan Singh, and Shankari Prasad cases
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Three Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998) • (A) Kesavananda Bharati case (1973): Established the Basic Structure doctrine.
• (B) Three Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998): Correct! The Collegium system evolved through three judicial rulings: First Judges Case (1981 - S.P. Gupta) held Executive had primacy; Second Judges Case (1993 - SC Advocates-on-Record) created the Collegium giving primacy to CJI and 2 senior-most judges; Third Judges Case (1998 - Presidential Reference) expanded it to CJI + 4 senior-most judges for SC appointments.
• (C) Maneka Gandhi case (1978): Expanded Article 21 to 'due process of law'.
• (D) Minerva Mills case (1980): Balanced Fundamental Rights and DPSPs.
tip: ► Collegium Evolution: 1981 (Executive primacy) -> 1993 (Collegium invented: CJI + 2) -> 1998 (CJI + 4 senior-most SC judges)! NJAC (99th Amendment) struck down in 2015 (Fourth Judges Case)!

Gen. E.N. Goddard. Following the surrender of Nizam's military commander General El-Edroos on September 17, Major General Chaudhuri served as the Military Governor of Hyderabad State from September 1948 to December 1949.

opts: Four (Burgula, Phoolchand Gandhi, V.B. Raju, J.V. Narsing Rao)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Senior ICS officer appointed as Chief Minister by Government of India • (A) Elected representative from Hyderabad State Congress: B. Ramakrishna Rao was elected later in 1952.

VELLODI, a senior ICS officer appointed by the Union Government. Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan was made Rajpramukh. Vellodi's induction of large numbers of Andhra/Madras officials sparked widespread discontent leading to the 1952 Mulki agitation.

q: The 1952 Mulki Agitation first erupted in Warangal in July 1952 following the appointment of non-local teachers by which local education official?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Transfer of non-Mulki teachers into Warangal government schools • (A) Transfer of non-Mulki teachers into Warangal government schools: Correct! In July 1952, the 1952 Mulki Agitation began when Warangal District Board school inspector Dr. Sheela (a non-Mulki) transferred several local Mulki teachers while recruiting non-Mulkis on fake domicile certificates. Students led by Warangal Student Union leaders (including Bucchiah and Hayagrivachary) staged massive protests, raising the historic slogan 'NON-MULKI GO BACK! IDHI TELANGANA, IDHI MANA DESAM!'.
• (B) Increase in bus fares: 1969 spark.
• (C) Dismissal of Osmania Vice-Chancellor: University administrative issue.
• (D) Imposition of sales tax on agricultural produce: Peasant issue.

q: During the tragic 1952 City College police firing incident on September 3, who was the Commissioner of City Police Hyderabad who authorized the use of live ammunition against unarmed students?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Justice Jaganmohan Reddy Commission • (A) Justice Jaganmohan Reddy Commission: Correct! On September 3 and 4, 1952, police opened fire on student demonstrators outside City College and Afzal Gunj in Hyderabad, killing several youth including Mohammad Qasim, Shaikh Mahbub, and Ramulu. Chief Minister Burgula Ramakrishna Rao appointed a one-man judicial commission headed by High Court Judge JUSTICE P. JAGANMOHAN REDDY, which investigated the police atrocities and excessive force.
• (B) Justice Bhargava Committee: Appointed after 1969 agitation to assess revenue surpluses.
• (C) Justice Wanchoo Committee: Appointed in 1969 to examine constitutional validity of Mulki rules.
• (D) Justice Srikrishna Committee: Appointed in 2010.

subject: Telangana Movement
q: When the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazal Ali Commission) visited Hyderabad State in June–July 1954, how many memoranda were submitted by various political bodies and civil groups regarding Telangana statehood?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Para 386 - Advised that Telangana can remain separate initially and consider unification after 5 years with 2/3rd majority • (A) Immediate unconditional merger with Andhra: Recommendation opposed by Fazal Ali.
• (B) Bifurcation of Hyderabad into three Union Territories: Not recommended.
• (C) Para 386 - Advised that Telangana can remain separate initially: Correct! In its historic 1955 report (chaired by Justice Fazal Ali with members H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar), paragraphs 371–389 highlighted Telangana's legitimate apprehensions of being dominated by educationally and financially advanced Coastal Andhra. Paragraph 386 explicitly advised that Telangana should constitute a separate State ('Hyderabad State') for 5 years and merge with Andhra only if two-thirds of the newly elected Telangana legislators voted for it in 1961.
• (D) Annexation to Maharashtra: Marathwada went to Maharashtra, not Telangana.
tip: ► SRC (Fazal Ali Commission) Famous Quote: 'Unification would look like an unequal partnership between a developed Coastal Andhra and an underdeveloped Telangana!' Proposed Telangana as a separate State in Para 386!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under Clause 14 of the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement, the safeguards and regional council mechanisms granted to Telangana were subject to mandatory review after:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Safeguards should be reviewed after 10 years and continued if the Telangana Regional Committee so desires • (A) Permanent reservation without expiration: Not time-bound.
• (B) Safeguards should be reviewed after 10 years and continued if TRC desires: Correct! Signed on February 20, 1956 at Hyderabad House, New Delhi by 4 Andhra leaders (B. Gopala Reddy, N. Sanjiva Reddy, G. Latchanna, A. Satyanarayana Raju) and 4 Telangana leaders (B. Ramakrishna Rao, K.V. Ranga Reddy, M. Chenna Reddy, J.V. Narsing Rao). Clause 14 specifically provided that the regional safeguards should be reviewed after a period of TEN YEARS and may be continued further if the Telangana Regional Committee so desires.
• (C) Automatic expiration after 5 years: Too short.
• (D) Revocation upon CM's proclamation: Unilateral power denied.
tip: ► Gentlemen's Agreement (1956): 14 clauses! Clause 1 = State expenditure in proportion to revenue | Clause 14 = Review after 10 years! Signed by 8 signatories (4 Andhra, 4 Telangana)!

q: The iconic Telangana Martyrs Memorial obelisk situated at Gun Park, Hyderabad, commemorating the 369 student martyrs of 1969, was sculpted by:
explanation:

The iconic TELANGANA MARTYRS MEMORIAL (Amaraveerula Stupa) at Gun Park, facing the State Legislative Assembly in Hyderabad, was sculpted by renowned artist and sculptor AKKALA YADAGIRI RAO (then faculty at JNTU Fine Arts). subject: Telangana Movement
q: The Justice Wanchoo Committee, appointed in April 1969 under the Eight-Point Formula to examine legal safeguards for Telangana, concluded that:
opts: Public employment reservation for locals could be achieved by ordinary executive order
Local reservation in public employment within a State was unconstitutional under Article 16(3) without a Constitutional Amendment
Hyderabad should become a Union Territory
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Declared that public employment reservation for Mulkis was unconstitutional under Article 16(3) • (A) Recommended separate Telangana state immediately: Opposed statehood.
• (B) Declared that public employment reservation for Mulkis was unconstitutional: Correct! Following the Supreme Court ruling in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao case striking down Section 3 of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act 1957, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi appointed a committee of jurists under former CJI K.N. WANCHOO (with M.C. Setalvad and Niren De). In April 1969, the Wanchoo Committee reported that Parliament had no power under Article 16(3) to prescribe domicile requirements for a SUB-PART of a State (such as Telangana), ruling Mulki employment quotas constitutionally untenable without constitutional amendment.
• (C) Validated Telangana revenue surplus calculations: Kumar Lalit committee role.
• (D) Abolished the Telangana Regional Committee: TRC continued until 1973.
tip: ► Legal Crisis 1969: Wanchoo Committee said domicile rules cannot apply to a fraction of a state under Art 16(3). This deadlock ultimately required the 32nd Constitutional Amendment inserting Article 371-D!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: In the 1971 parliamentary elections, the Telangana Praja Samithi (TPS) fought on a single-point manifesto of separate Telangana statehood and achieved a landslide victory, winning:
explanation:

tip: ► 1971 Election Milestone: TPS won 10/14 seats! Polled 47.5% of total votes in Telangana! Symbol = SPADE!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Presidential Order of October 1975 issued under Article 371-D, what was the minimum continuous schooling period required in a local area to qualify as a 'Local Candidate' for non-gazetted employment?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Zones V and VI • (A) Zones I and II: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam (Zone I); East and West Godavari, Krishna (Zone II).

The Andhra Pradesh Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order, 1975, promulgated under Article 371-D pursuant to the Six-Point Formula, divided the State into 6 zones. The 10 districts of Telangana were organized into ZONE V (Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam) and ZONE VI (Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Medak, Mahabubnagar, Nalgonda, Nizamabad).
• (C) Zones III and IV: Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore (Zone III); Rayalaseema districts (Zone IV).
• (D) Zone VII: Created later under 2018 New Zonal System.
tip: ► 1975 Zonal System (Zones 1-6): Zone V = Basara/Kaleshwaram districts | Zone VI = Charminar/Hyderabad districts! (Under 2018 New Zonal System, Telangana has 7 zones & 2 multi-zones).

explanation:

• (B) Submitted in September 2004 detailing thousands of violations: Correct! Appointed in June 2001 by the Chandrababu Naidu government to review non-implementation of G.O. 610 (issued in 1985 to repatriate non-locals), retired IAS officer J.M. GIRGLANI submitted his final report on SEPTEMBER 30, 2004. • (C) Reported zero violations in education and police: Extensively documented violations in police and education.
• (D) Focused only on river water sharing: Employment focus.

subject: Telangana Movement
q: In 2004, the newly elected Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA-1) government incorporated the demand for a separate Telangana State in its official policy roadmap titled:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Committed to separate Telangana through consensus and consultations • (A) Outright rejection of Telangana statehood: Contradicts actual pact.
• (B) Committed to separate Telangana through consensus and consultations: Correct! In the May 2004 general elections, TRS entered into an alliance with the Congress. In the UPA-1 National Common Minimum Programme (NCMP) released in May 2004, item 7 formally included the commitment: 'The UPA Government will consider the demand for the formation of a Telangana State through consultations and consensus'. President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam reiterated this in his joint address to Parliament in June 2004.
• (C) Demanded a second States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) only: Stand of certain regional leaders, not NCMP text.
• (D) Declared Hyderabad as a permanent Union Territory: Rejected idea.
tip: ► 2004 UPA NCMP Landmark: First time the Telangana demand was enshrined in an official national governing policy agenda of a Union coalition government!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: In November 2009, when K. Chandrashekar Rao commenced his fast unto death demanding Telangana statehood, where was he initially detained by the police before being shifted to NIMS?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Khammam Sub-Jail • (A) Chanchalguda Central Jail: Located in Hyderabad.
• (B) Khammam Sub-Jail: Correct! On November 29, 2009, while proceeding from Karimnagar to Siddipet to commence his indefinite hunger strike at 'Diksha Divas', TRS Chief K. Chandrashekar Rao was intercepted by police at Alaganur village and arrested. He was produced before a magistrate and remanded to KHAMMAM SUB-JAIL, where he commenced his fast unto death before deteriorating health led to his transfer to NIMS, Hyderabad.
• (C) Warangal Central Jail: Intermediate transit detention.
• (D) Cherlapally Central Jail: Outer Hyderabad maximum-security jail.
tip: ► Diksha Divas (29 Nov 2009): Arrest at Alaganur -> Sent to Khammam Sub-Jail -> Shifted to NIMS Hyderabad -> Culminated in Chidambaram's midnight announcement on Dec 9, 2009!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: The Committee for Consultations on the Situation in Andhra Pradesh (Srikrishna Committee), appointed in February 2010, proposed 6 options in its final report. Which option was designated as 'Bifurcation of the State into Telangana and Seemandhra'?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) Option 5 • (A) Option 1: Maintain status quo (found completely unviable).
• (B) Option 3: Bifurcation of State into Rayala-Telangana and Coastal Andhra.
• (C) Option 5: Correct! The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee report (submitted December 30, 2010) listed 6 options: OPTION 5 was 'Bifurcation of the State into Telangana and Seemandhra as per existing boundaries with Hyderabad as the capital of Telangana and Seemandhra to have a new capital'. OPTION 6 was 'Keeping the State united and providing for creation of a statutory Telangana Regional Council' (which the committee recommended as its first preference, rejected by the people of Telangana).
• (D) Option 6: United state with statutory regional council.
tip: ► Srikrishna Committee Options: Option 5 = Creation of Telangana state with Hyderabad as capital! Option 6 = United AP with regional council (Committee's biased preferred option, rejected by Telangana populace)!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: On September 30, 2012, TJAC organized a massive rally that encircled the entire perimeter of Hussain Sagar Lake, known as:
explanation:

• (B) Sagara Haram (Telangana March): Correct! On SEPTEMBER 30, 2012, under the leadership of TJAC (Prof. M. Kodandaram), lakhs of Telangana agitators defied prohibitory orders, tear gas, and massive barricades to stage the iconic 'SAGARA HARAM' (Telangana March), encircling the entire 14-km perimeter of Hussain Sagar Lake in Hyderabad despite pouring rain and police crackdowns.
• (C) Sadak Bandh: 48-hour blockade of NH-44 (Hyderabad-Bengaluru highway) on March 21, 2013.
• (D) Chalo Assembly: June 14, 2013.

explanation:

Thousands of students, women, and employees broke through massive multi-layered iron barricades, concertina wire, and water cannons surrounding the State Assembly in Hyderabad, paralyzing administration and sending an unmistakable signal to New Delhi.

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, how many assembly constituencies were initially allocated to the Telangana Legislative Assembly?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 119 elected constituencies (+1 nominated Anglo-Indian member) • (A) 90 constituencies: Chhattisgarh Assembly strength.
• (B) 119 elected constituencies (+1 nominated Anglo-Indian member): Correct! Under Section 15 and 17 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the total number of elected seats allocated to the Legislative Assembly of the successor State of Telangana was 119 (plus 1 nominated Anglo-Indian member, prior to 104th Amendment). The residual Andhra Pradesh Assembly was allocated 175 seats.
• (C) 125 constituencies: Arbitrary figure.
• (D) 175 constituencies: Allocated to residual Andhra Pradesh.
tip: ► Legislative Representation (2014 Act): Telangana = 119 MLAs, 40 MLCs, 17 Lok Sabha MPs, 7 Rajya Sabha MPs! AP = 175 MLAs, 58 MLCs, 25 Lok Sabha MPs, 11 Rajya Sabha MPs!

subject: Telangana Movement
q: Under the Twelfth Schedule of the 2014 Act, how was the coal produced by Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) allocated between the two successor states?
opts: 100% of coal produced by SCCL was allocated to the State of Telangana, while existing thermal power plants were allocated power based on historic consumption
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) 100% of coal produced by SCCL was allocated to the State of Telangana, while existing thermal power plants were allocated power based on historic consumption • (A) Telangana 100%, Andhra Pradesh 0%: Oversimplified power allocation.
• (B) 100% of coal produced by SCCL was allocated to the State of Telangana: Correct! Under Twelfth Schedule (Section 92) of the AP Reorganisation Act 2014, 100% of the coal produced by Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) was allocated to the State of Telangana. Equity in SCCL remained shared between Government of Telangana (51%) and Government of India (49%).
• (C) 50% each: Equal split rejected.
• (D) Based on population ratio: Population ratio (58.32 : 41.68) was applied to general assets/liabilities, NOT Singareni coal.

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The saint-poet Bammera Pothana, who translated the Sanskrit Bhagavata Purana into Telugu as 'Andhra Maha Bhagavatham', famously refused to dedicate his immortal literary work to which local ruler?
opts: Sarvajna Singa Bhupala (Ruler of Velama dynasty / Rachakonda)
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Sarvajna Singa Bhupala (Ruler of Velama dynasty / Rachakonda) • (A) Sri Krishnadevaraya: Dedicated Amuktamalyada to Lord Venkateswara.
• (B) Sarvajna Singa Bhupala (Ruler of Velama dynasty / Rachakonda): Correct! BAMMERA POTHANA (15th century, from Bammera village, Jangaon district) translated the Sanskrit Bhagavata Purana into Telugu as 'Andhra Maha Bhagavatham'. When local Velama ruler Sarvajna Singa Bhupala II of Rachakonda demanded that the epic be dedicated to him in exchange for riches, Pothana famously refused, proclaiming that he would rather till the soil as a humble peasant than sell his poetry to mere mortal kings ('Kanta Koraku Kavita Kanyakani Ammaradu'). He dedicated his immortal masterpiece exclusively to Lord Rama.
• (C) Ibrahim Qutb Shah: Patron of Gangadhara Kavi ('Malkibharama').
• (D) Prataparudra: Kakatiya monarch to whom Vidyanatha dedicated Prataprudra Yashobhushanam.
tip: ► Pothana's Immortal Verse: 'Balantharakhyuni kani, Naradhamulaku iyyi nenu Kavitha Kanyaka!' Dedicated Andhra Maha Bhagavatham only to Sri Rama!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The 17th-century Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna), Tahsildar of Palvoncha who constructed the Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple at Bhadrachalam using state revenues, was imprisoned for 12 years in Golconda Fort under:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Abul Hasan Tana Shah • (A) Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah: 5th Qutb Shahi Sultan who founded Hyderabad (1591).
• (B) Abul Hasan Tana Shah: Correct! Kancharla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu), maternal nephew of ministers Madanna and Akkanna, served as the Tahsildar of Palvoncha. He utilized nearly 6 lakh varahas of state tax revenues to construct the Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple at Bhadrachalam. When discovered, Sultan ABUL HASAN TANA SHAH (the 8th and final Qutb Shahi Sultan) imprisoned him for 12 years in the solitary dungeon cell at Golconda Fort, where Ramadasu composed his sorrowful 'Dasarathi Sathakam' and kirtanas before his release.
• (C) Abdullah Qutb Shah: 7th Sultan of Golconda.
• (D) Aurangzeb: Mughal Emperor who conquered Golconda in 1687.
tip: ► Ramadasu Jail Cell: The 'Ramadasu Bandikhana' with carved figures of Hanuman and Rama is a prominent historic site inside Golconda Fort!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The famous 'Kurikyala Inscription' (Gangadharam mandal, Karimnagar district), composed in 945 CE by Jinavallabha, holds momentous linguistic importance because it contains the earliest known:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Earliest Telugu Kanda verses (poetry) • (A) Earliest Telugu Kanda verses (poetry): Correct! The KURIKYALA INSCRIPTION (dated 945 CE), found on Bommalagutta hill in Kurikyala village, Gangadharam mandal of Karimnagar district, was inscribed by JINAVALLABHA (younger brother of Adi Kavi Pampa, the court poet of Vemulawada Chalukya ruler Arikesari II). It holds immense linguistic prominence because it contains the EARLIEST EXTANT TELUGU KANDA VERSES, proving that Telugu poetic meters flourished well before Nannaya's 11th-century Mahabharata translation.
• (B) Urdu ghazals in Deccan: Deccani Urdu developed under Bahmanis and Qutb Shahis.
• (C) Sanskrit copper plates: Pre-dated by centuries.
• (D) Prakrit edicts: Ashokan edicts are far older.
tip: ► Literary Milestone: Kurikyala Inscription (945 CE) by Jinavallabha established that metric Telugu poetry (Kanda Padyalu) existed long before Nannaya!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The celebrated ancient temple of Sri Rajarajeswara Swamy, revered by devotees as 'Dakshina Kashi' where Lord Shiva is worshipped as Rajanna and a holy Dargah stands on the temple premises, is situated at:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Vemulawada (Rajanna Sircilla district) • (A) Alampur: Known as the Gateway of Srisailam with Navabrahma temples (Jogulamba Gadwal).
• (B) Vemulawada (Rajanna Sircilla district): Correct! The historic Sri Rajarajeswara Swamy Temple at VEMULAWADA in Rajanna Sircilla district is revered as 'Dakshina Kashi'. Built by the Vemulawada Chalukyas in the 8th–10th century CE, devotees perform 'Kode Mokku' (offering of a decorated sacred bull) to Lord Shiva (Rajanna). Exemplifying communal harmony, the temple premises also house a holy dargah of a Muslim saint.
• (C) Dharmapuri: Ancient Narasimha temple on the banks of Godavari (Jagtial).
• (D) Kaleshwaram: Famous for dual lingas (Shiva and Yama) on a single pedestal.
tip: ► Vemulawada Highlights: Built by Vemulawada Chalukyas | Unique ritual = 'Kode Mokku' | Houses both Shiva Temple & Muslim Saint Dargah!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: Which traditional handloom cluster in Telangana, famous worldwide for its geometric double-ikkat tie-and-dye silk sarees, was recognized by the UNWTO as one of the 'Best Tourism Villages' in 2021?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) Bhoodan Pochampally (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district) • (A) Gadwal: Famous for silk sarees with kuttu borders.
• (B) Bhoodan Pochampally (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district): Correct! BHOODAN POCHAMPALLY in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district is globally celebrated as 'Silk City of India' for its geometric double-ikkat tie-and-dye Pochampally sarees (which received GI status in 2005). In November 2021, the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) conferred the prestigious 'Best Tourism Village' award on Pochampally. Historically, Acharya Vinoba Bhave launched the historic BHOODAN MOVEMENT here on April 18, 1951, when Vedire Ramachandra Reddy donated 100 acres of land.
• (C) Narayanpet: Renowned for lightweight cotton-silk sarees with temple borders.
• (D) Siricilla: Textile hub known as 'Textile Town' / powerloom center.
tip: ► Dual Historic Fame: Bhoodan Movement birthplace (1951 - Vinoba Bhave) + UNWTO Best Tourism Village (2021) = Bhoodan Pochampally!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The 'Dokra' bell-metal craft, crafted using the lost-wax casting technique (cire-perdue) to produce exquisite tribal figurines and brass lamps, is practiced by the Ojha tribal artisans of:
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Adilabad (Ushegaon / Keslapur) • (A) Adilabad (Ushegaon / Keslapur): Correct! DOKRA (or Dhokra) is a centuries-old bell-metal casting craft practiced by the traditional OJHA TRIBAL CRAFTSMEN of Adilabad district (concentrated in Ushegaon, Jainoor, and Keslapur). Using the primitive lost-wax technique (cire-perdue) with beeswax, clay, and molten brass/bronze, they create figurines of tribal deities, folk dancers, and oil lamps without any joint seams (awarded GI tag in 2018).
• (B) Warangal: Famous for Dhurries (carpets) and brass vessels.
• (C) Nalgonda: Telia Rumal handlooms.
• (D) Mahabubnagar: Koilkonda brassware.
tip: ► Craft GI Tags: Dokra Metal Craft = Adilabad (Ojha artisans) | Pembarthi Metalware = Jangaon | Cheriyal Scroll Paintings = Siddipet | Nirmal Toys = Nirmal!

subject: Telangana Culture
q: The legendary revolutionary balladeer and poet 'Gaddar' (Gummadi Vittal Rao), whose songs energized the Telangana mass struggle, penned which iconic song that became the heartbeat of the movement?
explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) Amma Telanganama Akali Kekala Ganam • (A) Amma Telanganama Akali Kekala Ganam: Correct! Legendary revolutionary balladeer, poet, and cultural icon GADDAR (Gummadi Vittal Rao, 1949–2023), founder of Jana Natya Mandali, composed and sang 'AMMA TELANGANAMA AKALI KEKALA GANAM'. This soul-stirring song portrayed the hunger, tears, exploitation, and indomitable resilience of Telangana, becoming the immortal spiritual anthem of the mass struggle.
• (B) Na Telangana Koti Ratanala Veena: Composed by Dasarathi Krishnamacharyulu.
• (C) Jaya Jaya He Telangana: Composed by Ande Sri (notified as State Song of Telangana in 2024).
• (D) Nageti Salallo Naa Telangana: Composed by Nandini Sidha Reddy.
tip: ► Telangana Literary Anthems: 'Amma Telanganama' = Gaddar | 'Jaya Jaya He Telangana' = Ande Sri (State Anthem) | 'Koti Ratanala Veena' = Dasarathi | 'Nageti Salallo' = Nandini Sidha Reddy!

explanation:

Revanth Reddy launched the 'YOUNG INDIA INTEGRATED RESIDENTIAL SCHOOLS' initiative in October 2024. Designed as state-of-the-art residential campuses spanning 20 to 25 acres in each Assembly constituency, these integrated schools bring SC, ST, BC, and minority students under one roof with world-class infrastructure and English-medium curriculum.

subject: Telangana Economy & Governance
q: Under the 'New Record of Rights (RoR) Act, 2024' (Bhoomi Matha) introduced to reform land administration, the Government of Telangana aimed to overhaul and replace the deficiencies of:
explanation:

The Government of Telangana introduced the 'Telangana Record of Rights in Land Act, 2024' (popularly titled 'BHOOMI MATHA') to overhaul land administration and replace the controversial DHARANI PORTAL. The new system remedies Dharani's structural defects by reinstating revenue courts, appeal mechanisms before RDOs/Collectors, physical verification, and clear grievance redressal for disputed lands.

• (C) The Bhu-Aadhaar Registry: Central 14-digit ULPIN scheme.

q: Under the 'Maha Lakshmi' scheme, what is the subsidized price at which domestic cooking gas (LPG) cylinders are provided to eligible white ration card-holding families in Telangana?

Under the flagship 'MAHA LAKSHMI' scheme (part of the 6 Guarantees implemented from February 2024), eligible BPL households possessing food security (white ration) cards receive domestic LPG cooking gas refills at a subsidized price of RS. 500 PER CYLINDER. q: Under the 'Praja Palana' governance framework, public grievance representation petitions ('Praja Vani') submitted by citizens are tracked using which centralized digital tracking mechanism?

explanation:
